During a severe accident, the core can melt and be relocated to the lower plenum of the reactor pressure vessel. The molten corium can be relocated in the containment cavity forming a debris bed if water is present in the cavity. Hence, a scale down experimental test facility in power and volume has been designed with thyristor controlled rectifier system feeding high current to the test section of the facility to simulate the fission heat flux generated after severe accident in nuclear reactor. The paper presents design considerations, development and subsequently the performance of 15 kA thyristor controlled, six pulse rectifier system. The circuit simulation of the rectifier system is also presented.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Quality using Advanced Artificial Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the present scenario of power system network, active filter are being designed using advanced technology for compensating harmonics and reactive power for better quality of power supply. The present paper implements a Shunt Hybrid Active Filter (SHAF), necessary for reactive power compensation in the nonlinear load and suppresses harmonics for improving the power quality (PQ) in the distribution network. In this work, an adaptive linear neuron (Adaline) based variable step size leaky least mean square (VSSLLMS) control approach is applied for extracting harmonics. This competent approach is needed for generating the gating pulses essential for IGBT inverter and increasing the performance compared to the conventional Adaline-LMS controller. The proposed controller provides faster convergence and also provides better performance compared to conventional one. Simulation results show the significant improvement in Adaline-VSSLLMS approach compared to Adaline-LMS approach. The simulations of the proposed controller and system is done using MATLAB/ SIMULINK under different load conditions.

Author Keywords: variable step size leaky least mean square (VSSLLMS)

articleTitle: DC-Link Voltage Regulation of Full-Power Converter for WECS in Weak-Grid Using a Variable-flux Dual-Stator PMSG
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) in weak-grid and stand-alone modes suffer from voltage and frequency fluctuations due to wind speed or/and load variations. However, it is needed to regulate output voltage before supplying to grid/load. Thus, generator output is rectified and then inverted to constant voltage and frequency before supplying to load. In standard configurations, rectifier and inverter both use controlled switches. Therefore, full control over the output voltage is achieved however, higher no. of electronic switches with their complex control circuitry and use of mechanical sensors jeopardizes reliability of the system. This paper proposes a WECS that uses half the no. of controlled switches with simpler control circuitry. It is to be noted that no mechanical sensors had been used in sensing the wind speed. The proposed system consists of a variable-flux dual-stator permanent magnet synchronous generator with an uncontrolled rectifier and an inverter working at constant modulation indexes. A proof-of-concept generator had been fabricated and tested under simulated wind conditions. The generator was tested for voltage regulation under two conditions. First under variable wind speed and constant load (VWCL) and second under constant wind speed and variable load (CWVL). It was observed from results that in proposed system the generator regulates its output voltage and power invariant to variable input wind speed and variable load.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Types of Voltage Sag and Its Effects on Adjustable Speed Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Voltage sag continues to be the most common power quality event causing repeated mal-operation of Adjustable Speed Drives (ASD). It either creates speed and torque fluctuations or completely shuts down the operation of ASD. This paper analyze the effects of different types of voltage sag on ASD. The analysis of this phenomenon, including the variation in DC link voltage, input RMS current of ASD, torque and speed of motor due to voltage sag are presented in this paper. A typical ASD with its parameters and different types of voltage sag are also discussed in this paper. To study the performance of the ASD under voltage sag, simulation based study is carried out for symmetrical, unsymmetrical and phase shifted voltage sag and results are presented comparatively. Different voltage sag mitigation techniques for ASD are discussed in brief.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control Technique for Load Sharing and Seamless Transition in Microgrid Mode of Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposed a hybrid control technique for AC microgrid in order to achieve adequate load sharing and seamless transition of microgrid between grid connected mode and islanded mode. The hybrid control technique is a combination of proposed modified droop control technique and modified power control technique. The modified droop control technique is developed to improve the dynamic response during the re-synchronization of microgrid to the main grid. In addition, a centralised controller is developed in order to participate all available DGs in the microgrid for re-synchronization to the mian grid by utilizing communication system, therefore the power stress on single DG is avoided. The performance of proposed hybrid control technique in the microgrid for seamless transition between mode of operations is verified by using real time simulator.

articleTitle: A Novel PWM Technique for MMCs with High Frequency Link and Natural Capacitor Balancing for Grid-Interfacing of Renewables
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new pulse width modulation (PWM) technique for a high-frequency link Modular Multilevel Converter topology for grid-integrated renewables. The topology generates a multilevel output voltage with low harmonic distortion, increased reliability, and design flexibility due to the modular nature of the converter. A central full-bridge converter is connected to multiple High Frequency Link modules via high frequency transformers. Each module produces its own isolated DC voltage, and modules are inserted or bypassed to synthesize large AC voltages. The proposed PWM technique equalizes module utilization without increasing losses, and retains inherent capacitor voltage balancing. Simulation results using SIMULINK models show that the proposed modulation scheme results in better performance than conventional schemes such as level-shifted carrier PWM, phase-shifted carrier PWM, hybrid schemes or nearest-level modulation.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Battery Embedded Fourth-Order Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Battery embedded fourth-order dc-dc boost Converter (BEFOBC), having two switches and two diodes is proposed in this paper. As this converter replaces the multiple converters used for dc system, space used for the dc system is appreciably reduced. In addition, utilization of battery within the converter provides the fixed output power irrespective of variation in irradiance and variation in load. Thus, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) at the input of converter and voltage regulation (VR) at the output of the converter is achieved simultaneously. A mathematical model is presented for its operation under charging and discharging condition of the battery. Two PI controllers are then designed and decoupled to ensure independent input current control for MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) and output voltage control for VR (Voltage Regulation). 30V to 48 V boost converter with an embedded battery of 12 V is considered in PSIM simulation to verify the working of this converter.

articleTitle: Eight Switch CHB based Three-Phase Shunt Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an eight switch Cascaded H bridge based three-phase three-wire shunt active power filter for mitigation of multiple power quality problems in source current. The proposed shunt active power filter established by using two H-Bridge and a capacitor in series with coupling inductor for reduction of DC link voltage. So the proposed topology not only save the component count but also reduces the voltage stress across each switch. A drawback of proposed eight switches shunt active filter is, DC link capacitor voltage unbalances. To defeat this drawback, the proposed topology employs a modified feedback control as an additional PI controller. i.e the proposed topology balances the DC link capacitors voltage by controlling both real and reactive power flow. The proposed shunt active power filter is analyses for mitigation of current harmonics, current unbalance and reactive power compensation. The performance of the proposed shunt active filter is analyzed and verified through MATLAB/ Simulink.

articleTitle: Basic Design equations of Linear Electric Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Application of linear electric machine has been increased in recent due to automation of the manufacturing industry, fast transport systems and various defence applications. These machines performance is superior to their rotary counterpart in various specialized applications. So it is necessary to derive the generic equations for designing of linear electric machines. Among different linear electric motors, linear induction motors (LIM) have been widely used due to their simplicity and low construction cost. During design stage of these LIM, it has been observed by the authors that basic design equations of rotary induction motors (RIM) are commonly used. Though the Equations of RIM can be used for design of LIM, but it does not gives a true flavor of LIM. Further, many specialized softwares for designing and analyzing require basic dimensions. These generic design equations of linear induction motor are derived and converted by referring conventional rotary induction motor in this paper. The simple design equation of LIM separates out basic dimensions of like length and width. The end effect and Edge effects are neglected in this study. Derived design equation is used to design double sided linear induction motor (DSLIM), 12 meter in length in this paper. Also 3D Maxwell software is used to analyze this motor at no-load condition.

articleTitle: A single phase cascaded five level Quasi Switched Boost Inverter based on switched capacitor structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multi Level Inverters (MLIs) are gaining more attention in medium voltage, high power applications. This paper presents a single phase Cascaded Five level quasi Switched Boost Inverter (CFqSBI) topology based on Switched Capacitor (SC) structure. The traditional cascaded MLI is able to produce an N level staircase output voltage waveform without any boost in the input voltage. The significant advantage of the CFqSBI topology is that it can boost the available dc input voltage along with the inversion operation compared to a conventional MLI due to the addition of switched capacitor structure. The design, modes of operation and steady state analysis of CFqSBI are elaborated. A modified phase shifted Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) algorithm is used to produce the firing pulses. The entire structure is simulated and analyzed in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. An experimental prototype of the proposed topology is designed for the output power of 200W to validate the operating principle of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Real-time estimation of model parameters and state-of-charge of lithiumion batteries in electric vehicles using recursive least-square with forgetting factor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A precise estimation of the lithium-ion battery's inner state, such as the state of health (SoH) and the state of charge (SoC) of the battery, is crucial for a reliable and effective performance of a battery management system in an electric vehicle. In this paper, an improved real-time model-based battery parameters estimation method using the recursive least-square algorithm with forgetting factor (RLS-FF) is proposed. Compared to the traditional methods, the proposed model yields the capability to accurately estimate the battery SoC and SoH by including the real-time variation of open circuit voltage and internal resistance of a battery, respectively. Moreover, a forgetting factor is used to capture the online parameter variations by reducing the impact of the older data to keep the model simple and suitable for EV applications. To verify the validity of the proposed model, an experimental test is carried out on a 2012 Nissan Leaf 31.1 Ah Manganese-oxide Li-ion battery cell.

articleTitle: A Novel Power Incremental GMPPT Method based on Modified Voltage Lines for Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Under the partial shading conditions (PSC), the characteristics of PV arrays show multiple maximum power points (MPPs). Conventional global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) method generally assume all peaks approximatively locating at the multiple of 0.8V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</sub>. However, it has been proven it is not really accurate. In this paper, an explicit expression of modified voltage lines for the multiple MPPs is derived, which is more accurate than the 0.8V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</sub> model. Based on the modified voltage lines, a novel power incremental GMPPT method is proposed. The searching area can be gradually reduced by an incremental power line.

articleTitle: New Modulation Techniques for Single Phase to Three Phase Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Single phase to three phase $(1\phi-3\phi)$ power conversion is of particular interest in rural electric systems and in the operation of three phase motor drives from a single phase supply. Conventionally, the conversion is brought about by AC to DC rectification, followed by generation of three phase voltages from a voltage source inverter (VSI). However, such a conversion requires a large DC link capacitor, making it unsuitable in applications where space and/or size constraints exist. Moreover, the presence of an energy storage element such as capacitor in the DC link, compromises on the reliability of the system. An alternative topology for $ 1\phi-3\phi$ power conversion is a $ 1\phi-3\phi$ direct matrix converter $(1\phi-3\phi\ {\mathrm {MC}})$, which brings about static power conversion from single phase to three phase without any intermediate DC link, hence eliminating the need for any energy storage element. Matrix converters are successfully used in three phase to three phase power conversion, however, $ 1\phi-3\phi$ MCs have not gained significant popularity due to their low output voltage ratio and also due to the presence of lesser order harmonics in their output voltages. This paper presents two novel strategies for the modulation of a $ 1\phi-3\phi$ matrix converter driving an inductive load, both addressing the problem of lower order harmonics in the output. It deals with delta-sigma modulation (DSM) for $ 1\phi-3\phi MCs,$ which is a voltage control technique at variable switching frequency. Further, modulated model predictive control (MMPC) is discussed as an alternative current control based modulation for the same converter. MMPC is an improvised variant of model predictive control that offers the benefit of a fixed switching frequency besides having a fast dynamic response.

articleTitle: A Variable DC Link Voltage in On-board Battery Chargers for Electric Vehicle Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The two-stage on-board battery chargers in electric vehicles consists of conventional boost power factor correction (PFC) stage and an isolated DC-DC converter stage. Conventionally, the DC link voltage at output of PFC converter in the on-board chargers is maintained at 400 V which limits the charger output voltage in a range of 36-48 V, 72-150 V and 200-450V based on selection of DC-DC converter. The proposed variable DC link voltage at output of PFC converter enables wide output voltage range of charger with same DC-DC converter. The conventional boost PFC converters has the limitation that the required output voltage to be always greater than the peak of the input voltage. This paper presents a non-inverting two-switch buck-boost power factor correction (PFC) converter for use in on-board battery chargers to provide a wide DC link voltage. The operating modes of the converter in output voltage less than the peak of the input voltage and greater than peak of input voltage are explained in detail. The topology also maintains high power quality in both the modes. A 1kW PFC converter with universal input voltage 85-265 V(rms) is simulated in PSIM (11.0) and the preliminary experimental results is also been presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Investigation of Pn and F-MRAS based Speed Estimators For Vector Controlled Switched Reluctance Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the unipolar excitation-based speed sensorless vector controlled SRM drive. The use of mechanical or direct position/speed sensor is not a good practice because of the cost, reliability, compactness and environmental issues to name a few. Therefore, for speed control of SRM drive, we necessarily require some estimation strategy which estimates the speed/position. Since the control of the machine is done in dq0 reference frame, so to utilize these variables for speed/position estimation which appear as d.c quantities in dq0 reference frame can be advantageous. From this view point, the “FMRAS (Flux based Model Reference Adaptive System)” and “Pn-MRAS (Net-Input Power based Model Reference Adaptive System)” based speed estimators are proposed and investigated for estimating the speed utilizing these mentioned dq0 quantities. The speed estimators implemented here are simple and free from obtaining of magnetization characteristics of the machine. Both Pn & FMRAS based speed estimators are completely stable in all the four quadrants of operation. Although being quite similar, the two estimators differ in few attributes. The FMRAS based speed estimator poses integrator in the adjustable model, while the Pn-MRAS based speed estimator is free from the integrator terms appearing in the adjustable model which is an advantage. Also, at one point of load Pn-MRAS based speed estimator becomes totally insensitive to rotor speed which makes estimation of speed totally impossible at that point. Hence, in this regard the FMRAS based estimator is better alternative to Pn-MRAS based speed estimator. The speed sensorless SRM drive has been extensively simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The MATLAB simulation results are also verified in real-time on typhoon-HIL platform.

articleTitle: Rank Ordering Criteria Based Weighting Factor Evaluation in Model Predictive Torque Control of Five-phase Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Predictive torque control (PTC) is an emerging and promising technology in electric drives. The effective performance of the PTC drive lies in its simple control law wherein different constraints can be easily added with weighting factors. However only empirical approximation methods are used for the determination of weighting factor. This paper presents a ranking weight method to find the weighting factor in predictive torque control of five-phase induction motor (IM). The weighting factor value is based on the rank ordering of the criteria (such as torque, flux, xy-plane current harmonics, CMV etc.) considered in the cost function. Assigning weights based on the rank of the criteria is more reliable than randomly assigning weights to the criteria because the decision makers are more confident on the ranks of the criteria than weights. Rank order centroid (ROC) weight technique is presented and compared with conventional weighting technique. The viability of the concept is verified by numerical simulations and the results are validated through experimentation.

articleTitle: Control of Mixed Energy Storage System Based Micro-grid Using Modulator-Less Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A grid interactive microgrid with mixed storage system is gaining appreciable attention in commercial and residential applications. Effective control is one of the key concerns in deployment of microgrids. Compared to conventional control strategies, dynamic model prediction based control schemes has better dynamic performance and can handle the inherent non-linearity of power electronic converters. Faster dynamic response as a basic requisite, this paper presents a modulator-less model predictive control (MPC) scheme for grid interactive microgird, which comprises Photovoltaic (PV) and Battery-Super capacitor (SC) based Mixed Energy Storage (MES). The complete control scheme consists of (i) A proportional-integral (PI) controller which generates the reference current to regulate dc-link voltage, (ii) A low pass filter (to segregate average and oscillatory components) with power managing scheme and (iii) Finite Control Set Model Predictive Controller (FCS-MPC) which controls the power converters to track the reference currents. The effectiveness of proposed scheme is verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: Design and Development of GaN HEMT Based High Performance LED Driver for Automotive DRL Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: LED technology paved way to rapid advancements in the automotive lighting with increased demands for safety and luxury. This paper presents design and development of a LED driver for DRL application using a modified Buck-Boost converter with GaN HEMT switching at 500kHz. High performance is achieved by using the GaN based HEMTs as switching device, with the primary advantage of switching at higher frequency with low losses. The converter topology is analyzed for the Bright/Dim operation requirements of the DRL application. GaN LED driver with a power rating of 9W was developed. Measures were taken to meet the critical parasitic restraints of high frequency power switching. The high performance of the module is test evaluated and it is having higher power density compared to the presently available DRL drivers. The technology has evolved as import substitute in this area of application. The proto model is further encapsulated to be demonstrated in the rugged environment of the in-vehicle operations.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of Isolated Buck (F1y-Buck) Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of time domain analysis of multi-output isolated buck (fly-buck) converter with and without considering the effect of parasitics in continuous conduction mode. Time domain analysis of fly-buck converter has been performed to study the transient and steady state behavior of a converter in a faster and more accurate manner. It constitutes the derivation of mathematical expressions for the parameters like inductor currents, capacitor voltages and output voltages in each mode by various methods such as expansion of state transition matrix as a power series, modal decomposition method etc. The inductor current waveforms obtained by plotting the derived mathematical expressions from time domain analysis in MATLAB, are compared with the waveforms obtained from PSpice simulation and percentage errors are calculated for each mode. The PSpice simulation of a 5W fly-buck converter operating with a switching frequency of 100 kHz is carried out to substantiate the analysis carried.

articleTitle: Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter Based Grid Integration of Solar Power with PQ Improvement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper a two stage Solar Energy Grid Connected System (SEGCS) with Zeta converter for DC-DC and Cascaded H-bridge Multilevel Inverter (CHB-MLI) for DCAC conversions are proposed. The shunt connected SEGCS is demonstrated with a non linear unbalance reactive local load. The active power generated in the Photo Voltaic (PV) system with respect to the irradiations is shared to the load and the grid. The reactive and distortion power demand of load is continuously delivered by the SEGCS and therefore keeping the grid voltage and current sinusoidal and in phase by implementing Synchronous Reference Frame Theory-Phase Disposition PWM (SRFT-PDPWM) based control. The power sharing by the cascaded H-bridges improves the power rating. The increased number of levels and reduced switching frequency results reduction in harmonics and filter dimensions compared to two level inverters. The performance of CHB-MLI is compared with other topologies in this paper. The wide range operation of Zeta converter utilized for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in addition with the firefly algorithm based duty ratio calculation. The Simulation analysis of the proposed work carried out with a 100 kVA capacity in MATLAB/SIMULINK model and a hardware prototype is developed. The steady state and dynamic performance of the SEGCS under various PV side and load side disturbances is carried out and results produced in this paper to validate the theory.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Resources Integration To Grid With Improved Power Quality Capabilities And Optimal Power Flows
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper a new control algorithm has been proposed to control the power flow of the utility grid which has been penetrated by renewable energy sources (RES). The proposed control algorithm ensures utility grid to undergo minimum power changes. The hybrid energy storage system consisting of high power density element such as super capacitor and high energy density element such as battery storage has been used to compensate the residual power. The proposed control algorithm has been implemented to the distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) to achieve multiple goals, such as integrating photo voltaic (PV) to the utility grid, compensating the reactive power and current related power quality issues and the power flow balancing. The balancing of the energy flows and current related power quality issues have been compensated using a DSTATCOM. The proposed configuration of the system has been implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and the corresponding simulation results are being presented in the manuscript.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Phase Locked Loop Controllers for Grid Tied Inverters in Weak Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper analyses, the effect of the phase locked loop (PLL) controller in the stability of the voltage source converter(VSC) in a microgrid or when connected to a weak AC grid. While designing the controller for PLL, it may not be possible to consider the effect of the load and line impedance as they are not readily known. In a microgrid or in a weak grid, the dynamics of the PLL are affected due to the high impedance nature of the network. A small signal model is built to show how the PLL controller affects the stability of the VSC. A comparison is made between proportional (P) and proportional-integral (PI) controller, using detailed time domain simulation in PSCAD/EMTDC to demonstrate this problem.

articleTitle: Robustness Analysis of H∞ Controller for Feedback Linearized Model of Grid Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a robust H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> mixed-sensitivity loop shaping control synthesis is proposed to stabilize a output feedback linearized grid-connected voltage source inverter (VSI) system. Traditionally, linear controllers are applied for the reliable operation of VSI to tackle small disturbances around a specific operating point. However, the performance of such controllers degrades under severe disturbances. Though there are several nonlinear control scheme to overcome issues related to operating points, but the robustness against different factors is not covered. The dynamical nonlinear model of VSI is linearized by output feedback linearization scheme to provide independent operating point. However, the feedback linearized system performance is depend on system parameters. The main contribution to investigate the robustness on existing controller for feedback linearized grid-connected VSI system under severe disturbance. The proposed scheme will be developed also to provide robustness during measurment noise rejection of output feedback signal.

articleTitle: Single stage PV fed reduced inverter based PMSM for standalone water pumping application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a standalone PV fed PMSM drive for water pumping. The proposed system aims at reducing the switching losses and overall cost by using reduced switch inverter. The proposed system comprises of a PMSM drive, fed by PV source through an inverter employing reduced number of switches. The inverter uses only four switches whereas the conventional VSI utilizes six switches. Field oriented control scheme is employed to control the PMSM drive. Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT technique is used to generate a speed reference to PMSM drive. Simulation studies for the proposed PV fed 400 W PMSM driven water pumping system are performed using MATLAB platform and respective results are presented to show the efficacy of the system.

articleTitle: A Matrix-Based Solid-State-Transformer For A Hybrid Nanogrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a Front-end Matrix based Bidirectional Solid-State-Transformer (SST) for a nanogrid having both AC and DC power distribution networks. A single-phase Matrix-converter (MC) is used to convert the line-frequency grid voltage to High-Frequency AC (HFAC). The MC is modulated using a modified Sinusoidal-Pulse-Width Modulation (SPWM) scheme. The HFAC voltage is then fed to a Current-Doubler-Rectifier (CDR) to form a stiff Low-Voltage DC (LVDC) bus. A bidirectional-converter is used to facilitate energy interaction in between the AC and DC buses of the nanogrid. Simulation of the proposed SST scheme is performed and the results are presented to verify the theoretical analysis. A comparative analysis of the proposed topology with other relevant topologies is also presented. The proposed topology has comaparatively high reliability, exhibits high power density and superior input side power quality.

articleTitle: A Space Vector Based PWM Scheme for Realization of Virtual Pentagon, Pentacle Connections in open-end Winding Five Phase Machine Drives with Single DC Source
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a Space Vector based Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) scheme for obtaining different virtual winding connections in a dual Inverter fed open end winding five phase machine drives with a single DC source. A five phase machine can have three possible winding connections named star, pentagon and pentacle. The winding changeover is a commonly used method to increase the voltage across the stator windings in a machine so as to extend the operational speed range. The winding connection changeover was initially achieved using magnetic contactors and later by power electronic switches. A smooth transition from one winding connection mode to the other can be virtually realized using dual inverter fed motor with open end stator windings by employing the space vector based PWM scheme presented in this paper. The proposed scheme requires only one DC source to produce virtual pentagon, pentacle connections and the PWM technique employed prevents flow of common mode current. The proposed scheme is experimentally validated on a five phase induction motor with open end stator windings using TMS320F28335 DSP as the digital platform for implementing the control scheme.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Submodule for MMC with DC Fault Ride-Through Capability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has become the most prominent topology for high voltage direct current (HVDC) applications due to its modularity, lower losses, less filtering requirements and flexible controllability. However, MMC still lacks in terms of efficiency and fault tolerant capability compared to the line commutated converters (LCC) based HVDC systems. This paper proposes a thyristor bypassed fault tolerant half bridge submodule (TBFT-HBSM) for MMC to achieve high efficiency as that in LCC while retaining DC fault tolerant capability and controllability. The lower switch of conventional HBSMs is replaced by anti-parallel thyristor switches to reduce the overall conduction losses of the converter. A new control algorithm has been proposed to balance the arm voltages. Moreover, loss analysis of proposed submodule (SM) is carried out and its efficiency compared with existing SM topologies. Simulation as well as experimental studies are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed SM structure and its control.

articleTitle: Improved Power Quality LED Driver with SELV Norms for Streetlight Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, Light Emitting Diode (LED) driver design for streetlight application is given according to safety extra low voltage (SELV) norms without compromising high power quality and efficiency. The LED driver is developed in constant current mode in order to get same brightness even at forward voltage reduction of power LED due to ageing effect or phosphor quality. The current regulation is less than 2% for input voltage range (110V-275V AC). The input low voltage and high voltage cuts are implemented at 85VAC and 300VAC respectively with 25V hysteresis. The LED open as well short circuit protections are implemented in this design. The input current total harmonic distortion (THD) and power factor (PF) are less than 10% and more than 0.97 respectively. It is Implemented using low cost THD enhancer analog circuit. The power converter is of 90W rating with 24-36V/2.5A LED load operation. The overall efficiency of power converter is more than 87%.

articleTitle: Single-Phase to Three-Phase Power Converter with Reduced DC-Link Voltage Ripple and Grid Current Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a single-phase to three-phase converter topologies with the DC link voltage ripple reduction and grid-side current quality improvement with proposed bus-clamping pulsewidth modulation control. In this paper, performance of conventional five-leg (5L) converter, four-leg (4L) converter and parallel five-leg (P5L) converter are compared. Conventionally, the active front-end converter with sinusoidal pulsewidth modulation (SPWM) scheme and space vector pulsewidth modulation (SVPWM) technique for inverter side control is adopted in such topologies. In these converters, the low frequency voltage oscillation across the dc-link capacitor is the inherent problem. It is proposed to use advanced bus clamping PWM (ABCPWM) technique for the load side inverter to reduce such ripples. This modulation technique minimizes the dc-link voltage oscillation and also improves the inverter output current and voltage profile in terms of reduced current and voltage THD. The grid current with reduced THD and unity power factor operation for conventional five-leg (5L) converter, four-leg (4L) converter and parallel five-leg (P5L) converter is also presented. The performance comparison of single-phase to three-phase power converter for these topologies with 30° ABCPWM control through simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Minimization of the Number of Full-Bridge Submodules in Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Hybrid modular multilevel converter (MMC) topology, employing both half-bridge (HB) and full-bridge (FB) submodules (SMs), has dc fault current limiting capacity. In order to add the capacity of reactive power support to the ac grid during dc fault, higher proportion of FB-SMs are required which results in increase of cost and losses. This work attempts to minimize the proportion of the FB-SMs without compromising the performance. The major obstacle faced is the tendency of MMC arm currents to become unipolar with reduction in the dc voltage. This phenomenon affects the cyclic charge/discharge of the HB-SMs in the MMC which depends on the polarity of the arm currents. A method is proposed in this work where a second harmonic circulating current (SHCC) is injected in each leg of the MMC during the reduced dc voltage conditions. This ensures that the arm currents have both the polarities at any dc voltage level. Hence, the unnecessary increase of FB-SMs can be avoided. The method is tested through simulations performed on PSCAD /EMTDC software platform.

articleTitle: Single Carrier-Based Pulse Width Modulator for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Carrier-based pulse width modulation (PWM) schemes are the preferred choice for modular multilevel converters (MMCs) due to their simplicity and ease of implementation. However, the required number of carriers for gating signal generation drastically increases with the number of submodules (SMs) in an MMC. These carriers should be accurately synchronized with each other to generate the high-quality output voltage and current waveforms. However, it is difficult to achieve the synchronization due to the memory constraints, sampling issues, computational delays, and control complexity. To overcome these issues, a simple single carrier-based PWM modulator is proposed in this paper. In addition, a simple SM capacitor voltage-balancing approach with less computational burden is presented. The proposed scheme can be easily applied to the n-level MMC without any modifications and applicable to any SM type. The effectiveness of the proposed modulation scheme and SM capacitor voltage balancing algorithm is demonstrated through the simulations in the PLECS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software platform.

articleTitle: Control Scheme for Improved Efficiency in a H-bridge Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a control scheme for achieving improved efficiency in a H-bridge buck-boost DC-DC converter. The H-bridge buck-boost converter with conventional control scheme operates at lower efficiency compared to buck and boost converter for the same step down/up action, due to the absence of direct power component. A control scheme is presented in this paper to achieve better efficiency by introducing maximum direct power component without affecting the steady state voltage gain. A hardware prototype of 500 W is tested with the proposed control scheme and an efficiency improvement of 4 % is observed as compared to that of the conventional control.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Allocation of Capacitors in Radial Distribution System using Sine Cosine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The present work implements Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA) for obtaining optimal location and size of capacitor banks for addressing problems like voltage instability and line losses in radial distribution systems. By using power loss index (PLI) method, the buses that are more sensitive to the capacitor placement are identified and, thereafter, the location and size are optimized by using proposed SCA. The main objective of the system is considered as the minimization of the total cost. The algorithm is implemented on 33 bus and 69 bus test systems and the results obtained are compared with those yielded using other algorithms.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Quadratic Following Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A boost converter following the quadratic gain is proposed in this paper. At moderate duty ratios, this converter is able to step-up a lower source voltage to a higher load voltage, which is higher than the traditional boost converter. Its gain almost follows the conventional quadratic boost converter gain with an offset. Steady-state analysis is performed for this converter in continuous conduction mode and then a state-space average model is derived. A systematic procedure for selection of L-C components is established. A PID type controller is also designed for closed loop operation and stabilization. A 36 to 100 V, 60 W converter is first used in simulation. Prototype of the proposed system is made and then experimental measurements are captured for validation. Simulation and experimental results are in close agreement with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: A Three-Level Half-Bridge Flying Capacitor Topology for Single-Stage AC-DC LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: LLC resonant converters are one of the best choices in AC-DC converters. But, low power factor is a serious problem in AC-DC LLC resonant converters. Adding a boost circuit in front of the converter improves the power factor albeit the increase in circuit complexity. To reduce the size and cost, both the boost and LLC stage can be controlled by the same switches. However, these single stage topologies are less efficient in regulating DC bus capacitor voltage pertaining to transients in the line voltage and load conditions. The paper proposes a new single stage topology for AC-DC LLC resonant converters. The circuit consists of three-level half-bridge flying capacitor topology. Discontinuous conduction mode ensures inherent unity power factor operation. Switching frequency control and PWM duty ratio control are used to regulate the output voltage and bus capacitor voltages of the converter respectively. This dual control scheme makes the converter DC bus voltage nearly constant over a wide range of load and line voltage variations. Furthermore, the three level topology guarantees reduced switching stress and losses. The operation of the topology has been validated using MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: An Experimental Validation of single-phase AC power Generation from PV using H-bridge Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: solar energy is considered as one of the fastest growing renewable energy sources after wind energy for electrical power generation and is clean, abundant and free in nature. The power generation from solar photovoltaic system mainly depends upon environmental conditions such as temperature and irradiance. In which, photo voltaic (PV) output power varies mostly on variation of irradiation and which reflects on PV output current. Because, the voltage supplied to electrical loads must be almost constant and this can be achieved with the help of closed loop control of DC-DC boost converter. The output from PV panels is DC hence for AC load applications two stage conversion circuits are required such as DC-DC converter for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and an DC-AC inverter to achieve desired AC voltage and frequency. In this paper, a DC-DC boost converter along with perturb and observe (P&O) MPPT and an H-bridge 2-level inverter is designed to convert the DC voltage to chopped AC voltage and filtered to give pure sinusoidal AC output. The output from the inverter is fed to transformer to get 230-volt AC RMS value, which makes the system suitable for local AC loads are simulated in MATLAB-SIMULINK environment as well as validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Ampacity Estimation for HV Submarine Power Cables Installed in Saturated Seabed
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The maximum current carrying capacity of a power cable (Ampacity) is determined by the thermal characteristics of the cable components and surrounding medium in which they are buried. Power cable ampacity calculations are based on typical standard tables defined with predetermined parameters. In real-time, the environment of installation plays significant role in cable current carrying capacity. This paper presents FEM approach to determine the maximum current capacity within the safe operating limits of the cable. The study includes complex thermoelectric coupling and heat transfer in different zones surrounding the cable and its effect on the conductor operating temperature. The results show the difference between the proposed approach and standard calculations and improvements to accurate rating of the cables.

articleTitle: Fixed-Frequency MCCF Based Grid Synchronization Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) is widely adopted for estimating the grid voltage parameters. A good dynamic performance of SRF-PLL can be achieved under ideal grid conditions. However, its performance devolves in the presence of harmonics and fundamental negative-sequence (FNS) component. To address this issue, two module (TM) fixed frequency multiple complex coefficient filter (FF-MCCF) which acts as a prefilter. The frequency adaptive MCCF structure increases the overall dynamic response of the PLL. Further, under off-nominal frequency condition, TM-FFMCCF output introduces error in the estimated phase and amplitude. However, estimated frequency will not suffer any error in estimation. The error compensation in the estimated phase and amplitude is done by developing an error correction criteria. The implementation of proposed scheme is through with MAT-LAB/Simulink environment. Various test cases are considered and results are presented.

articleTitle: Adaptive Bandpass Digital Filter Control of Photovoltaic-Battery Energy Storage Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new control of a solar photovoltaic (PV) array with a battery energy storage (BES) based microgrid. This microgrid is interfaced to the three phase grid at point of common coupling (PCC). A bidirectional converter connects BES at DC link of voltage source converter (VSC) and regulates the discharging and charging currents of the battery. The VSC operates in a current control technique in the grid connected mode, whereas in standalone mode, VSC operates in the voltage control. The fundamental current component of nonlinear load, is obtained through an adaptive lattice bandpass digital filter. The current control algorithm is used for power factor correction and load balancing. It utilizes the feed-forward term of solar PV (FFPV) array to enhance the dynamic performance of proposed microgrid under variable environmental conditions. The changeover between current control to voltage control, is achieved through a solid state switch. The operation of microgrid system is validated through hardware in loop with OPAL-RT. Its performance is observed satisfactory in both modes during dynamics and transitions.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Medium Frequency High Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The use of medium frequency allows the transformer size to be reduced at the higher power level. Reduction in size of the transformer leads to a reduction in installation area which is of prime concern in many renewable energy resources. But the reduction in size at higher power level comes with the cost of higher loss density and lower thermal stability. Therefore, this paper deals with the various constraints and considerations that are required to be taken care of while designing the medium frequency high power transformer (MFHPT). This paper also provides the optimal design of transformer w.r.t. frequency and power. For analysis and comparison purpose, both core and shell type design is developed in Ansys Maxwell (Ver. 16) for 3 MVA transformers at 1000 Hz of frequency using nanocrystalline core material.

articleTitle: 2-DOF Controlled Interleaved DC/DC Converter Operating in CCM Using Characteristic Ratio Assignment for Green Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents closed loop operation of Inter-leaved boost converter using 2-Degree of Freedom (2-DOF) with characteristic ratio assignment to achieve desired characteristics at high switching frequency. In two 2-DOF control configuration the forward and the feedback paths are independently controlled to achieve the desired set point response and to eliminate the disturbance. The closed loop DC-DC PWM Interleaved boost converter with the 2-DOF PID controller are studied and analytical expressions of controllers are derived by specifying to desired closed-loop transfer function using characteristic ratio assignment (CRA). From the transfer functions of boost converter using an linear averaged circuit small-signal model with 2-DOF PID controller we have achieved very good set point response, and that it provides better performance over simple PID controller in terms of faster rise time and disturbance rejection. The proposed design method for boost converter demonstrate better performance.

articleTitle: Effective Utilisation of Solar Energy Conversion System with Energy Storage in AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The microgrid system proposed in this paper, strives to offer a solution to the problems faced by the consumers by supplying a minimum of a predefined amount of power into the utility from the solar energy conversion system (SECS) when the load is peaking thus preventing the cost per unit from shooting up. The proposed AC microgrid consists of a SECS connected to a DC link through a boost converter, which takes care of the operation at the maximum power point. An energy storage (ES), consisting of a battery bank and a bidirectional converter (BDC), is connected to the DC link. The DC link is connected to a voltage source converter (VSC), which is subsequently integrated to the grid through interface reactors and ripple filters. The design of the AC microgrid consisting of the SECS, boost converter, ES, VSC and the BDC along with a nonlinear load has been exhibited systematically. The modelling and simulation of this designed AC microgrid system are carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. Simulated results obtained from this model are authenticated by conducting experimental studies on a hardware prototype built in the laboratory.

articleTitle: High Voltage Gain q-ZSI with Low Inrush Current
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The high amount of inrush current that flows during the initial run-time of a classical ZSI/q-ZSI has been a major problem in the field of energy converters, owing its existence mainly to the use of dc-link capacitors in the design. This paper proposes a modified L-Z source inverter (L-ZSI), which offers a high voltage gain and eliminates the use of the dc-link capacitors. The proposed topology uses a Switched Inductor (SL) structure, containing a capacitor in series with the inductors. This capacitor helps in absorbing voltage spikes appearing across the dc-link voltage due to sudden changes in inductor current in the non-shoot through state. Moreover, being in series with the inductors, the capacitor also reduces the inrush current flowing through the switched structure circuit. Additionally, this topology offers a common ground for the input dc source and the main inverter circuit. Thus, the proposed topology provides an increase in voltage gain an overall reduction in weight, volume and cost of the inverter. These results from the derived network were validated in a MATLAB/Simulink generated environment, and then on an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Detection and Analysis of Power Quality Variations for initiating control actions in DGs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Identification and classification of Power Quality (PQ) events have been a subject of recent interest for researchers from the point of view of initiating suitable control actions in Distributed Generation Systems (DGs) for achieving improved performance. This requires carrying out a detailed analysis of the various characteristics of real time electrical signals through a set of signal processing techniques. In this context, two major parameters are considered to arrive at suitable control actions needed for monitoring and control of DGs. These parameters include PQ distortions due to environmental factors, such as change in wind speed and solar irradiations. Signal features are extracted using S-Transform while signal-classification is done by Least Square Support Vector Machine (LS-SVM) technique. A 17-bus test system is modeled using the open source software, Open Distribution System Simulator (OpenDSS). LS-SVM and S-Transform are implemented using MatLab. Smart converter control is realized with inputs received from signal classifier, so as to initiate proper grid-support functions.

articleTitle: QFT based Robust Controller design for Switched Inductor-Capacitor Hybrid Buck–SEPIC Two-Input DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper discusses about the robust control strategy applied to Switched inductor-Capacitor Hybrid Buck-SEPIC Two-Input DC-DC converter (SICHBSTIC) suitable for giving wide range of voltages for different applications. The prime concern of multi-input converter topologies is to trim the burden on primary source, and also provide wide range of output voltages. Further it is necessary for MIC to maintain the voltage-regulation and load-sharing, ensuring the stable operation throughout its usage. The SICHBSTIC is operated in continuous conduction mode, and discrete-time models of converter are established for trailing-edge pulse width modulation. The multi-input multi-output (MIMO) robust Quantitative feedback theory (QFT) based control strategy is employed in discrete-domain to study and control the disturbances and uncertainties. A 36/12 V to 24 V and 200 W DC power rating is considered to verify converter robust control in simulation environment.

articleTitle: Impact of Crash Override and Tampering Communication Data Cyber-Attacks on the Power Quality of the Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Energy storage is an essential device in a smart hybrid system. The hybrid grid controllers are regulated through an Internet based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. The involvement of internet makes the system vulnerable to cyber-attacks and affects the performance of the system. This work analyzes the effects of cyber-attacks on the performance of a supercapacitor energy storage (SES) located in a hybrid grid system. Two types of cyber-attacks, such as the tampering communication data/signals and crash override, targeting the controllers of the energy storage system, have been considered. To quantify the results, two indices, namely the voltage index (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">index</sub>) at the point of common coupling (PCC) and the total harmonic distortion (THD) have been evaluated. Simulations have been performed by using the Matlab/Simulink software. Simulation results show that the performance of the hybrid grid system is deteriorated due to the cyber-attacks on the SES controller.

articleTitle: Performance Investigations of Adaptive ANN-SVPWM Controlled Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Efficient and Adaptive Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) for mitigating harmonics is presented in the paper. ANN based reference current generation is implemented using Neural Synchronous method while Levenberg Marquardt method is used for training algorithm. ANN based Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (ANN-SVPWM) controller is realized for the effective control of SAPF. Performance of the proposed ANN-SVPWM controller is compared with conventional Hysteresis Current Controller (HCC). Hence, both the reference compensating currents as well as controller of the proposed SAPF are realized using Artificial Neural Network. Effective compensation of the load harmonics and good dynamic response of the ANN based SAPF is proved by the presented simulation results using MATLAB. The proposed SAPF effectively compensates for the load harmonics in steady-state as well as during dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Robust Control of IPMSG Based Wind Energy Conversion Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust control approach for IPMSG based direct drive wind energy conversion systems to extract maximum possible power under varying weather condition. The proposed control approach is robust against parametric and modelling uncertainties. The proposed approach includes nonlinear back-stepping control with sliding mode observer (SMO) theory. The SMO is used to estimate the disturbance in the IPMSG based wind energy conversion system model arising due to parametric and modelling uncertainties. The effectiveness of the proposed approach has been validated through rigorous simulation studies carried out on a grid connected direct drive IPMSG wind energy conversion system.

articleTitle: 3L Switching Sequences using Parallel Connected 2L VSIs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper analyzes two parallel connected two-level (2L) three-phase voltage source inverters (VSIs) as a single three-level (3L) VSI. Conventionally the parallel connected 2L VSIs are modulated using the continuous and discontinuous 2L pulse-width modulation (PWM) techniques. However, any conventional 3L VSI PWM technique could also be implemented using parallel connected 2L VSIs. Moreover, for implementing a 3L PWM technique or 3L switching sequence using the parallel connected 2L VSIs, there could be many 2L switching sequences. Among the different 2L switching sequences, depending on the system constraints such as individual VSIs line current ripple, circulating current, and switching loss appropriate 2L switching sequence is found out for implementing a 3L switching sequence. Analytical, simulation, and experimental results are also provided.

articleTitle: Standalone PV system based on Isolated Quasi Z-Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Standalone PV system based on isolated quasi zsource dc-dc converter is proposed in this paper. Low voltage PV source and battery is integrated on quasi z-source network. Battery is integrated through bidirectional dc-dc converter. Voltage boost is obtained by using shoot-through method as well as isolation transformer. The output of the isolation transformer is rectified, and the dc voltage output is then used as an input of the single phase inverter which supplies to AC load. The PV source and battery power flow control algorithm is proposed. The proposed configuration and control method is verified with simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of High Frequency, High Ratio Transformer configurations for DC-DC Converter Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a study of different high-frequency transformer winding configurations. Impact of winding configuration on the parasitics is studied. A Finite element analysis solver is used to obtain leakage inductance and winding capacitance. An optimal layout is identified, built for a 1 kVA, 10 kHz prototype and tested in order to the study the performance in terms of efficiency and regulation. It is presented that the optimal layout reduces the parasitics effects. Experimental results of performance show good agreement with the simulation based on model estimation.

articleTitle: A Novel wavelet Technique for fault detection in Transmission line during Power Swing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper a wavelet technique based spectral energy is proposed to detect both symmetrical as well as unsymmetrical fault during the power swings. As the fault detection is a great challenge in the power swing period, this technique must help for fast detection of all types of fault. This technique starts with measuring current signals at relay points and process through it in discrete wavelet transform at a low sampling rate to calculate the detail coefficient in first level. In this technique the extraction of current is done by daubechies in Db-4 wavelet. The identification and classification of fault job is done by the spectral energy of detail coefficient (D1). The performance of the discussed scheme is tested on 400 kV single machine infinite bus (SMIB) parallel transmission system through PSCAD/EMTDC platform. The simulation results clearly describes the effectiveness of the algorithm for reliable and accurate fault classification and fast detection.

articleTitle: PEDES 2018 Tutorial Sessions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the tutorial presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Performance improvement in PM machine using two-piece stator design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Miniature permanent magnet (PM) brushless motors used in Industrial power tool application require high torque and efficiency. Further, the size constraints imposed by the hand-held tool requires the use of high torque density motor. Therefore, by utilizing the stator slot area to achieve the required number of amperes turns is important while considering the low-cost motor solution. Existing single-piece stator lamination design has poor conductor fill factor in the slots due to manual insertion of the coils in the narrow slot opening. Hence to solve the poor slot fill factor (SFF) and to simplify the winding process, the stator lamination is split into two-parts and the pre-wound coils are placed outwards in the open slots. This results in increased SFF and result into 22% improvement on motor regulation. The FEA based the simulation is carried out and simulated motor performance is validated with experimental results. In addition, the challenges during the prototype motor build is discussed.

articleTitle: Wind-Storage Hybrid Turbine - Field Deployment Experience
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With increased penetration of renewables, particularly wind and solar, the need for providing flexible and predictable output from the renewable plant is critical. To meet such requirements, an energy buffer such as battery storage which can be controlled and integrated with the renewable plant in a cost-effective manner is a key enabler. This paper presents a wind turbine integrated storage solution which was deployed at a wind farm in the United States. Such demonstrated capability can provide confidence in technology which has the potential of enabling large scale shift to renewables.

articleTitle: A new Three Phase 5L-UIPFC for wind energy applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new multi-point clamped (MPC) structured, three phase five level uni-directional improved power factor converter (TP5L-UIPFC) for wind energy integration application is proposed. The converter can be modeled as classical MPC structured converters like diode clamped converter with reduced device count due to the omission of clamping diodes. The validation of a new TP5L-UIPFC with carrier based PWM controlling scheme is verified with simulation and a down scaled prototype experimental setup.

articleTitle: Decentralized economic model predictive control for energy efficiency in a multi-zone building
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to design a decentralized economic model predictive control (eMPC) strategy for an HVAC system in a multi-zone building. The primary source of coupling between interconnected zones is the shared walls of which a direct temperature measurement is either not available or difficult to obtain. To circumvent this issue, we design a full order nonlinear state-observer to estimate the walls temperatures of zones using which the system is decomposed into control-oriented thermal models of individual zones. Subsequently, a decentralized eMPC is designed whose economic performance, in fact, turns out to be the same as that of a centralized control strategy. As a result, the control signal is now computed faster for a longer prediction horizon, thereby, makes the proposed eMPC scheme suitable for the real-time implementation. The effectiveness of the proposed control approach is demonstrated on a one floor, three-zone building constructed using SIMulation of Building and Devices (SIMBAD) toolbox.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Control For Power Sharing Between Single Phase Parallel Inverter In Autonomous Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Single phase VSCs are in use mainly for low power level resources and can be used for responsibility of maintaining the voltage and frequency for power transfer to the loads conected to a single phase microgrid. This paper presents an adaptive droop control based algorithm between the parallel single phase inverters for proportionate active and reactive power-sharing between them in the wake of varying network parameters and changing loads. A MATLAB based simulation results are presented in the paper to support the proposed control algorithm towards satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: A Large Signal Dynamic Model of Loosely Coupled IPT System for EV Based on Laplace Phasor Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper presents a new Laplace phasor transform based feasibility study of LCL topology for dynamic inductive power transfer (IPT) system. The developed large signal model of the complex power electronic converter makes a reliable dynamic model of the system. Analysis of this higher order resonant circuit based on Laplace phasor transform is simpler and accurate than the conventional analysis technique. The experimental results from the developed prototype corroborates the simulation results and theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Novel Methodology for Sensorless Control of Three Phase Variable Inductance BLDC Motor Driven Thruster for Under Water Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for sensorless control of three phase BLDC motor driven thruster utilizing variable inductance nature. The methodology proposes utilization of peaks and valleys of the phase inductance to generate commutation instants/firing sequence for sensorless control. It is shown through simulation studies of a BLDC motor incorporating position dependent inductances that the firing instants corresponds to peak or valley points in the line inductance. The same is also validated through finite element analysis and experimental studies of the motor. A sensorless control scheme is proposed based on these observations.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Steepest Descent Optimization for MTPA Control of IPMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper describes a maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control for Interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM). The proposed method operates the IPMSM at the MTPA angle which optimizes the stator current by dividing it into d-axis and q-axis currents. The proposed method does not rely on motor parameters and converges quickly to the operating point. It uses the `Steepest Descent' optimization method with two objectives: following the reference torque, and, doing so at the MTPA angle. The partial derivatives required for the Steepest Descent are evaluated by injecting virtual signals into the modeled torque equation and extracting the desired dc component by heterodyning. Since actual injections into the machine are not made, the resulting disadvantages are avoided. The method is robust and works under dynamic conditions. The validity of the proposed method is proved by extensive simulations.

Author Keywords: Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) Drive

articleTitle: Modeling and Voltage Regulation of Boost Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A better performing, non-ideal high single stage inverter for generating a regulated, lower level THD ac output voltage which is greater than the unregulated dc input voltage is suggested in this literature. This work is developed in contrast to the traditional Voltage Source Inverter, which always generates lesser ac instantaneous output voltage with higher levels of THD. The suggested topology is supervised by a suitable instantaneous controlled input. A detailed mathematical modeling, a vast examination, and the simulated results are also included for verification of the non-ideal boost inverter topology presented. The obtained results effectively validate the suggested strategy.

articleTitle: LQR based Active Damping of Induction Motor Drive with Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Sinusoidal LC filter are generally placed in between a voltage source inverter (VSI) and a squirrel cage induction motor (SQIM) to lessen the harmonic distortion in the stator voltage as well as stator current and also to reduce the high voltage surges at the motor terminals. However, it may destabilize the operating points of the rotor-flux oriented control (RFOC) of the SQIM drive with filter due to the resonance frequency oscillations as found in the voltage and the current profile of the SQIM. Therefore, the instability of the closed loop SQIM drive with filter at two operating points has been investigated, and an active damping technique has been proposed to stabilize the unstable operating points of RFOC of the SQIM drive with filter by damping out the resonance frequency oscillations without any active power loss.

articleTitle: Current Error SVPWM based Speed Sensorless IM Drive with Stator Resistance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A current error space vector PWM (CESV-PWM) based speed sensor-less vector control scheme with on-line stator resistance estimation for induction motor (IM) drive is presented in this paper. The current error space vector PWM based control introduces inherent protection against over-current while ensuring fast dynamic response. Absence of speed sensors makes the overall drive system rugged. A stator resistance estimator is employed to improve the accuracy of the speed estimator at low speeds and high loads. The proposed scheme is extensively simulated on a MATLAB-Simulink environment. The scheme is experimentally verified on an induction motor using TMS320F28335 DSP as the digital platform for control scheme implementation.

articleTitle: Control Methods of Sine-Cosine Motor for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric motors which are used in spacecraft for different payload mechanism should be capable to deliver smooth and continuous torque efficiently in terms of power and mass. Slot-less Sine-Cosine motor, a type of Brushless Permanent Magnet motor with sinusoidal back emf pattern is a suitable candidate for such applications. This paper presents the control methods of a Slot-less Sine-Cosine Motor. Two major control methods are discussed with its merits and demerits.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control based Dual-Port Back to Back Current Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a configuration of dual input dual output back to back converter with current source converter topology. The rectifier is capable of converting the dual three phase source with 6 diodes. The common DC link is connected with a reactor. The inverter with six semiconductor switches capable of supplying two independent loads. The control strategy is based on integral sliding mode control. The prototype model is fabricated and performance is analysed. The dual port back to back converter is capable of supplying to two independent loads or to grid and load.

articleTitle: High voltage network resonances in hybrid electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: the automotive industry is currently undergoing tremendous changes with the rapid adoption of electric power train technology. The market players are currently experimenting with the proven technologies to bring their versions of electric vehicles to market. One of the biggest pitfall in this approach is that, since the requirements come in a top down manner. The component level requirements may not be considered in the initial stages of the development. There can be resonances between the components which may not be very obvious at the first Iteration of the design. This paper presents a study of such a resonance behavior at the DC link in a parallel inverter set up used in hybrid electric vehicle (HEV).

articleTitle: Modular Multi-Input-Isolated Voltage Multiplier Converter for PV fed DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A PV interfaced new Multi-input-port isolated voltage multiplier converter (MIP-IVMC) feeding the DC microgrid is proposed. The ability of the proposed converter to provide high voltage gain utilizing multiplier cells facilitates integration of multiple low voltage PV panels with the 380V DC microgrid. MIP-IVMC incorporates high frequency transformer with the facility of maintaining quasi square voltage in the winding and is capable of reducing the voltage stress on the devices, therefore reducing the conduction loss and improving the efficiency. The input stage of the proposed converter significantly reduces the ripple at the input side by interleaving the current in the inductors. The case of 500W MIP-IVMC feeding the DC microgrid integrating two PV panels in parallel are considered while avoiding the flow of circulating current. The presented results demonstrate fast dynamics and efficient tracking of maximum power under all conditions, even during partial shading conditions. The proposed converter exhibits flexible, robust and reliable operation under all conditions.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling and Non Linear Control of SSSC to enhance Power Flow in IEEE 5 bus System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
