Droop controlling of bi-directional DC/DC converter is performed for both charging and discharging operation. A MATLAB/Simulink model of SoC based droop control included three battery units with bidirectional DC/DC converter system is developed and simulation results at the constant speed of EV are shown to demonstrate and verify the approach. Then federal urban driving schedule of an EV is applied as a load to test the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Single Phase Transformer Excited by Superposition of Square and Sine Wave
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper the performance of single phase two winding transformers is analyzed when excited by a voltage produced by superposition of square and sine wave and supplying different kind of loads. The transformer is excited in this manner to increase its voltage rating which results in power capacity enhancement. A study is carried out to access the response of two different class of transformers, small transformer (1 KVA) and distribution transformer (25 KVA) with different loads, for above said input. The effect of above said excitation on magnetizing current, load voltage, and load current is analyzed and compared with sine wave excitation. To access the effectiveness of this power capacity enhancement method, numerical simulations are carried out and the empirical results are presented.

articleTitle: A New Soft-Switched High Gain Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new soft-switched high gain coupled-inductor boost converter operating within permissible range of duty ratio. All semiconductor switches of the proposed converter change their states under soft switched condition and the diodes commutate softly. Operation of the proposed converter is presented and analyzed in detail. A hardware prototype of the proposed converter rated with nominal 16V-24V input, 220V/500 W output and 100 kHz switching frequency was designed, fabricated and tested in the laboratory. Switching behavior of the converter was found to be matching with the predictions.

articleTitle: A Shadow Tolerant Configuration for PV Integration to Grid using Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A shadow-tolerant photovoltaic converter configuration using the modular multilevel converter and the differential power processing converter without compromising the efficiency of the overall system is presented in this work. The proposed configuration is able to extract maximum power from the unshaded panels in the photovoltaic string under partially shaded condition, therefore, increasing the overall energy yield. A method to eliminate capacitor voltage ripple on the unshaded PV module is presented. This further improves the efficiency of energy collection by mitigating the effects of voltage ripple around the maximum operating point.

articleTitle: Selection of Voltage Levels in DC Microgrids using DC Bus Signaling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DC Bus Signaling (DBS) is reported in the literature as an economical method for power management in DC microgrids, in which, the DC bus voltage is used as an indirect communication signal among the elements present in the microgrid. The bus voltage is regulated at different levels by different microgrid elements depending on the mode of operation. Choice of these voltage levels is guided by the microgrid architecture, type and length of cables, number of elements in the microgrid and acceptable voltage drop. This paper analyzes the factors responsible and the related trade-offs for selection of these voltage levels. Also, the extendibility of DC microgrid with the increase in distances among the elements and increase in number of elements is one major concern in DBS scheme. The DBS scheme discussed in this paper ensures effective power handling irrespective of the power/energy rating and availability of microgrid elements. Detailed simulation results are presented in support of the analysis.

articleTitle: Non-linear Magnetic Characteristics Modeling for Switched Reluctance Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a simple mathematical model for the non-linear magnetic characteristics of a switched reluctance machine (SRM). The proposed model realizes the flux-linkage characteristics by representing the flux-linkage as a unique non-linear function of the excitation current and its coefficients vary with the rotor position. This proposed model is based on a rational function with first-order and second order polynomials in the numerator and denominator, respectively. Initially, for simplicity, it is considered that the coefficient of the numerator is equal to the air-gap inductance. Then, the coefficients of denominator is obtained using the nonlinear regression to fit inductance and excitation current profile under saturation. For validation, these characteristics, obtained from the proposed model and standard finite element method using Ansys Maxwell, are compared along with the current waveforms to confirm the accuracy of the proposed model. Finally, a sensor-less scheme is implemented, where the turn-off angle is estimated using the proposed model, and results are presented for further validation of the proposed model.

articleTitle: A new Dual Stator-Dual Rotor Switched Reluctance Motor for Electric vehicle propulsion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Switched Reluctance drives are gaining importance as an alternative to Permanent magnet BLDC motors due to their low cost and simple construction. In this paper a new Dual stator-Dual rotor Switched reluctance motor (DS-DR SRM) is proposed which is competent to Permanent magnet Brushless DC motor (PM-BLDC) with high power density. Non-linear magnetic analysis on the machine is carried out using 2-D Finite element model and all the magnetic parameters and load characteristics of the machine are derived. The current-torque characteristics of the proposed topology is compared with conventional external rotor SRM and observed an increment of 30% in peak torque density. The proposed motor is best suitable for high Power density applications where non-permanent magnet machines are gaining importance like electrical vehicles.

articleTitle: Predictive Average Current Control Considering Non-Idealities for a Boost PFC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The design of the current control loop in a boost PFC converter plays a significant role due to the large signal variations in the input waveforms. A predictive average current control law based on triangular modulation considering the converter non-idealities, time variation of waveforms and computation delays is proposed and validated with simulation and experimental results. A digital method for the boost inductance value estimation is also proposed which could be used with predictive current control laws.

articleTitle: A Two Switch Non-Isolated High Gain DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a two switch non-isolated high gain DC-DC converter at low duty operating region with reduced number of elements is proposed. It is derived from a single-phase quasi Z-source inverter with necessary changes; two controlled switches of the inverter bridge are replaced by diodes, one of the capacitors of impedance network is replaced by a diode and AC filter inductor is eliminated for the DC operation. A comparative analysis among the proposed converter and some of the high gain DC-DC converters is given in terms of voltage gain and number of elements. Steady-state behavior of the proposed converter is verified through PSIM based simulation results along with the scaled down laboratory prototype experimental results.

articleTitle: Development of System-On-Chip Based Digital Control for Power Converter Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Development of digital controller requires the control platform to achieve the desired performance. Implementation of the complex algorithm needs the high computation accuracy, faster and real-time calculations, monitoring and data logging. This paper discusses the different controller platform like DSCs, DSPs and FPGAs including their subunits required for the PCC. FPGA based unit is used to test the control component employed and then the final application specific processor can be designed for the same. Employing the high-end control platform also increases the cost as it is underutilized. In order to improve this DSCs can be used to develop the SoC for low and medium end applications.

articleTitle: Low Source Current Ripple Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper proposes a low source current ripple buck-boost converter which is feasible in point of load applications. This converter topology has reduced source current ripple which eliminates the need of filter damping network at the source side and reduces the EMI as well. The proposed converter's performance is examined in time-domain together with steady-state analysis. The buck and boost feature of the converter are explained along with design equations of L, C elements. State-space analysis is done to yield transfer functions which are the basis for controller design. A 15/36 V, 36 Watt prototype point of load converter is built to supply power at constant load voltage. A DC source of 24 V is used while a switching frequency of 100 kHz is adopted for the prototype converter operation both in simulation and experimentation. The results obtained from simulation and experiments are in line with the analytical predictions.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of High Step-Up Gain Multi-Phase Interleaved Coupled Inductor Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Interleaved Coupled Inductor Boost Converter (ICIBC) is widely used for high step-up gain and high power application. Interleaved coupled inductor high step-up gain converters reduce the ripple of the input current and improve the efficiency. In a distributed generation system, Voltage Mode Control (VMC) is normally applied for regulating output voltage. Designing VMC with a feedback controller requires a small signal model of multi-phase ICIBC. This higher-order converter encountered significant challenges while modelling. This paper derives a mathematical model of multi-phase ICIBC using state space averaging method. It also presents step by step PI controller design using the root locus technique for voltage loop control. Simulation study of voltage loop control of two-phase ICIBC under variable load condition is analysed to attain regulated output voltage in PSIM.

articleTitle: Quad-Active-Bridge DC-DC Converter based on-board Power Electronic Interface for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Driven by concerns of climate change and depletion of fossil fuels, there is an increasing trend to migrate to electric vehicles (EV) from conventional Internal Combustion Engines (ICE). Aided by the support of various governments, the era of all-electric-vehicles is becoming a reality. However, the commercialization of EV is hampered to some extent due to the drawbacks of EVs such as limited driving range, sluggish response and shorter operational life of on-board battery. A hybrid energy storage system (HESS), comprising a battery and ultra-capacitor (UC) can overcome some drawbacks of an EV with battery as the only energy storage. The power electronic architecture that integrates the HESS is one of the most important aspects to be considered in designing the drive-train of the EV. This paper uses a Quad-Active-Bridge (QAB) DC-DC converter as the on-board interface for the HESS. The system inherits several desirable features like high power density, soft-switching and higher efficiency from active-bridge topologies. The technical design of the proposed system along with structure of digital controller is included in this paper. Simulation and experimental results to substantiate the performance merit of the system are also included.

articleTitle: An Advanced Model Predictive Controller for Grid-Tied Four-Leg Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: An advanced Model Predictive Control (MPC) for three level diode clamped four leg Inverter is Introduced by exploiting its space vector representation in natural coordinates. The advanced MPC predicts reference inverter voltage (RIV) vector at every sampling instant to simplify the implementation of MPC. In this procedure, every switching state is isolated from each other by its optimal volume to control grid current. The optimal volume of the switching state is identified by predicting the RIV vector. The identification procedure employs the simple coordinate geometry concept. It does not require the calculation of the objective function. A generalized advanced MPC for any four leg grid-tied multilevel inverter is developed as well. Simulations are carried out for the advanced MPC. A detailed comparison with the conventional MPC is included. Preliminary experimental results of the advanced MPCC are also presented.

articleTitle: PLL-Less Compensation control for Single-Phase Grid Interfaced Wind Energy Generation System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work proposes a notch filter based load compensation technique for nonlinear load connected to a single phase grid integrated wind energy generation system (WEGS). It includes permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) coupled to a wind turbine with back to back connected two-level voltage source converters (VSC) with a common DC link. The purpose of grid connected VSC is to mitigate grid current harmonics and to improve the power factor. The generator side converter (GSC) serves the purpose of maximum power extraction from wind turbine and mitigates the harmonics in generator currents. A notch filter based control is designed for fundamental load current extraction. The notch filter does not require phase locked loop (PLL) for its operation, which reduces the system dependency on tuning of proportional integral (PI) controller and minimizes the computational burden. A feed-forward term for wind contribution is introduced for improving the dynamic response for change in wind speeds. The proposed system is developed in the laboratory and its behavior is tested under dynamic loading and changing wind speed conditions. The behavior of proposed system is found to be reasonable and grid current total harmonic distortion (THD) is found well within the IEEE 519 standard.

articleTitle: Constant Switching Frequency State Feedback Control of Cascaded H bridge Multilevel Inverter with Reduced Switches
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a constant switching frequency state feedback control of a cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter. The inverter topology consists of a number of full-bridge cells, each equipped with a transformer, connected in parallel to a single dc source. The turns ratio of one transformer is modified to 1: 2 which reduces the number of components required to generate an N-level waveform, thus decreasing the size and cost of the inverter. Level shifted multi-carrier sinusoidal pulse width modulation technique is modified for application to this topology such that each bridge generates a PWM output waveform. For closed loop operation of the inverter, state feedback control is applied to drive the inverter output to the desired operating point. The control law is derived using state space modelling of the inverter and is used as the modulating signal in PWM technique so as to generate a constant switching frequency closed loop operation of the inverter. The inverter operation is verified using PSCAD-EMTDC. Results are presented both for open loop and voltage controlled mode of operation. The working of the controller is verified with step changes in load, reference value and, dc-link voltage.

articleTitle: A Novel High Gain Soft-Switching Interleaved LCL Integrated Fly-back Step-up Converter without An Auxiliary Switch for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: An interleaved soft-switched integrated fly-back step up DC-DC converter topology with high voltage conversion ratio is proposed for the hybrid energy systems. Input current stress is minimized. Doubling of the ripple frequency due to interleaved operation will also reduce the size of the filter capacitor. Additional active clamp is not required in order to minimize the voltage stress on the main switches. Series resonance causing by leakage inductance of the both the coupled inductors with common capacitor (LCL Network) providing wide range of Zero Voltage Switching with the variations in duty ratio and also this LCL network efficiently recycling the energy stored in leakage inductance of both the coupled inductors to the output port. Zero Current Switching is obtained for the output diodes. This is achieved due to secondary leakage inductor of the coupled coils and the voltage quadrupler capacitors, there by reverse recovery problem of the diode is mitigated. The converter is designed at 1kW,100kHz.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring framework for Converter Transformers used in Marine Electric Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electrical and magnetic domain parameters for online condition monitoring of converter transformers used in marine power system is explored, where the traditional DGA and PD techniques are not much applicable. Current signal and leakage flux from transformer core and winding are studied, with an emulated inter-turn fault in a 10 kVA lab-scale converter transformer. It is expected that the presence of valve winding in converter transformer will pose a challenge, for condition monitoring as it has inherent harmonics. There is a need for an online monitoring technique which is simple, cost effective and rugged to diagnose the fault and raise an alarm on-board ship, as it may lack the right maintenance technician or a replacement transformer during the voyage. Method of emulating the inter-turn fault in transformer, experimental studies and the frequency domain results from electrical and magnetic sensors for condition monitoring are discussed.

articleTitle: Assimilation of Wind Plant to the Utility Grid by An Improved Active and Reactive Power Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel current control technique for the control of active and reactive power is presented in this paper so that the effective integration of the wind plant to the utility grid can be achieved. The proposed recurrent neural network (RNN) controls the amount of power to be transferred to grid side by maintaining the system stability. The RNN weights is updated through the Hebbian-LMS algorithm get quick tracking. The proposed controller is designed and analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink. RNN current controller is the best solution to control the power transfer to the grid side with improved quality and stability even under the system variations. Also, existing DC-DC converters are replaced with high gain DC-DC converters to achieve high voltage levels with better performance and is controlled by Kalman MPPT algorithm.

articleTitle: Field Experience on Effect of Power Electronic Component Failure in Excitation Circuit of a 5 MW Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Nowadays, brushless excitation systems are used in medium voltage synchronous motors. A brushless excitation system is coupled to the AC generator with its field circuit on the stator and the armature circuit on the rotor. The three phase output of the generator of the AC exciter is rectified using solid state rotating rectifiers. Brushless excitation systems provide high reliability by eliminating the use of collector rings, brushes and carbon dust, which greatly reduce maintenance, operational and inspection costs. Redundant rotating rectifiers with detection of diode failure while in operation, allows for more convenient operational interval. The field synchronizing and field voltage dissipation modules play a key role in the successful operation of this excitation module. This paper explains the effect of failure of these excitation modules and proposes a scheme for more reliable operation for the same.

articleTitle: Optimization of Capacitor for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Miniaturized version of Micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) based Piezoelectric (PZ) a.c. energy harvester is becoming a potential solution to power today's low power electronic systems. This a.c. electrical output energy needs to be converted into d.c. to power the systems. This conversion efficiency directly depends on the magnitude of flipping the voltage across the internal capacitance (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) of the PZ device during the zero crossing of the internal current source (i<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>(t)) of the PZ device. Recently, the synchronized switch harvesting on capacitance (SSHC) is becoming an efficient method of flipping the voltage across the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. The effectiveness of such circuits highly depends on the values of the parameters of the circuit primitives. For optimal flipping, the theoretical value of switching capacitance (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) of SSHC is equal to C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. However, considering the practical issues in implementation, the flipping efficiency increases with C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>. In this paper optimal value of the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> is obtained to increase the flipping efficiency. The circuit is implemented using 0.18 μm technology. The value of the Cr is considered as 25 nF. Using theoretical optimum value of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> as 25 nF, the improvement in the a.c. to d.c. conversion efficiency is 12.16% with respect to the normal FBR. The conversion efficiency increases to 14.86 % with C1 as 50 nF. This shows a direct improvement of the conversion efficiency by 2.7 %.

articleTitle: Control of Solar Power based Soft Switched Boost Converter for PMBLDC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with the design and analysis of zero voltage switching (ZVS) based quasi resonant step up converter (QRSUC) used in photovoltaic (PV) power based permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor for driving fan load of humidification plant. The solar power-based humidification plant for space cooling is an attractive solution to curtail load demands on grid supply system or to feed remotely located loads. An electronic commutation based PMBLDC motor control under variation in solar irradiation is used. The MATLAB based simulation environment is used to model the control of proposed QRSUC based PMBLDC drive and simulation results are shown for validating the proposed concept under variations in operating conditions.

Author Keywords: Humidification plant, Quasi Resonent Step-Up Converter

articleTitle: Emulation of Wind Turbine System using Vector Controlled Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Depleting fossil fuels and concerns about global warming have forced a paradigm shift towards renewable energy resources in meeting our energy requirements. Wind energy utilization has been growing at a rapid rate fuelling research and development in high power wind turbines. To advance research and education in wind energy conversion systems, a controlled test bed is necessary that does not depend on wind availability. In this paper, a control structure is proposed to emulate high power, large inertia wind turbines using low power, small inertia machines. Majority of the existing methods for wind turbine emulation employ DC or induction motors with torque compensation loop. However, it suffers from noise and instability issues. DC motors have several disadvantages compared to induction machines in terms of cost, maintenance, speed and ruggedness, even though their control is simple. Hence, in this paper, Squirrel Cage Induction Machine (SCIM) in speed controlled mode is employed for emulation. The performance of the control structure is demonstrated through an experiment involving step change in wind velocity, where the dynamics of a high inertia wind turbine system are emulated. Simulations and experiments are conducted on a 7.5 kW Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) driven by a 5.5 kW SCIM, emulating a wind turbine.

articleTitle: A new control strategy for single phase cascaded H bridge multilevel inverter in stationary reference frame with nonlinear loads
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified multiloop control strategy in stationary reference frame for the control of single phase multilevel converter in standalone mode. A new feedback method is proposed for the current control loop. The weighted sum of the filter inductor current and capacitor current is taken as the feedback to the inner current controller. Using this current measurement, a voltage control strategy using multiresonant voltage controllers is used to compensate for nonlinear loads. A cascaded H bridge multilevel converter is used for interfacing energy sources to load. Simulation and experimental results from a laboratory scale prototype is demonstrated to assess the performance of the suggested control scheme.

articleTitle: Influence of Maximum Current Control Strategy on Torque Ripple in BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Brushless dc motors are voltage source inverter (VSI) fed permanent magnet motors which are popularly known for their faster dynamics, high efficiency, and low maintenance. The dynamics of the motor is predominantly influenced by the type of controller employed in the control loop. Faster dynamics and precise control of BLDC motors is usually achieved by employing hysteresis current controllers. The current sensed either from the DC Link or from the phases of the motor is employed for the control. This paper brings out the effects of these current sensing strategies on torque ripple and switching frequency. It also proposes methods to eliminate the nonlinearities in computing Maximum of Phase Currents by employing micro-controllers.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Electric Vehicles using Vector Controlled Multiphase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the performance enhancement of an Electric vehicle on implementing Indirect Field Oriented Controlled (IFOC) Five-Phase Induction Motor Drive as its propulsion unit using MATLAB/SIMULINK. Engagement of multiphase induction motor in place of three-phase induction motor significantly improves the motor drive performance in terms of average torque, power and energy requirement during the EV drive cycles. Percentage improvement of energy with significant reduction in torque ripple towards vehicle dynamics is developed by the drive. Simulation analysis is carried out on the developed torque and effective speed tracking capability of the model under standard drive cycles. Energy requirement under standard drive cycles is calculated and the results are illustrated.

articleTitle: Grid-PV Array Fed Induction Motor Drive for Water Pumping
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with a PV array fed water pumping system operated by a mechanical sensorless induction motor drive. The recurrence of PV power outage causes the disturbance in water pumping. One possible solution is to use a utility grid as a backup source. The power is delivered by the grid in case the PV array is unable to meet the required power demand. A current multiplier approach is developed for unidirectional power flow control through a power factor improved boost converter. The utilization of reduced number of sensors makes the system cheap. The proposed system enables a consumer to get a rated quantity of water regardless of duration or the climatic condition. Simulated and test results justify the suitability of the system under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Single-Inductor Dual-Output Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper performance of Single-Inductor Dual-Output (SIDO) buck converter controlled by Model Predictive Control (MPC) is analyzed. The system considered in this paper is a dual output system. So, cross coupling affects the system performance. Performance of the plant is studied by implementing MPC algorithm and it is observed that effect of cross coupling is reduced due to inclusion of optimization algorithm in MPC. MPC involves primarily two step design procedure. First, SIDO DC-DC Buck converter is modeled using states space average technique for output prediction. Second step includes an optimization algorithm which obtain optimized duty ratio for reference tracking.

articleTitle: Impact of Hybrid Renewable Sources on the Transient Stability of Multi-machine Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method to improve the transient stability of a multi-machine power system integrated with hybrid renewable sources. The study aims at investigating and understanding the transient stability of the system with constant and varying power injection by doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind farm and solar photovoltaic (PV) farm. The controllers of the converters in DFIG and Solar PV system are modified in such a way that during fault period both the renewable sources allow maximum reactive power injection unlike during normal period. This coordinated reactive power support during fault causes improvement in the bus voltage magnitude and thereby enhance the overall system transient stability. Faults are considered in different load buses and stability is compared for the cases with and without the proposed controller. The study is carried out in WSCC 3-machine 9-bus system and the platform used for simulation is PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Partial Unfolding Scheme for Grid Feeding Transformerless PV Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Transformerless photovoltaic (PV) inverters are popularly used for grid feeding systems owing to their high efficiency, low weight and compact size. These inverters are expected to have high conversion efficiency and low earth leakage current over wide input voltage range. This paper proposes a method to improve the conversion efficiency, when the PV array maximum power point voltage becomes less than the grid peak voltage. This scheme reduces effective switching frequency of inverter, which results in less switching and recovery losses. The detailed operation of the proposed modulation and control scheme is explained. Estimated efficiency is also compared with the state of the art. In order to validate the operation, simulation studies are carried out using Matlab/Simulink environment and results are included.

articleTitle: Magnetic Equivalent Circuit for Surface-Mounted PM Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electric machine design optimisation requires tools that provide reliable information about machine parameters. Magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) technique is selected here for predicting machine performance. MEC is developed for a fractional slot, permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The model includes saturation, fringing effect in air gap and accounts for relative motion of the rotor. Even with saturation being incorporated, the adopted solution converges the model within few iterations. Performance quantities of the motor like flux density, induced EMF, flux linkage, inductance and cogging torque are evaluated. The results of MEC are validated with finite element analysis (FEA) and few with experiments.

articleTitle: Simulation of a 5-Pole Linear Induction Machine using Finite Element Method showing the Source Independence of the Peak-to-Peak Thrust Ripple
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, it has been shown that in a Linear Induction Machine (LIM), the thrust ripple that arises due to the magnetic asymmetry, does not depend on whether the machine is being fed from a current source or a voltage source. When a LIM is supplied from a balanced 3-phase voltage source, the LIM draws unbalanced currents from the supply due to the open magnetic circuit of the machine. This unbalance causes a ripple in the developed thrust. The thrust ripple increases with increase in speed of the LIM. However, when the LIM is being fed from a 3-phase balanced current source, there will be no unbalance in the line currents. This paper shows that even in such a scenario, there is no change in the amount of ripple in the developed thrust at any given speed. The thrust ripple is independent of how much current the LIM draws from the supply, how much terminal voltage is applied or the nature of the source from which the LIM is being supplied. This means that thrust ripple of a LIM is unique, and its variation depends only on the speed of the machine.

articleTitle: A Comparative Design Approach of a Novel Wide Angle Torque Motor for Pointing Mechanism for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Limited angle operation of an actuator is being envisaged with dc limited angle torque motor, a special type of brushless motor. This paper explains the design, analysis and realization of a Wide Angle Torque motor for spacecraft mechanism application in detail. Configuration study was carried out with four different types of brushless dc motors and a suitable Wide Angle Torque motor was selected based on the application need. Modelling and analysis of a bipolar brushless dc motor is carried out using finite element analysis and optimized to deliver flat torque for 180 deg. and commutation free region for 90 deg. The designed motor is realized and characterized.

articleTitle: Optimal Site and Size of DG with different Load Models using Cuckoo Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Optimal set up of Distributed Generation (DG) resource in a distribution system with different objectives is a crucial requirement in the deregulated power market environment. A multi-objective optimization approach considering both technical and economic benefits with practical load models needs to be analyzed. Therefore, in this paper active and reactive power loss minimization, voltage stability index (VSI) improvement, as well as DGs installation cost, are used to formulate the multi-objective function (MOF). Voltage dependent real and reactive power loads are modeled to have practical results. To find the optimal site and size of multiple DGs in a distribution network, a brood parasitic breeding behavior based meta-heuristic Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA) is implemented. To investigate the effect of five different types of load models, the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution network is considered as a test system. Change in optimal size and location of DG with different voltage dependent load models are examined. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology, a comparison is made with Particle Swarm optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Simulation results verify the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Three Winding Stator Interturn Fault on Induction Machine for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a transient model of an induction machine with a stator interturn fault in three windings of the machine with different percentages of shorted turns is analyzed for electric vehicle application. Stator fault is the most common and severe faults occurs in the motors. Analyzing the effects of a stator turn fault on the motor is a crucial feature in fault diagnosis of electric vehicles. This compels us to develop a model, which helps to analyze the behavior of the machine under stator fault conditions in any of the winding or on multiple windings. The percentage of turns shorted in the machine is varied and complete machine modeling with such a fault is performed in a stationary reference frame. The motivation of this paper is to predict the performance of an electric vehicle drivetrain under abnormal running conditions with a sudden stator fault. Moreover, the stator fault resistances in the three winding fault is also varied. This model helps to design a fault prediction and diagnosis system in electric vehicles to avoid sudden stalling during drive mode. The abnormal behavior in line currents, speed and torque of the induction machine under sudden fault conditions is simulated in MATLAB and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Inner Loop Stability of Peak Current Controlled Cuk and SEPIC Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In reported literature, generally, switch current is sensed to implement inner peak current programmed mode (PCPM) loop. However, two inductor and switch currents are the three possible inner loop variables in fourth order dc-dc converters like Cuk and SEPIC. This paper examines the stability of inner loop for these three different cases. Design of passives are purely done with the aim to restrict their ripple content. Inferences are made by studying the location of closed inner current loop transfer function poles. In course of analysis, it is found that mere selection of proper value of compensating ramp slope does not ensure the stability of PCPM. It is a necessary but not the sufficient condition. Ripple factors in inductor current selected for designing parameters play an important role in stability. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the derived findings.

articleTitle: Differential Mode Y-Source DC-DC Converter for Better Performance with Loosely Coupled Inductors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Magnetically coupled inductor based impedance source dc-dc boost converters are capable of producing high voltage boost with reduced components and low shoot-through duty ratios (STDR). A Y-source converter (YSC) is one of the prominent topologies in the family of magnetically coupled impedance networks, which offers the highest degree (three degrees) of freedom to the controller to maintain constant output voltage compared to the former magnetically coupled Z-source topologies. However, YSC requires tight coupling (nearly unity) among three coupled windings to generate high voltage boosting. But, the continuation of tight coupling is quite difficult in the design of offline YSC when it involves high switching frequency operations. The leakage inductances are common in the design of any magnetically coupled topologies under high operational frequencies. High voltage overshoots, voltage boost degradations are the consequences of the leakage inductance with loosely coupled inductors. This paper attempts to analyse the effect of leakage inductances mathematically with detailed circuit representation of coupled inductors. In addition, a differential mode Y-source converter (DYSC) is proposed which is derived from the former Y-source network by changing the winding orientation. The performance of the proposed DYSC is analyzed using Matlab/Simulations™ and also compared with YSC. The hardware results are presented to validate the theoretical simulations of both YSC and DYSC topologies.

articleTitle: PV Distributed-MPP Tracking: Total-Cross-Tied configuration of MICs to extract the Maximum Power under Partial Shading conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) central inverter architecture comprises of various PV module configurations. The PV module configurations are vulnerable to shading effects and cause mismatching power losses. To reduce the detrimental effect of shading and mismatching on energy production, Distributed-Maximum Power Point Tracking (D-MPPT) architecture has been proposed. In this architecture, an individual DC-DC converter is integrated to each PV module/sub-module or short-string of PV modules to extract the maximum power. This topology is referred to as Module-Integrated-Converter (MIC). In conventional D-MPPT architecture, the output terminals of the MICs are connected in series or parallel configuration only. In series configuration, because of cross-coupling effects, the operating points of MICs are deviated from the Maximum Power Point (MPP). In parallel configuration, the cross-coupling effects are not present. But, the limitations of parallel configuration are lower conversion efficiency, lower voltages and higher currents, two-stage voltage conversion and also the use of isolated converters. To overcome the limitations of conventional configurations, this research paper proposes the Total-Cross-Tied (T-C-T) configuration of MICs. The performance of the proposed configuration is compared with the conventional configurations under various partial shading conditions. The proposed configuration extracts the maximum power from each PV module/sub-module or short-strings by minimizing the cross-coupling effects.

articleTitle: Controller Gain Impact on Islanded dc Microgrid Stability with Constant Power Load
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: DC microgrid is gaining attention of researcher due to their higher efficiency, more reliability and easy integration with renewable sources. Along with all advantages, it also creates design challenges for the researcher. To address one of the challenge, in this paper a small-signal mathematical modeling of an islanded dc microgrid has been derived in closed-loop and the effect of controller gain on the microgrid stability has been studied for constant power load. The eigenvalue analysis has been carried out for the tuning of controller, which ensures the stable operation. An islanded dc microgrid is simulated using Matlab/Simulink and validated through analysis.

articleTitle: DFCE Based Control of Solar PV-Wind Energy System Interfaced to Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the control of single stage solar PV (Photovoltaic) array with variable speed WECS (Wind Energy Conversion System) using DFCE (Dual Fundamental Component Extraction) based control algorithm for power quality improvement of the distribution network. The variable speed WECS uses P&O (Perturb and Observer) based MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) algorithm for peak power extraction, and it is accomplished by a generator side VSC (Voltage Source Converter). However, the solar PV array maximum power is extracted using INC (Incremental Conductance) based MPPT algorithm through the grid side converter. The solar PV array and WECS, are feeding active power to AC mains at unity power factor through grid side VSC. The grid side VSC control approach is capable of compensating the load harmonics and maintaining the three phase grid currents balanced at variable solar and wind powers. The proposed control algorithm uses the fundamental load current, and voltage components for estimation of reference grid currents. This control algorithm has a self-tuning filter for accurate and fast fundamental component extraction. Tests results have demonstrated the satisfactory performance of proposed grid-tied PV-WECS on a developd prototype in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Dual-Input Dual-Output DC-DC Converter for DC Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative dual-input dual-output (DIDO-DC) DC-DC converter for the DC microgrid applications. The proposed converter is derived from the classic buck-boost DC-DC converter. The converter has four IGBTs, two inductors, two filter capacitors and three diodes to integrate two input sources and two loads. Using this converter topology, both the loads can be powered even when one of the input sources is not available. Compared to the conventional topologies, the proposed topology has fewer component counts and low voltage stresses which improve the converter efficiency. The output voltage expressions of the DIDO-DC converter are derived from the analytical waveforms for the buck-boost mode of operation. To verify the operation of the converter, the simulation studies have been carried out using PSCAD 4.5.1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software. The experimental prototype of the converter is fabricated and tested successfully in the laboratory. The measured experimental results are also presented in this paper. Finally, the performance comparison of the DIDO-DC converter with the conventional topologies is discussed.

articleTitle: Solar based Air Conditioner with BLDC Motor and Battery Backup
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes the designing of an air conditioner utilizing solar energy obtained from photovoltaic (PV) panels. In this proposed system maximum power is obtained from PV panel by the help of perturb & Observe (P&O) tracking algorithm. Duty cycle of buck-boost converter, which maintains the voltage at the output of the inverter to control the brushless DC (BLDC) motor to drive the compressor and blower is controlled by perturb and observe technique. Battery is connected to the system through a charge controller to increase the trustworthiness of the system. The proposed air conditioner is designed to obtain satisfactory system performance even under dynamic conditions. The performance and effectiveness of the system is evaluated and verified using simulation.

articleTitle: Impact of PLL on Harmonic Stability of Renewable Dominated Power System: Modeling and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For reliable operation of power system, the system should be stable not only in the fundamental domain but also in harmonic domain. Power electronic converters of renewable generators inject harmonics into the power systems. So, at higher renewable penetration levels, study of power system stability in harmonic domain i.e. harmonic stability is required. The Phase Locked Loop(PLL) is used for grid synchronization of renewable generators. PLL affects the dynamic behavior of power electronic converters in harmonic domain also. This paper analyzes the impact of PLL on the harmonic stability of renewable dominated power systems. A small signal state space model is developed for PLL in harmonic domain to analyze the behavior of PLL. The obtained state space model is a periodic Linear Time Varying (PLTV) system, making the state space model of the whole power systems also a PLTV system. As the obtained state matrix is periodic in nature, the concept of time varying eigen-values is employed to analyze the harmonic stability. The standard IEEE-39 bus system is modified to enable high renewable penetration level and the modified system is used to carryout the harmonic stability analysis. Impact of PLL parameters on harmonic stability is analyzed using the modified IEEE 39 Bus system. The impact of renewable penetration level on harmonic stability for given PLL parameters is also analyzed. It is observed that the PLL parameters and renewable penetration level have impact on the harmonic stability of power system.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction in Unsymmetrical Two Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, an approach for reducing the torque ripple in a two phase unsymmetrical induction motor is analyzed. A single phase induction motor is basically a two phase induction motor and generally, the windings on the stator are not identical. Hence, it is called unsymmetrical two phase induction motor. If an unsymmetrical motor is supplied by two phase balanced supply voltages then the ripples in the electromagnetic torque are unavoidable. However, if the supply voltages are made unbalance to counter the unbalance in the windings the torque ripple can be reduced. The mathematical model of the machine in stator attached reference frame is used to derive the torque expression in terms of stator currents. The torque expression consists of a constant term and a pulsating term. These terms used together unable finding the conditions on stator currents and hence stator voltages so that the ripples in the torque produced can be mitigated.

articleTitle: Pre-Filter Based Third Order Sinusoidal Signals Integrator Algorithm for Grid Tied PV System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The performance of a grid tied photovoltaic (PV) system with connected nonlinear loads at PSL (Point of shared link), depends on synchronization and compensation of the voltage signal. In this paper, the main aim is to improve the functions of a grid tied PV system feeding balanced and unbalanced nonlinear loads connected at PSL. The control of interfaced voltage source converter (VSC) of PV system, is based on extraction of in phase component of load currents by extracting of harmonic components using third order sinusoidal signal integrator (TOSSI) with interfacing filters. TOSSI based pre-filter improves dynamic response by increasing the selectivity of extracted fundamental load currents. The proposed control algorithm is developed and implemented first, using soft tools in MATLAB software and then validated through experimental results on a developed prototype in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Power Converter Based Impedance Emulation of Passive Loads for Anti-Islanding Tests
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A passive RLC load is essential for conducting anti-islanding tests of inverter based grid connected distributed generator (DG) systems. A variable load is desirable if the tests need to be carried out over a range of operating conditions and on multiple DG based inverters of different ratings. Use of a physical load results in increased cost and space requirements, particularly when the rating of the DG under test increases. This paper presents power converter based impedance emulation technique to actively implement such a parallel RLC load. The dynamic and steady-state response of the load are synthesized using closed loop control of the passive load emulation converter (PLEC), such that the terminal behaviour of the converter matches the passive RLC load characteristics closely. The proposed technique is verified using simulations and experiments that consist of proposed PLEC working in tandem with a current controlled $ 3\phi $ DG based inverter on a 5 kVA hardware prototype in laboratory.

articleTitle: Integration of Multiple Energy Storage Sections in Solar PV based HMGs using Multi-Input DAB
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For the hybrid microgrid (HMG) fed from solar photovoltaic (PV) system, single battery storage section could prove economical than using individual batteries. This in turn requires high power high efficiency dc-dc converters. This paper proposes an isolated multi-input dual active bridge (MIDAB) based dc-dc converter topology for integrating the multiple batteries section. It provides a high end power transfer along with the capability to distribute the power among different battery storage sections as per the MIDAB modulation indices. The converter has been tested for the configured hybrid DC/AC solar microgrid system capable of operating in both grid-connected and isolated modes. The power management strategy has been modified for efficient power transfer in different operating modes. A simulation model of the proposed MIDAB based solar PV microgrid system has been built on MATLAB to verify the proposed control strategy under various solar radiation level and load conditions.

articleTitle: Improved SVM-HCC with nearly constant switching frequency for electric spring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In present era to meet the increasing load demand there is integration of intermittent Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in the power sector. The penetration of these clean energy sources causes voltage instability, frequency fluctuation and propagation of harmonics in the system. This paper presents Electric Spring (ES) to suppress the harmonics caused by the non-linear critical load. Basically Electric Spring is a current controlled voltage source with Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) as a basic building block. To switch the inverter current controlled techniques are used. Therefore, this paper proposes Modified Space Vector based Hysteresis Current controller (SVM-HCC) for Electric Spring applications in smart grid to achieve constancy in switching frequency. The proposed technique capitalized on the combined advantages of both Space Vector Modulation (SVM) and Hysteresis Current Control (HCC) techniques. Simulation results are obtained using MATLAB environment are used to demonstrate the advantages of Modified Hysteresis Controller compared to Conventional Hysteresis Controller to achieve constancy switching frequency.

articleTitle: A Modified Buck-Boost Zero Voltage Switching Converter for Photo-voltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Modified buck boost converter with abridged ripple in the output voltage has been proposed. The converter is achieved from altering the existing two switch buck boost converter with zero voltage switching incorporated. The optimum selection of turn ON duration of altered two switch buck boost converter enables to operate in buck, boost, buck boost modes. The zero voltage switching (ZVS) is achieved by combing the auxiliary circuit with modified two switch buck boost converter. The proposed converter provides isolation between the ports of input and output, reduced switching voltage stress, reduced power loss with freedom of selecting gate signal and higher efficiency. The proposed converter performance has been validated in both in MATLAB/Simulink solver and digital controlled prototype model and the voltage control through ZVS is effectively validated.

articleTitle: Probabilistic optimal reactive power planning with wind generation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, an optimal probabilistic reactive power planning method considering uncertain loads and intermittent wind generation is proposed. The objective of the probabilistic planning strategy adopted is to maximize the annual profit of the utility in face of large grid penetration of uncertainty. To maximize the profit, a modified MPSOGSA optimization technique has been used. The performance of this developed technique has been compared with those obtained from GA, GSA and PSOGSA optimization methods. Extensive simulation studies on IEEE-118 bus systems show that the with the loads and wind uncertainty included, the optimal reactive power planning can be accomplished with modified MPSOGSA.

articleTitle: A Robust Power Control Scheme for a Dual-Input Single-Output converter with a Standalone Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A robust power control scheme for a standalone solar Photovoltaic system utilizing a dual-input single-output buck-boost(DISOBB) converter operating under deficit solar PV power proposed. A battery energy storage is used to supplement the insufficient solar PV power to satisfy the requirements of the dc load. This is achieved by integrating MPPT tracking to extract maximum power from solar PV with voltage regulation of the dc load by modulating power flow from the energy sources to the dc load in a time shared manner. A versatile switching and power flow control scheme has been explained in detail. A state-space average is developed and dynamic characteristic of the converter is analyzed. The simulated dynamic response of the system to the variations in solar PV temperature, solar insolation and dc load are presented. A hardware prototype of the system is designed and implemented which validates the working of the proposed dynamic power control scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamically Converging Binary Search for PV-MPPT
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new dynamic and converging binary search algorithm (DC-BSA) based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method for a Photovoltaic (PV) system. The DC-BSA drives the controller to reach the operating point towards MPP quickly without involving complex calculations. It also enables the convergence to the MPP avoiding large oscillations of the converter in a shorter time. The obtained results demonstrate the enhanced performance of systems both in the transient and steady-state conditions with proposed algorithm when compared with the Perturb and Observation (P&O) MPPT technique. The analysis behind the theory and design of the algorithm is presented in detail. The results are demonstrated both. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through simulations on MATLAB/Simulink and experimental investigations.

articleTitle: Control of SCIG Based Distributed Power Generation Scheme Supplying Nonlinear and Unbalanced Load
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The proposed work has considered, developed, and implemented a combined control to handle squirrel cage induction generator (SCIG) fed to stand-alone nonlinear and unbalance load. The novelty of the proposed work is implemented successfully with transition from linear load to nonlinear and unbalance load. The main objective is to eliminate the harmonic component during nonlinear loading and to remove the negative sequence component of the unbalance load current. To improve the voltage quality, a control scheme, including filter parameter, has been implemented in this work for the load side converter. Further, the three-stage control technique is used for machine side converter to keep the dc link voltage fixed throughout the operating conditions. The harmonic mitigation and maintenance of output load voltage and frequency are achieved with the control of load side converter. The simulation results have been presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed controllers.

articleTitle: Power Management of Multi-level Renewable-Grid Integrated Hybrid Energy Harvesting System using Model Predictive Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the model predictive control approach to optimize the operation of hybrid microgrid system which contain hybrid energy harvesting and storage (HEHS) devices and bidirectional 3-Level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) based 3-Phase Voltage Source Converter (VSC). The intermittent nature of renewable energy sources has direct effect over the health of the connected microgrid system. Hence the essential salient feature needed for hybrid microgrid is to encounter the discrete nature of loading conditions. Which arises the need of that system which can deal with such kind of practical problems in the microgrid system. This work revisits and utilizes the key elements of Model Predictive Control (MPC) to achieve the voltage regulation in the DC link of AC/DC microgrid, reduction in grid harmonics and managing the power for the whole system. Along with this the given topology is optimally utilizing the DC link split capacitors by maintaining the same voltage level on them. Besides, the performance of MPC based grid connected HEHS system with 3-Level neutral point clamped converter topology is demonstrated via simulation in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Design of Backstepping Controller for a Three-phase Shunt Active Filter Interfacing Solar Photovoltaic System to Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a controller for a three-phase four-leg shunt active power filter (SAPF), interfacing solar photovoltaic system to distribution grid. The controller consists of a non-linear, robust dc-link voltage control loop based on backstepping algorithm. It also consists of a current harmonic mitigation loop based on dual self tuning filter instantaneous power theory (DSTF-pq theory). The limitations of conventional pq theory based current harmonic mitigation controller are addressed in this paper by employing self tuning filters (STF) to extract the fundamental components of load currents and grid voltages. The effectiveness of the algorithm under steady state and dynamic conditions are comprehensively studied and evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed controller is implemented in XC7a35t-cpg236-1 FPGA. The performance of the controller is tested and verified on a laboratory prototype of shunt active power filter.

articleTitle: A Double Bootstrap Gate Driving Scheme for HERIC Topology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Highly Efficient Reliable Inverter Concept (HERIC) inverter is a popular choice in transformerless solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. It comprises four 'high-side' (not connected to DC side ground directly) and two 'low-side' (connected to DC side ground directly) semiconductor switches. Pulse transformers or opto-coupler circuits when used to drive the high-side switches increase the size and cost of the driving circuit. In this paper, a double-bootstrap gate driving scheme for high-side switches is proposed and investigated. The scheme, which uses easily available high-side driver ICs, results in a cost-effective and simple driving scheme. The operation of proposed scheme is established using both simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A 1-phase Static VAr Compensator with Low Current THD and Wide Control Range
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A 1-phase Static VAr Compensator (SVC) topology is proposed using a tapped Thyristor Controlled Reactor (TCR) and a third harmonic tuned filter. The TCR is controlled by firing angle delay over a limited range initially and its tapping is changed to create operation using different equivalent value of effective reactance, such that the amount of harmonics generated is limited. The third harmonic filter attenuates the corresponding harmonics to low magnitude and also presents a capacitive reactance at the fundamental frequency for VAr compensation. Such an arrangement prevents the third harmonics from entering into the supply system while some major characteristic harmonics are kept limited, along with control of VAr through the TCR. Thus, without using any additional complex set of individual harmonic filters, or additional capacitor bank, this scheme enables reactive power control with a low current THD over a reasonable range of control, meeting requisite harmonics standards. Simplicity in construction and operational requirements of the proposed topology makes it a viable and cost effective solution. Its modeling, analysis and performance assessment are presented. Simulation and experimental results support the theoretical proposition.

articleTitle: Wavelet Modulated Inverter for WECS using Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a better control techniques known as wavelet modulation is proposed at the inverter side of wind energy conversion system. Permanent magnet synchronous generator is one of the generator used for integration of wind energy into power electronic topologies due to its simple construction & it provide direct coupling & number of poles can be change easily. A back to back converter topology is the most commonly used one, consist of rectifier on rotor side and inverter on grid side. Several modulation techniques are there for the control of inverter connected to load side in a wind energy conversion system. Switching pulses for inverter is generated using dSPACE1104 controller. The overall system is modelled and performance is verified in MATLAB Simulink & in hardware and obtained Low harmonic content and magnitude of fundamental component is high as compared to conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Frequency Adaptive Circle Tracing Observer-Based Control Algorithm for Grid-Connected SECS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The frequency adaptive circle tracing observer based control strategy is proposed for power quality (PQ) improvement of the grid tied solar energy conversion system (SECS). The adaptive observer based control scheme has multi-functionalities such as harmonics compensation, unity power factor (UPF), grid currents balancing. The sliding mode control is used to extract maximum power in SECS under varying atmospheric conditions. The adaptive DC link voltage based approach is used to regulate the DC link voltage of voltage source converter (VSC), which reduces the tripping probability and losses of the converter under weak grid conditions. The optimization based approach is opted for optimal tuning of proportional integral (PI) regulator of the DC link voltage. Simulation results are demonstrated for various operating scenarios such as loads currents imbalancing, variation of common coupling point (CCP) voltages. Test results demonstrate the satisfactory performance of the system under various dynamic cases such as grid currents balancing, distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) to SECS mode, SECS to DSTATCOM mode. The THDs of the grid currents are obtained within the IEEE-519 and 1564 standards.

Author Keywords: MPPT and Solar energy conversion system

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a General Purpose Device Characterization Setup
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Semiconductor switches of distinct underlying device technologies but with identical ratings are commercially available from a range of manufacturers. Selection of appropriate device for a given power conversion application is critical for meeting the trade-off between cost and performance objectives. This paper discusses the design of a PCB based general purpose discrete device characterization setup using which comparative study of switching and short-circuit behavior of TO-247 devices is performed at room and elevated case temperatures in the range from 120° C to 160° C . The design ensures that the test fixture safely handles the abnormal levels of current stress occurring in the event of a catastrophic device failure. Experimental studies conducted on 1200V, 40A silicon (Si) and 1200V, 50A silicon carbide (SiC) devices from varied manufacturers verify the performance of the characterization setup. The distinctions in their respective switching behavior at nominal and fault conditions, along with the deviations in their characteristics observed at elevated operating temperatures are reported in this work.

articleTitle: Improved Pulse-Width Modulation Technique for 11-level Series-Parallel Switched Hybrid Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, improved Pulse-Width Modulation technique for an 11-level series-parallel switched Hybrid Inverter is presented. The series-parallel switching of the inverter bridge reduces the switching devices used for the same output voltage level as compared to traditional topologies. The hybrid modulation technique used is further separated as continuous and discontinuous. Results of both the modulation techniques are compared on the basis of their harmonic performance, which is measured in terms of total harmonic distortion and weighted total harmonic distortion. Discontinuous hybrid modulation is proved to be harmonically superior to its continuous counterpart. The validity of the proposed scheme is verified through simulated and experimental results.

articleTitle: Sensorless Double-Inverter fed Wound Rotor Induction Motor Drive with Reduced Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the sensorless vector control strategy for Double Inverter fed Wound Rotor Induction Motor (DI-WRIM) drive with reduced current sensors. This strategy involves two current controllers on the stator side to control the stator currents and a V/F controller on the rotor side to control the rotor supply frequency. The control algorithm requires reduced number of current sensors i.e., the currents of the side on which vector control is employed are only sensed, instead of both the stator and rotor currents. The simulation and the experimental results from a 3 kW WRIM drive are presented to validate the control algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of Feedback Linearizing Model Predictive Controllers for Grid-Connected Systems with Multiple Photovoltaic Units
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents an feedback linearizing model predictive control scheme to design controllers for grid-connected systems with multiple photovoltaic (PV) units. The controllers are designed based on the generalized dynamical models of grid-connected systems with multiple PV units. The feedback linearization technique is applied to linearize the whole system which decouples the dynamical models of multiple PV units. The dynamic interactions among different PV units are considered as noises which are also decoupled through the proposed feedback linearization scheme. This decoupling allows to design linear controllers in a decentralized way for individual PV units. In this paper, a receding horizon-based model predictive scheme is employed to design linear controllers for feedback linearized PV units. The performance of the proposed scheme is evaluated on an IEEE test system under different operating conditions and compared with an existing PI controller in terms of maintaining unity power factor operation. Simulation results clearly show that the proposed controller performs in a much better way as compared to the PI controller.

articleTitle: Stator Flux Based Model Reference Adaptive Observers for Rotor Position and Speed Estimation in Doubly-Fed Induction Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Sensorless estimation of speed is preferred for Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) used in wind energy conversion systems, in view of cost, maintenance, cabling and reliability issues. This paper proposes two stator flux based Model Reference Adaptive Observers (MRAO) for rotor position and speed estimation in doubly-fed induction machines. The cross product of reference and estimated stator flux linkage vectors is fed as controller input in the existing method, thereby making the observer model non-linear. The first proposed method, which is based on notch filtering, offers a performance comparable to that of the existing method, while reducing the number of voltage and current sensors required. The second method linearizes the observer model, leading to superior dynamic performance over the existing methods. This also simplifies the design of the controller. Simulations and experiments are performed on a 10 HP DFIG coupled to a Squirrel Cage Induction Motor (SCIM).

articleTitle: A Novel Three Phase Transformerless Inverter with Negative Grounding for PV Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Three phase transformerless inverters are quite popular due to its high efficiency and compact structure. However, removal of the isolation transformer can lead to varying common mode voltage across the PV parasitic capacitance. This leads to the flow of a large common mode leakage current which compromises the safety of the inverter. One method to tackle this issue is applying only those vectors wherein the common mode voltage remains constant. However, this reduces the inverter modulation index and leads to poor dc link utilization. In this paper, a novel three phase transformerless inverter is presented wherein the leakage current is directly eliminated by grounding the PV negative terminal. Moreover, the proposed topology facilitates the application of all the active vectors thereby improving the dc link utilization. The proposed topology employs stored energy modulation (SEM) thereby reducing the interlinking capacitor size. The proposed topology is analyzed in detail and its control is discussed. Simulations of the proposed inverter confirm the feasibility and good performance of the inverter.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Control for Synchronous Generator Based Wind-PV-Battery Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A new topology of microgrid comprising of a wind turbine driven synchronous generator (SG) and solar photovoltaic (PV) with a battery as an energy storage (ES) for reliable renewable energy harvesting is proposed in this work. The stochastic behavior of the inputs for proposed system, is agitated by the nonlinear time dependent parameters such as variable wind speed and changing solar insolation. The speed variations are absorbed using back to back interfaced voltage source converters (VSCs) namely synchronous generator side VSC (SGVSC) and load side VSC (LSVSC) with a common DC link where a double stage solar PV array with ES is tied directly. The SGVSC uses vector control (VC) for speed control of SG and maintains unity power factor (UPF) at the stator terminals. The hybrid fuzzy precompensated (HFP) proportional integral (PI) controller is used as the speed controller. The battery with LSVSC, absorbs the changes in the load and regulates the DC link voltage. A prototype is developed and tested under different conditions of sudden disconnection of load, wind velocity variations as well as under varying solar PV insolation. Test results validate the efficient functioning of the control algorithms along with keeping the system performance intact under the imposed changes.

articleTitle: A modular multilevel traction converter configuration with reduced conversion stage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a traction converter configuration based on modular multilevel converter and a medium frequency step-down transformer. The main objectives are to reduce the number of conversion stages and to minimise the dv/dt on the transformer windings. The control of the converter configuration is such that it can be applied for a traction system with a transformer having multiple secondary windings for driving multiple traction motors.
