The capacitor emulation technique is used to block the flow of DC current in the transformer windings in order to prevent saturation of the transformer. In this work, a simplified mathematical model of a multiple secondary winding transformer is presented in order to develop the controller for driving multiple traction motor drives.

articleTitle: Predictive Optimal Switching Vector Controller based Microgrid Enabling Switching Frequency Constraint
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study proposes predictive optimal switching vector controller to generate optimal switching sequences to voltage-controlled inverters in islanded microgrid systems. The conventional pulse width modulation controllers use output voltage and current with inner and outer current loops, thereby demanding the PI (Proportional Integral) regulators and PWM modulators. They are associated with finite dynamic response transient time by PI controllers and necessitate rigorous tuning for practical implementation purposes. To complement this problem, voltage and current predictive optimal switching vector control is proposed here, which completely eliminates the PID regulators, PWM modulators and synchronous co-ordinate transformations. It uses the model of the system to predict behavior of output voltages for each sampling instant. A minimization function is then used to select the switching state for the next inverter switching instant, while limiting the over-currents caused in the inverter. A switching frequency constraint is proposed to reduce the switching losses of the inverter. The proposed control strategy is verified through simulations and is experimentally validated on a prototype of microgrid system built in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Design of Demand Response based Load Management Solutions for a University Campus
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Demand Response (DR) is drawing the attention of the power system operators due to the increasing electricity demand and limited generation capacity to meet the growing demand. Traditionally, DR involved large industrial and commercial consumers only; but now due to the advancement in technology, it's deployment in small residential, commercial and educational sectors is also being considered. Moreover, the rural population would also get connected under `Power to All' program by government of India. Energy released due to DR action could be used to meet this mission to great extent. In this paper, DR program is designed and studied for a University Campus. A MATLAB/Simulink model of large loads like air conditioners, geysers, etc. has been considered to provide DR action. A new sub-model incorporating a thermostat that uses Real-time Pricing (RTP) of electricity to control the temperature setting of the air conditioner has been proposed in this paper. Results show that DR is useful in reducing the peak demand as well as the overall energy consumption.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Observers Based Wind Speed Computation Method in Wind Energy Conversion Systems Control Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Nacelle-top mounted anemometer gives wind velocity information pertaining to the surroundings of nacelle and this point wind velocity measurement may or may not be same as effective wind velocity which strikes the wind turbine rotor blades. In this paper, a new method for the computation of wind speed is proposed to avoid the presence of mechanical sensors like anemometer and speed encoders in the wind turbine control systems. Suitable sliding mode observers designed for the estimation of turbine rotor speed and aerodynamic torque. Effective wind velocity is computed by inverting the turbine's aerodynamic model after estimating the turbine torque and its rotor speed. Design criterion and inequality constraints are discussed in detail while satisfying the Lyapunov inequality condition. The simulation studies confirm that the computed wind speed under variable wind flow conditions is converging with true wind speed. This proposed method can be used for maximum power extraction and various control algorithms' implementations as well in wind energy conversion systems control applications.

articleTitle: A DC-DC Synchronous Buck Regulator with Mode Changing Control Strategy for Low Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This work presents a novel mode changing control strategy for enhancing the overall performance of low voltage DC-DC Synchronous Buck switching regulators for portable applications. Hysteretic mode control with Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) is employed in the light load range to optimize the switching and conduction losses and also, to regulate the inductor current ripple and hence the switching frequency. In the high load range, conventional voltage mode control is implemented to maintain high conversion efficiency. The converter can flexibly switch between the two modes based on the load current to achieve higher efficiency over a broad range of load current.

articleTitle: Thermal Loading of Multi-Megawatt Medium-Voltage Power Converters Serving to Variable Speed Large Pumped Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In recent era, large rated doubly fed induction machines (DFIM) are being preferred for variable speed pumped storage power plant (PSPP), due to its high round trip efficiency and high power discharge. To operate the large rated DFIM under variable speed operation, parallel connected back-to-back (BTB) power converters are employed in rotor excitation circuit. The semiconductor devices associated with the rotor excitation circuit are considered as the most vulnerable components in large hydrogenerating systems due to its thermomechanical fatigue stress. Especially, the major failure in the BTB converters are influenced by the thermal stress across the power semiconductor devices. In order to increase the BTB converter reliability, thermal stress on power semiconductor devices must be within the acceptable limits. With respect to this prime aim, this paper implements an active thermal control based on discontinuous pulse width modulation (DPWM) technique for multi-megawatt BTB power converters serving to a variable speed PSPP (4×250 MW DFIM, to be commissioned in Tehri dam, India). The implemented active thermal controller regulates the temperature fluctuation across power semiconductor devices with respect to varying speed (active power) conditions. The efficacy of the designed active thermal control is implemented and analyzed for real-time 250 MW DFIM with 5-channel 25 MW power converters in Matlab/PLECS environment.

Author Keywords: variable speed pumped storage power plant (VSPSPP)

articleTitle: A Three Phase Isolated Buck-boost Derived PFC Converter with a Novel Clamping Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a three phase isolated buck-boost derived power factor corrected (PFC) converter with a novel clamping circuit to limit the voltage spikes across the switches is proposed. The converter is operated in Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM) to achieve PFC at AC mains, thus the input current shaping circuit can be eliminated. It requires only one simple voltage control loop to regulate the output voltage, hence only one output voltage sensor. This makes the system cost effective, more reliable and robust. By using the proposed clamping circuit, the transformers leakage inductance energy is successfully captured in a clamping capacitor, and thereby it is fed to the load through a forward converter to improve the efficiency of the converter. The converter steady state operation and detailed design calculations are presented. The converter and its design is validated through the simulation and the experimental results.

articleTitle: Effect of Wear and Tear Bearing Fault in Induction Motor Drives Using FEM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Induction motors (IM) plays a critical role in many industrial applications. Though reliable IM are subjected to stator, rotor, bearing and miscellaneous faults. Among all the faults, bearing fault nearly accounts to 40% in IM. In inverter fed IM, bearings are subjected to severe stress due to switching of power converter devices which will cause more wearing away and degrade the performance of the bearing. Wear and tear is one of the common causes of faults in bearings and occurs due to lack of maintenance and poor handling which in turn will affect the friction co efficient of bearings. In this paper an analysis on bearing fault due to wear and tear in induction motor drive is realized using Finite Element Method (FEM). The effect of wear and tear of bearings in IM is incorporated in FEM by raising the friction coefficient of the rotor shaft. Several electromagnetic field quantities like flux line & flux density distribution over IM, air gap flux density radial component and its spatial FFT spectrum for various bearing friction coefficients are analysed in IM. The spatial FFT spectrum shows that the magnitude of fundamental element of air gap flux density radial component is decreased and magnitudes around 100 mm radial distance is increased depends on the intensity of wear and tear fault.

articleTitle: Multi-Party Energy Management of Microgrid with Heat and Electricity Coupled Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Combined heat and power (CHP) based Microgrids (MG) are quite popular. They can generate electricity based on electric or thermal demand. A framework of multi-party energy management is proposed in this paper with heat and electricity demand for the CHP-MG. Paper also delves on energy management of MG provided by CHP and photovoltaic (PV) prosumers. A model of Microgrid Operator (MGO) is developed to determine the operational profit of CHP system where MGO acts as a leader and prosumers are the followers. The main objective of MGO is economic operation of MG or to minimize the net cost of generation from Distributed energy resources and purchasing energy from the grid. It is established by simulation that the CHP system operating in hybrid mode by selecting following electric load (FEL) mode and following thermal load (FTL) mode dynamically the most economic operation of CHP is achieved. A dealing process between MGO and prosumers is also modeled. Lastly, a case study with CHP-MG and 6 building users are presented to verify the effectiveness of the model and to show the economic benefit of having the MGO along with the prosumers in a MG.

articleTitle: Non-Saliency of Interior Permanent Magnet Hybrid Excitation Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: It is a general perception that the interior permanent magnet machines will have different values of inductances along d-axis and q-axis and hence they are salient pole machines. Though it is true in most of the cases, some interior permanent magnet machines may turn out to be non-salient pole machines. Hence an accurate modeling of magnetic equivalent circuit is very much required in order to estimate the inductance values along d-axis and q-axis. A hybrid excitation machine with an interior configuration of permanent magnets and field winding is proposed in the literature. Though it appears to be a salient pole machine from rotor configuration view point, the actual analytical inductance analysis on this machine proves that it is a non-salient pole machine. A simpler analytical approach is carried out through approximate linear magnetic equivalent circuit. The analytical analysis is validated with analysis carried out through FEM software.

articleTitle: e-Battery for Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of electronic battery (e-Battery) for energy storage systems. The proposed e-Battery is a combination of ultra capacitor bank and power electronic converters. This paper looks at issues related to chemical batteries and proposes the concept of an e-Battery. The proposed e-Battery overcomes many of the drawbacks of a conventional chemical battery. The control strategy developed for the closed loop operation of the proposed e-Battery is also presented in this paper. The performance of the proposed e-Battery is verified through detailed time domain simulation in PSCAD/EMTDC. A hardware prototype is built to validate the performance of the proposed e-Battery experimentally.

articleTitle: Integrated power converters for innovative wind turbine generators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Integrated power converters that consist of induction generators and electronic units, are described. They are perspective for autonomous application, wind turbines in particular. Squirrel-cage induction generator has innovative compact winding with construction features. Windings with irregular cross-section conductors are brand new approach of machine’s design and they open possibilities for further improvement of electric machines. New construction of stator winding defines new methods of machine design. Resistance and end-winding leakage calculation is explained, the same as efficiency improvement. Reducing of size and mass of the induction machine is strongly relevant for small renewable energy installations and electric vehicles. Reduced overhang deviation allows to place electronic control units within the machine housing. Operation principle of electronic units is described. Direction of further researches in innovative compact induction generators is pointed.

articleTitle: Improved Power Quality of Sensorless Speed Controlled PMBLDC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a position sensorless speed control mechanism for a three phase permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor drive suitable to work in complete speed range. The indices of power quality such as power factor, crest factor, total harmonic distortion of the source current are maintained within standard limit of IEEE 519-2014 by improved power quality converter. The system is simulated using SIMULINK/MATLAB and analysed under variable speed and load conditions for the fan type load profile.

articleTitle: Generation of Switching Pulses for Three-Phase Switched Boost Inverter using Space Vector Modulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The switched boost inverter (SBI) has several advantages compared to classical voltage source inverter (VSI) such as satisfying both dc and ac load demands simultaneously, a wide range of output ac voltage, the capability to allow shoot-through, superior electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise immunity etc. However, the peak fundamental ac output voltage is limited in the techniques available in the literature. The conventional space vector modulation (SVM) can produce more peak fundamental output ac voltage compared to sine-triangle pulse width modulation (PWM) in classical VSI. In this paper, a switching pulses generation technique using SVM based approach for the three-phase SBI has been presented. The conventional SVM has been modified by the addition of a new set of space vectors named as `Shoot-through Vectors'. The Texas Instruments digital signal processor (DSP) TMS320F28335 has been utilized to generate the switching pulses. The space vector modulated three-phase SBI, with a dc load and three-phase balanced ac load, has been verified using an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: A New Brushless Synchronous Generator for DC Micro-grid Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Brushless generators are preferred for systems where safety is a major concern or for systems where maintenance becomes a key issue. Brushless synchronous generator proves to be a potential candidate in such cases. This work reports the development of a new brushless generation system applicable to HVDC grid or for medium voltage dc micro-grid. Here, two synchronous machines are placed on the same magnetic core in a cascaded manner and are wound for different pole configurations to exhibit magnetic decoupling. A control algorithm has been developed in order to regulate output voltage. Passive tuned filters are deployed to improve the current quality. Simulation results obtained from MATLAB/Simulink and experimental results from a fabricated laboratory prototype have been presented. Both simulation and experimental results reveal the effectiveness of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Zero Current Switching of CFSI using Auxiliary Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High gain inverters such as Z-source inverter (ZSI) and quasi-ZSI are gaining popularity in the applications of renewable energy sources due to limited DC voltage. Current-fed Switched Inverter (CFSI) is a derivative of ZSI, which has similar gain characteristic as ZSI and q-ZSI but with lesser components. However, in medium power applications, the boost stage of CFSI draws higher current, which increases the switching losses of the devices and lowers the overall efficiency. In this paper, by modifying the conventional CFSI, devices in the boost stage are switched under Zero Current Switching (ZCS) condition to reduce the switching losses. This paper discusses the operating principle and modes of operation of the proposed converter in detail. A lab prototype of proposed converter is built to validate the theoretical analysis. The efficiency of the proposed converter is enhanced by 2 % (at 450 W load) in comparison to conventional CFSI.

articleTitle: Comparison of Empirical Mode Decomposition and Wavelet Transform for Power Quality Assessment in FPGA
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper focused on the execution of a new field-programmable gate array (FPGA) based method for a signal processing algorithm to detect power quality disturbance in real-time for a grid-connected PV system. The real-time implementation of a signal processing algorithm to detect disturbances is still under the premature stage. To demonstrate the grid and distribution generation disturbances scenario in real-time, a PV connected with the emulated grid is taken into consideration for experiment analysis, which is capable to replicate the grid's behavior under normal operating conditions. Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Hilbert transform (HT) are a novel signal analysis technique which decomposes the signals into a different frequency component and extract hidden features of the signal to detect the disturbances. In the noisy scenario, DWT performance is deteriorated compared to EMD. Hilbert transform is applied to 1st IMF of EMD to gain instantaneous amplitude and phase of the signal.

articleTitle: Effective power sharing between Solar Refrigerator and DC Micro Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a control algorithm to effectively share the solar energy as a source of power between standalone solar refrigeration system and local DC grid benefiting the unelectrified villages in India. A single stage power conversion is used to feed the BLDC motor compressor (reciprocating) for the cold storage chamber (detachable). The power demanded by BLDC system is supplied completely from PV source. The cold storage chamber which uses Phase Changing Material (PCM) absorbs and accumulates the required energy by altering its phase and releases the energy during power interrupts or night time hence no battery backup is required. To extract the maximum power from the solar PV array an Incremental Conductance Maximum Power Point Tracking (IC MPPT) is used. The proposed control algorithm uses MPPT voltage reference itself to transfer the excess power to the DC grid without additional effort. The proposed system is evaluated by the simulation results obtained using MATLAB Simulink model.

Author Keywords: Incremental Conductance Maximum power point tracking (IC MPPT)

articleTitle: Effect of q-axis Inductance on the Design of an Industrial Inset Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive with Restricted DC bus Voltage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Inset PMSMs are widely used for critical high power applications demanding mechanical stability for high speed operations and simple constructional features. Even though the value of q-axis inductance differ from that of d-axis, the reluctance torque that can be extracted is minimal if the saliency is small, restricting the torque capability. However, the q-axis inductance plays a major role in the design of inset PMSMs for critical applications with a limited DC bus voltage. There may be variation in q-axis inductance of the manufactured machine from the designed value due to machine non-linearities and manufacturing tolerances, restricting the maximum torque capability at a desired speed. In this paper, a design guideline for selecting q-axis current rating and flux per pole of a machine considering variations of q-axis inductance and DC bus voltage fluctuation is presented. The effect of q-axis inductance variation on the operating point of an inset PMSM is analysed in detail.

articleTitle: Simplified Adaline based control of Shunt Active Power Filter with reduced sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Performance of Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) depends on the effectiveness of the reference current generation technique, which senses the voltages and currents of the system. Detection of voltage and current is done with the help of sensors. Failure due to faults in these sensors causes SAPF to aggravate power quality problems instead of compensating it. Therefore, sensorless and fault tolerant control of SAPF is a very attractive solution for its robust operation. This paper presents a simple modification in existing ADALINE based conventional control strategy which only requires source current and DC voltage measurement, thus eliminating load current, source voltage and filter current measurement and hence reducing the number of sensors involved. MATLAB/ Simulink results under different conditions are shown to validate the proposed work.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Renewable Energy Integration in Tamil Nadu Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: India has planned to add significant capacity in renewable space and this would be largely added in wind and solar rich states. Amongst all the states, Tamil Nadu (TN) is expected to have highest renewable capacity by 2022. This paper aims at assessing the operating philosophy of the TN state grid in 2022 due to planned renewable energy (RE) integration. The load-generation balance of TN power system has been analyzed for various operating scenarios. A reserve margin of about 15% on the net load basis (difference between actual demand and potential RE generation) is expected to be maintained to accommodate solar, wind and load variations. The study explores options to compute the curtailment of combined RE resources and suggest operating practices that TN can adopt to maximize RE generation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Energy Management on Smart Micro Grid along with Generation Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with the investigation of generation side management along with Dynamic Energy Management System (DEMS), which includes energy storage management and load management. The generation side management is accomplished with a governor control system on a hydro power plant and it is dynamically varied to handle the adverse conditions of frequency when operated in islanded mode. The main objective of this work is to enhance the operation of DEMS on an islanded Smart Micro Grid (SMG) by facilitating the hydropower plant with a governor control in turn investigate the operation of energy storage modules and also to inspect the different Demand Response Programs (DRP) when load management (LM) is performed.

articleTitle: Carrier-based hysteresis controlled constant switching frequency strategy for three-level inverter based DSTATCOM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes the constant switching frequency current control technique using carrier-based hysteresis modulation, for three-level inverter based Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM). The proposed scheme ensures constant and reduced switching frequency operation of three-level voltage source inverter (VSI). The analytical expressions are developed to select the proper carrier frequency range during positive, negative and zero-voltage states and design criteria is derived to avoid multiple and below crossings in the inverter switching dynamics. The proposed scheme is compared with the conventional three-level hysteresis current control and its improved performance in terms of bandwidth, Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and switching frequency is presented. Furthermore, the proposed strategy is applied for DSTATCOM applications to achieve load compensation at constant switching frequency. The detailed simulation Using MATLAB environment and experimental studies are presented to explore the suggested scheme.

articleTitle: A Buck-Boost Common-Mode Transformerless Inverter for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel common mode transformerless grid feeding topology with buck and boost operation from dc-link. This enables wide maximum power point tracking capability and yields higher energy. The novelty lies in coupling two switch buck-boost converter with four switch inverter such that a constant voltage is seen by parasitic capacitances of photovoltaic array. Furthermore, this connection is achieved in such a way that the operations of dcdc converter and inverter are not disrupted. This connection leads to very low earth leakage current and compliance with international standards. Since the front end converter seen by grid side is a conventional four switch inverter, the structure offers high conversion efficiency and ability to perform various grid support functions such as voltage ride through and reactive power support etc. The use of proven converter topologies makes the idea viable and intuitive. A proportional resonant controller is used for average current control, leading to reduced dc-link capacitance requirement for front end inverter. The working of structure is validated with help of simulations in MATLAB/Simulink software environment and the results are provided. Efficiency of the proposed topology is also estimated to show that it offers high efficiency over wide variation in voltage of photovoltaic array.

articleTitle: A Four-Quadrant Three-Phase AC-DC Converter for Virtual Electric Traction Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Virtual electric traction machine (VETM) is a power electronic converter based system capable of emulating behavior of an electric motor. The widely used VETM systems in industrial drives testing environment, makes use of traditional two-stage AC-DC-AC converter. However, this multistage conversion requires DC link energy storage device as well as individual control algorithm. Hence, to simplify control and reduce number of converter stages, this paper proposes a three-phase AC-DC converter topology suitable for four-quadrant operation of VETM system. Unlike twelve switches in traditional AC-DC-AC converter, the proposed topology uses ten power semiconductor switches reducing switching losses. In this paper, a detailed operation of proposed converter is presented in along with simulation and experimental results for a 2 kW PMSM motor emulator.

articleTitle: Fixed frequency based sliding mode controlled audio amplifier
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a fixed frequency based sliding mode controlled class D audio amplifier for high quality mid power audio applications. A carrier based sliding mode controlled technique is utilized which besides reducing the chattering effect offers high immunity to loudspeaker parameter variation and good power supply disturbance rejection. A low cost 20W, 20HZ to 20 kHZ audio amplifier using the analog electronics is developed. Experimental results with the developed prototype confirm good disturbance rejection, high immunity to load parameter variation and excellent linearity.

articleTitle: Hall-Effect Sensor Fault Diagnosis, Identification and Remedial Strategy in Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a simple fault tolerant control for failure of one Hall Effect position sensor of PMBLDC drive is proposed in a closed loop control scheme to increase the reliability of drive. The proposed system is capable to detect and identify the breakdown of one Hall sensor and replaces the faulty sensor signal by a fictitious Hall signal which is generated by the microcontroller. Effectiveness of the remedial strategy is also proven by the correct performance of PMBLDC drive under faulty condition during various transition conditions. After occurrence of the fault, PMBLDC drive is unable to self-start with only two hall sensors. Therefore, a new starting methodology is also presented. The proposed control and starting method have been experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Design and Comparison of Enhanced Voltage Gain Active Clamped Flyback Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents design and discontinuous conduction mode operation of three active clamping circuits. In addition to energy recycling, these circuits offer enhanced voltage gain by increasing the effective source voltage. A mathematical model is built to compare their voltage gain and lay down design rules for circuit passives. Operation of the converter which offers the maximum gain, is validated with a 400 V, 200 W laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: A Laboratory Scale Test-Bed for Demonstrating and Validating Smart Grid Concepts
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Currently, power distribution network is undergoing significant and rapid transformation to a decentralised, yet integrated network with customer oriented future called smart grid. This infrastructure will be equipped with monitoring devices, control units, bi-directional communication facility between central and distributed controllers, in addition to the Distributed Generators (DGs) and energy storage elements. The comprehensive development of smart grids necessitates innovations in real-time energy resource sharing and balancing, communication network design and data processing mechanisms. The successful implementation of the state-of-the-art technologies developed for smart grid calls for its validation in real hardware before deployment in the field. This paper presents the design and implementation of a laboratory scale smart grid test-bed, which can foster the researchers to analyse and validate the developed technologies in real hardware. The proposed test-bed is also a pedagogical model for the under graduate and post graduate students for project-based learning in smart grid.

articleTitle: Device Loading of a Modular Multilevel Converter with Flying Capacitor Submodules
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) continuously capture attention in various industrial and electric transportation applications due to the advent features of modularity, improved harmonic performance and fault-tolerability. However, the operation of MMCs under stringent environmental conditions in some applications could lead to failure of power semiconductor devices, thereby imposing a reliability challenge in the MMC. Consequently, it is essential to analyze thermal behaviour of the power switching devices under different kinds of operating conditions and the control schemes for reliability-orientated converter design. In this paper, an electro-thermal model is developed in a PLECS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> simulation environment to calculate power loss and analyze thermal loading on semiconductor devices in flying capacitor submodules (FC-SM). The impact of an active circulating current control in the MMC with FC-SMs in terms of loss and thermal loading of power switching devices are holistically investigated in this paper. The methodology and the analysis are of immense importance and establishes the further study on reliability improvement of the MMC.

articleTitle: A Zero-voltage Zero-current Transition Network for Dual Phase Interleaved Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a zero-voltage zero-current transition network is proposed for a dual phase interleaved converter. The proposed soft-switching network consists of an auxiliary transformer, an auxiliary switch, and a clamp diode. The enhanced gain of the converter over conventional interleaved boost converter is realized by utilizing a diode capacitor multiplier cell. The auxiliary transformer closely couples the current in the switch branches to achieve effective zero-current turn-OFF of the outgoing switch in addition to zero-voltage turn-ON of the incoming switch. Furthermore, zero-current turn OFF of all the diodes (main and auxiliary) is also achieved. Additionally, the proposed network facilitates zero current turn-ON of the auxiliary switch. A 60 to 270 V, 140 W prototype operating at 50 kHz is constructed and soft-transitions of the devices is demonstrated through experiments.

articleTitle: A Novel Poly-Phase Outer Rotor Homo-Polar Transverse Flux Machine using Ferrite Magnets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel topology for single stack poly-phase outer rotor transverse flux machine which use ferrite magnets. This machine has potential application such as wind generation, electric vehicle, in-wheel electric motor etc. Conventional topologies for transverse flux machine need multiple stacks of rotor and stator of single phase TFM, stacked on each other to make the machine poly-phase. However the topology proposed in this paper can be used to create a poly-phase machine in a single stack. Also, the use of ferrite magnets instead of rare earth magnets make the machine prudent. Paper aims to design a 3 phase outer rotor permanent magnet transverse flux machine and study its operational characteristics by performing Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in the Ansys Maxwell software.

articleTitle: Vector based analysis for design of single phase SRF controller in Dynamic Voltage Restorer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel vector based control scheme for single phase Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) is proposed to obtain fast and effective restoration of load. The proposed control scheme is based on exact voltage insertion method in which extensive analysis of inserted voltage vector is done. The complete vector analysis during sag provides the magnitude and phase of injected voltage. Improved single phase synchronous reference frame (SRF) theory is utilized for this vector analysis. Besides, closed loop control technique is adopted in phasor study. This proposed method completely removes the freezing of Phase-Locked-Loop (PLL) required at the sag instant where phase jump mostly occurs. Actually, the PLL is nonlinear in nature and must be slow in response to give proper voltage insertion. The suggested controller exhibits both feed forward and feedback path with separate magnitude and angle control. The digital simulation in MATLAB indicates that the suggested vector method for voltage insertion can effectively restore healthy value of voltage for nonlinear load as well.

articleTitle: Isolated Dual Boost Converter: Controller Design using Affine Parameterisation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: There is an increasing demand for high gain dc-dc converters due to the use of auxiliary sources at the consumer end. Isolated dual boost converter is a type of interleaved boost converter, which is used in the high gain dc-dc converter applications. The dynamic performance of the converter depends on the controller parameters. This paper discusses the detailed modelling and controller design of isolated dual boost converter. The controller is designed using affine parameterisation. The performance of the converter with controller is verified through MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Ultracapacitor Aided Performance Enhancement of Battery Powered Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents energy control of a battery powered Electric Vehicle (EV) with the aid of Ultra Capacitor (UC). Induction motor powered EV is fed by the battery through the buck boost converter and inverter with New European standard Driving Cycle (NEDC). A 48V battery and 300F UC is connected to the motor load of excitation of 200 V through a 5kW bi-directional buck boost converter. The voltage profile of the load is controlled by Reset-Set-Track (RST) controller thereby controlling the load torque profile. Energy flow to load is from both battery and UC with power management, which limits the battery current requirement and hence improves the battery performance. Results show that the voltage regulation of battery is improved from 4.8% to 1.8 % by the compensation of voltage sag of load with the aid of UC and the State Of Charge (SOC) is increased by4.2% over a period of2 hours. Peak power management is also improved by monitoring the load profile. Simulation has been done using MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: A Solid State Transformer for Integration of High Power PV plant to Medium Voltage Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a solid state transformer to integrate a high power PV plant to a medium voltage (MV) grid. This enables the plant to have distributed MPPT for multiple PV strings thereby increasing the extracted power from the PV modules. A 10 MW system is simulated with MATLAB/Simulink and the results are presented in this paper. Further, a scheme to mitigate the inter-phase power unbalance with zero sequence currents is presented. A detailed analysis of the system and the derivation of the magnitude and phase of zero sequence currents are also presented.

articleTitle: A Multi Objective Control Strategy Based Power Flow Management of PV System For Remote Power Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of Multi Objective Control Strategy (MOCS) based controller for the PV system with Soft Switched Interleaved Flyback (SSIFB) converter to balance the power flow between the PV modules, storage battery and loads. The MOCS controller generates the control variable based on the MPPT control loop and the battery charging loop. The effectiveness of proposed control strategy at constant irradiations, rapidly varying irradiations and load changes is verified by simulation and validated by hardware results. Both the simulation and hardware results prove that the designed controller optimizes the power flow management within the PV system such that PV power is utilized effectively, the battery is charged suitably and the load demand is satisfied irrespective of the variations in solar irradiations.

articleTitle: Modified Distributed Winding for Harmonic Reduction in Space MMF Distribution
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a modification in the conventional multi-phase distributed winding to reduce the space harmonics in the distribution of magneto-motive force (MMF) around the air-gap periphery. The technique used for modification in winding distribution includes the optimization of conductors per slots and the slot swapping in each phase. This method effectively reduces the dominant lower order harmonics, however, the number of harmonics reduced depends on the slots per pole per phase in the machine. The winding function approach is used to get the closed form expression of Fourier expansion of space MMF distribution. An example of 36 slot, 2 pole induction motor with both conventional single layer distributed winding (SLDW) and modified distributed winding (MDW), is used to compare the performance. The time-stepping Finite Element method is used to analyze the dynamic performance of the induction motor using the proposed winding scheme.

articleTitle: SPM Machine with Reduced Loss and Cogging for Wide-Speed Operating Range
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a cost effective, better efficient inset magnet solution for the surface mounted permanent magnet (SPM) motor that suits low speed applications. The pole arc angle of the permanent magnet (PM) is reduced by 30% and the vacant volume is filled with silicon steel laminations to introduce saliency within the PM machine. The machine losses are computed and the efficiency of the proposed motor is compared with an existing outer rotating PM motor with a wide pole arc angle (180° elec.) over the entire torque-speed operating range. The increase in the cogging because of the added saliency is reduced with the introduction of single/ multiple grooves on the stator teeth.

articleTitle: Effect of Leakage Flux on the Design of a LCI fed Active-Reactive Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Active-Reactive Induction Motor (ARIM) has been introduced in literature as an alternative to the synchronous motor in medium voltage Load Commutated Inverter (LCI) fed drives. The resulting drive has been shown to have lower cost with improved reliability and ruggedness. The ARIM is basically a squirrel cage induction motor with two sets of three-phase stator windings. While one winding is rated for high voltage and power, the other winding is rated for a lower voltage and power. The system is controlled such that the low voltage winding fed from a VSI, supplies enough reactive power to the machine so that a leading power factor is seen at the terminals of the high voltage winding. This enables the high voltage winding to be fed from a LCI which supplies all the active power. The ARIM being a non-conventional machine intended for a specific Medium Voltage (MV) drive topology, requires some special design considerations. This paper describes the effect of leakage flux on the operation of the MV LCI fed ARIM drive. An iterative design procedure to obtain the optimum ratings of the VSI and the flux winding is proposed. The proposed method is illustrated with an example design of a 6.6 kV, 1 MW ARIM drive. A prototype 3.3 kV, 75 kW ARIM is built to verify the design.

Author Keywords: Medium Voltage (MV) Drive and Vector Control

articleTitle: Modular HF Link Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an inverter topology with high frequency link, for conversion of low voltage DC at about 30V to 415V, 50Hz, three phase AC for standalone inverter systems. To establish suitability, the proposed topology is compared with another widely used topology based on practically relevant considerations. Devices and components have been identified for each of the topologies and actual device parasitics have been considered for loss estimation and efficiency computation. In addition, the paper also proposes and studies a proportional-resonant (PR) voltage control structure for the proposed topology for mitigating effects of non-ideal operating conditions such as unbalanced and non-linear loading.

articleTitle: An Implementation Issue for 3L PWM Techniques for Parallel Interleaved 2L VSIs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Different three-level (3L) pulse-width modulation (PWM) techniques could be implemented using two parallel interleaved two-level (2L) three phase voltage source inverters (VSIs). In case of two parallel interleaved 2L VSIs, there is a physical addition of voltage waveforms of individual 2L VSIs for constructing an equivalent 3L output voltage waveform. However, due to practical constraints such as dead-band, mismatch in device switching characteristics, delay due to logic gates, etc. there occurs an unwanted shift in the switching patterns which produces an unwanted variation in the equivalent 3L output voltage waveform. This unwanted variation in the equivalent 3L output voltage waveforms reflects as higher ripple in the ac side line currents of the individual VSIs and load current. This paper proposes a reference signal shifting based solution for mitigating the unwanted variation in the equivalent 3L output voltage waveform and hence reducing the ripple in the ac side currents. Simulation and experimental results are shown to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Controller for Improved Hybrid Three Quasi Z source Inverter for DG Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Design of high boost voltage converter configurations is essential for the better extraction of energy from renewable sources. An Improved Hybrid Three Quasi Z source Converter provides higher voltage gain compared with the existing impedance source converters within a single stage power conversion, makes it suitable for distributed generation applications. This paper presents the configuration and modes of operation of proposed converter. The performance of the converter is illustrated by employing model predictive control. The main objective is to get superior dynamic performance of the converter. The load variations can control by well defined cost function includes output ac current, dc side inductor current and capacitor voltage as control parameters. The total harmonic distortion in ac current is within IEEE standards.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Load Distribution and Drives Configuration Selection for Harmonic Mitigation as Per IEEE 519-2014 Standard
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Distribution of nonlinear loads and selection of variable frequency drives configuration in industrial power distribution systems shall be done appropriately at design stage itself so that the harmonic distortion levels at point of common coupling are within the IEEE 519-2014 standard limit. With the methodology as given in this paper, one can find out mathematically whether the total demand distortion exceeds IEEE 519-2014 standard limit or not instead of measuring it physically at field with harmonic distortion analyzer (instrument that measures current harmonic distortion and voltage harmonic distortion), which can be feasible only after installation and commissioning of all loads. With this approach it can be possible to take corrective action during the designing stage of power distribution systems in an optimal way. Also one can minimize the use of very expensive Active Front Ends variable frequency drives or can minimize the use of expensive multi pulse (twelve or higher pulse) variable frequency drives with input side having converter transformer by replacing with less expensive six pulse variable frequency drives with having higher percentage of line reactor by identifying at which distribution bus or at which distribution transformer, total demand distortion exceeds IEEE 519-2014 standard limit. This study will help in selecting the optimal configuration of variable frequency drives and thus will reduce the overall project cost. A comparative table of maximum allowable percentage of nonlinear load with respect to total load at secondary side of distribution transformer is evaluated based on current THD of these nonlinear loads and total demand distortion limit as per IEEE 519-2014 standard. Case study with different percentage of nonlinear load and various VFD configurations are analyzed mathematically and by PSpice based Vacon harmonic simulation software and the outcomes of case study are represented in pie chart diagram.

articleTitle: Integrated Modulation Technique for Switched capacitor Ultra Sparse Matrix converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ultra sparse matrix converter(USMC) is a unidirectional single stage AC-AC converter without DC link capacitor. However it has limited voltage gain. To enhance voltage gain and to achieve wider load power factor range, a switched capacitor USMC (SC-USMC) is being reported recently. Even for unbalanced supply conditions SC-USMC produced balanced output without any additional protection circuitry. By proper placement of switching states voltage gain of SC-USMC and capacitor voltage rating can be improved. This paper addresses these improvements by proposing integrated space vector modulation technique for SC-USMC. Proposed modulation scheme is validated through analysis, simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Development of a Single-Phase Inverter for Application in a Hybrid Solar UPS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Conversion of solar energy into a useful source of electric power at high efficiency is a challenge. In order to utilize the solar energy to its maximum potential a closed loop single phase inverter is developed for a 1kVA stand-alone hybrid solar UPS, capable of supplying a domestic load of 600W, with a worst-case power factor of 0.6, and a backup time of one hour. The control scheme is based on sensing the output voltage and using it in a feedback loop to ensure that the load voltage is regulated to the rated value. Sine triangle PWM technique is used to minimize the total harmonic distortions. Different topologies of snubber circuits utilized are compared and discussed. The simulations are carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK and the hardware model of the system is developed and tested under various conditions.

articleTitle: Field Oriented Control Strategy for a Differential Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The differential induction motor has a single stator with three phase winding and two axially separated rotors that are free to rotate independently. Thus each rotor has the independent capability to run either as motor or generator, permitting mechanical power flow out from the machine (motoring) or into the machine (generation), as long as the stator is electrically excited to establish the requisite flux. However, due to interdependency between the two rotors to some extent, implementation of a suitable control strategy is not straightforward. The machine is represented by its equivalent circuit while a Field Oriented Control strategy is proposed and implemented for the differential control of the two rotors, in order to establish a control over the speed of the two rotors independently. The control strategy is elaborated in this paper, supported by simulation as well as experimental data obtained from a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: A New Stator Resistance Estimation Technique for Vector Controlled PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the novel stator resistance (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) estimation techniques for a vector controlled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive. These estimation techniques have numerous advantages including maintenance and knowing the operating range of the machine. These techniques give indirect measurement of the temperature-rise in the stator of the machine. Therefore, an accurate estimation of the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> will help in condition-monitoring of the PMSM machine. Estimation of R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is done by using the Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS) which is built with reference values (current and voltage). One of the proposed stator resistance estimation technique is robust and offers dynamic performance in all four modes of operation including zero speed. Theoretical approach and simulation results are presented for various estimation techniques at various speeds and loads. The extensive simulation is performed and presented in this paper in MATLAB/SIMULINK to observe the performance of the proposed techniques and Real-time simulation results using a Typhoon Hardware In the Loop (HIL) system are presented to validate the performance of the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: Hybrid Wind-Diesel Remote Area Power Systems with Hydrogen-based Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the operation and control strategies for a hybrid wind-diesel remote area power system (RAPS) with hydrogen-based energy storage. Detailed models of the main components of the system have been presented and different control systems have be proposed to achieve the maximum utilisation of the wind energy and thus reducing the reliance on diesel energy. Two energy storage systems have been implemented for short term purposes based on battery, and for long term purposes based on electrolyser and fuel cells. The performance of the proposed hybrid RAPS system under continuously varying wind and fluctuating load conditions has been explored and results are presented.

articleTitle: Reduced Rating Active Phase Converter for Three Phase Induction Generator based Single Phase Grid-Tied Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The distribution systems and microgrids in remote and rural areas are often of single-phase in nature due to economic viability. However, three-phase induction generators (IG) is a popular machine even in such applications due to the large utility and its competitive price features. This paper proposes a control approach for injecting power to a single-phase grid from an active phase converter (APC) assisted three-phase IG. The presented approach ensures balanced operation of the IG even with variable generation. A method is proposed that reduces the loading on the APC and improves operating power factor at the single-phase grid. Closed form expression of the grid current for a given operating point of the IG is derived. Simulation and experimental results are provided to validate the theoretical framework and APC control approach. The experimental results with a 3 kW IG substantiate the proposed APC control approach injecting 2.6 kW real power into the single-phase grid at near unity power factor.

articleTitle: Network Theory Based Power Grid Criticality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A process of critical transmission lines identification in presented here. The criticality is based on network flow, which is essential for power grid connectivity monitoring as well as vulnerability assessment. The proposed method can be utilized as a supplement of traditional situational awareness tool in the energy management system of the power grid control center. At first, a flow network is obtained from topological as well as functional features of the power grid. Then from the duality property of a linear programming problem, the maximum flow problem is converted to a minimum cut problem. Critical transmission lines are identified as a solution of the dual problem. An overall set of transmission lines are identified from the solution of the network flow problem. Simulation of standard IEEE test cases validates the application of the method in finding critical transmission lines of the power grid.

articleTitle: LCL Filter Based Solar Photovoltaic Distributed Generation System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Power generation form renewable energy sources have gained prominent importance now a days due to its abundant availability and zero carbon dioxide emission nature. The interface of converters has become very vital in transferring the power from energy sources such as wind, solar to the grid. But due to switching action of the converter it generates total harmonic distortion (THD) in power output. So to reduce the total harmonic distortion, LCL filter is used to reduce the harmonics generated by the converter. Although there exist so many literature regarding designing and describing LCL filters, there are lack of systematic design procedures and methodology. After that also, there persist a clearly lack of defined mathematical modeling approach which taken into account two cases of delta-and wye-connected capacitors along with the resistor on grounding. This paper presents a systematic procedure to design a LCL filter and application in solar photo-voltaic distributed generation (PVDG) system along with a well defined approach for reduction of harmonics. The techniques and procedure presented in this paper has been applied to a small Solar PVDG systems and may also be apply for medium and above solar PVDG systems.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase 5-Level Inverter Topology with Reduced Semiconductor Switches
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: For any switching frequency, multilevel inverters produce better harmonic profile compared to basic 2-level inverters. Among the available multilevel inverters topologies in the literature, some of the topologies like neutral point clamped (NPC) or diode clamped, flying capacitor (FC) or capacitor clamped, and H-bridge are conventionally used. However, the NPC and FC type inverter topologies comprises the capacitor voltage balancing issue, and the H-bridge requires more number of isolated DC voltage sources and semiconductor switches. To overcome the issues encountered with the conventional topologies, a new single-phase 5-level inverter topology by excluding the capacitor components and with a reduced number of semiconductor switches is proposed in this paper. A reduced number of levels is also achieved with the proposed topology under certain fault conditions.

articleTitle: Speed Sensorless PMSM Driven Single-Stage SMC Controlled Solar Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a speed sensorless vector controlled permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driven single-stage solar water pumping system is proposed. The back-emf based rotor position estimation technique is used. The PMSM speed is controlled through sliding mode controller (SMC) based vector control. The solar photovoltaic (PV) array feeds power to a voltage source inverter (VSI), which drives the PMSM. The PV array is regulated at maximum power point by VSI, which also controls the armature winding currents. The hysteresis current controller produces switching signals for VSI. The reference speed command is generated using output of DC link SMC controller and DC link feed-forward term. The proposed system is designed, modeled and simulated on MATLAB/Simulink platform. The performance of proposed system is obtained for starting, steady-state and dynamic conditions under variable solar irradiations. Test results are obtained on a developed prototype of the system in the laboratory to validate the control algorithm and modeling of the system.

articleTitle: High Gain Energy Efficient DC-DC Converter for True Maximum Power Tracking in PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: High voltage gain boost converter is usually employed as impedance matching circuit in photovoltaic (PV) systems to allow transfer of maximum power to the loads. On account of converter switching, ripple content in the converter input current results in high power oscillations. This leads to a decrease in power extracted or deterioration in tracking of maximum power point (MPP). In this paper, a high gain energy efficient DC-DC converter (HGDC) is proposed for PV system for extraction of maximum power. The use of the HGDC is envisaged for the PV systems to minimize the ripple content in the PV current to enable extraction of true maximum power. The HGDC operation is explained for different duty cycles. The performance of the HGDC is tested for various insolation levels and its performance characteristics are compared with the conventional boost converter and also with a high-gain converter reported in the literature. The results presented in the paper sufficiently demonstrates superior performance of the HGDC mainly in terms of reduction in PV current ripple, power oscillations and hence operation close to true maximum power point. In addition, the HGDC has higher energy efficiency and also has lower voltage stress on the switching devices used when compared to the other converters.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Switched Reluctance Motor Drive for Light Electric Vehicle Using Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved method for the control of switched reluctance motor drive (SRMD), with an application in light electric vehicles (LEV). A low voltage, three phase, switched reluctance motor (SRM) is used in LEV. The flux and torque characteristics are estimated using DC excitation technique. For the control of LEV using SRM, a fuzzy logic control (FLC) method is analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink® based simulation. The control of SRM using the FLC algorithm, takes less settling time for tracking the reference speed of the SRMD. Thus, the starting performance of the SRMD is improved with the use of FLC as compared with the traditional PI controller. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the system using FLC algorithm for LEV.

articleTitle: Risk Adjusted Co-optimization of ATC in High-Low Voltage Interconnected Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Available Transfer Capability (ATC) determination, accounting for the stochastic effects of uncertain sources and loads, is of key significance for the safe and economic operation of a power system, especially in a competitive market environment. In this paper, a two-stage risk-adjusted stochastic optimal power dispatch problem is proposed. The reduction in ATC due to active power uncertainties in renewable energy sources and also the load is taken as the risk. The problem considers a combined transmission-distribution system (TDS) with solar, wind and other conventional energy sources. The ATC is estimated using Continuation power flow (CPF) and power transfer sensitivity factor (PTSF) methods. The joint probability distribution function (PDF) of ATC is derived using individual discrete PDFs of random variables (renewable power generation and loads). The risk is minimized using stochastic weight trade-off particle swarm optimization (SWT-PSO). The proposed approach helps to hedge the financial risk of the network/transmission system owner/operator.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of Breather for Transformer Health Assessment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Distribution Grid is considered to be a blind spot in power system network. The complex nature of the Distribution Grid makes it difficult to monitor and control. Power and Distribution Transformers are the major nodes in Distribution network and it is an equipment of potential importance in the Distribution Grid. Its failure monitoring and diagnosis are important for a reliable power system since it is the connecting link between consumers and utility. The additional attachments namely breather, cooling fan, bushing, differential relay, Buchholz relay are synchronized with the transformer operation. The operating condition of transformer are changes fast or decrease of oil temperature because of step change in the electrical loads and the cyclic heating and cooling of the oil due to the natural loading of the transformer, hence breather filled with silica gel plays very important role in transformer health assessment by absorbing moisture content. The actual data has collected from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited substation and model is developed from these data. This paper present, a fuzzy logic technique for on-line condition diagnostics of transformer oil on the basis of leakage current flows through silica gel of breather and changes in color of silica gel.

articleTitle: Conductivity Estimation for Reliable Assessment of Power Transformer Insulation at Reduced Time
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a method to estimate the conductivity of oil paper insulation is proposed for fast and effective diagnosis of power transformer insulation. Instead of conducting conventional frequency sweep from 1mHz to 1kHz, frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) measurement was conducted from 50mHz to 1Hz and the imaginary part of complex permittivity (ε'(ω) ) of the oil paper insulation was obtained, based on which an equivalent model of the insulation system was developed. Two important parameters namely conductivity (σ ) and imaginary part of susceptibility (χ" ( ω)) were computed from the equivalent model. Finally these two aforesaid parameters were optimized to obtain the imaginary part of complex permittivity (ε'(ω) ) from 1mHz to 1Hz. Experimental verification on several laboratory prepared samples confirmed that the practicability of the proposed method. It was observed that the overall measurement time was reduced up to 78.5% enabling insulation diagnosis to be conducted quicker in comparison with conventional method.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault-Tolerant Converter Topology for Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault-tolerant converter topology for a three phase induction motor drive to maintain normal operation under various fault conditions. This proposed topology uses a two-level VSI with a storage capacitor at its input terminals and an additional capacitor between the motor faulty phase and negative input terminal of the inverter. As the proposed topology uses a single dc-link capacitor, the DC voltage balancing issues associated with split capacitor topology is eliminated. Modelling and analysis of the proposed topology is explained and performance is observed using Matlab/Simulink and results are compared with the conventional fault-tolerant topology.

articleTitle: Resonance based Current-fed Isolated DC/ DC Converter for High Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel resonance based modulation strategy for a full-bridge current-fed isolated DC/ DC converter for high voltage applications. Output regulation is obtained using variable frequency modulation on the primary side to compensate for line and load variations. A two-step method is used for current commutation and usage of active clamp based snubbers are avoided. Circuit operation under different operating modes in steady state are described in detail. Closed form expression for the converter gain and other values of interest are derived using state plane concepts. The presence of a discontinuous conduction mode is discussed and the mode boundary is identified. Design steps for arriving at the component values of the converter based on set of specifications is discussed. Proposed concept, operation and derived closed form expressions are validated through simulation.

articleTitle: A simple reduced order model for switching dynamics of Silicon Carbide MOSFET power module
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The problem of overshoot and oscillations in Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFET power converters is well known. A simplified second order model, whose response is well understood, is presented in this paper which helps in gaining an intuitive insight in the overshoot and ringing. The modelling is done with the assumption that the gate of the SiC MOSFET power module is driven by a current source of fixed magnitude. The model presented in this paper is experimentally verified on a SiC MOSFET power module with a current source driven gate driver.

articleTitle: Self-Adjustable Step Based Control Algorithm for Multifunctional PV System under Sag-Swell Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper describes the single-phase grid connected multifunctional solar PV (Photovoltaic) system with seamless power transfer capability. This multifunctional PV system is also helpful to enhance the quality of power in the utility grid. This PV system comprises of two stages. First stage is a boost converter that performs the MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) and another is VSC (Voltage Source Converter) that executes the task of harmonic elimination, injection of harvested energy to the utility along with non-active power compensation. A PI (Proportional Integral) controller is used to sustain the DC link voltage to a specific value. In order to improve the dynamic response of the PV system, a feed-forward control for solar PV participation is used. A self-adjustable step-based control is introduced for the VSC of PV system in this work. This estimates the real power reflecting portion of the load current in order to show the all features of the PV system. Simulation studies are carried out in MATLAB Simulink. Under realistic deficient grid condition, the experimental performance of the developed PV system is found satisfactory.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Scheme for Wind Driven DFIG Interfaced with Utility Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a phase-locked loop (PLL) based novel control scheme for a wind driven doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) connected to the utility grid. The wind driven DFIG has two converters namely rotor side converter (RSC) and grid side converter (GSC) with a battery energy storage (BES) connected at DC link. The control of GSC, is modified to export/import constant power to/from the grid. The averaged wind power and state of charge of BES, help in deciding the reference export power to the grid apart from the manual selection. The RSC and GSC have taken care of unity power factor operation at stator terminals and to mitigate harmonics, grid currents balancing, respectively. The system performance is found robust as the PLL response is not affected even under grid voltages with DC offset. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme, a prototype of the system is developed. Test results demonstrate the satisfactory performance under various operating conditions such as varying wind speeds, change in the load, change in export and import of grid power and nonlinear load connected at point of common coupling (PCC). The grid currents and voltages are achieved according to the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Buck Boost Inverter Based Inverter Topologies for Domestic Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Ever increasing power demand and the urge to ensure uninterrupted power quality have enforced the usage of renewable sources in distribution systems among which solar power is a prime contender. For the effective and cost efficient extraction of solar power, a single stage buck boost inverter capable of bucking and/or boosting the DC voltage is presented in this work. This converter uses lesser components making it compact and light in weight. Absence of a transformer enables double grounding, providing improved safety. A single PV source supplies the BBI in both half cycles, leading to symmetrical operation. This paper carries out detailed investigation of this converter for domestic applications needing constant voltage supply during source and load variations.

articleTitle: Converter-less MPPT for rural area applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A popular method to extract maximum power from a solar PV array is the direct connection of a DC/DC converter to the PV array. It is known as Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique. In this approach, the PV array is perturbed at a fractional voltage and few tens of kHz frequency. Drawbacks in this approach of maximum power extraction include oscillations in the DC voltage, reduced conversion efficiency and frequent maintenance of the converters (owing to the frequent failure of electrolytic capacitor), which makes it unsuitable to rural area PV applications. This paper proposes Dynamic PV array (DPVA) approach for extracting maximum power from PV array. In this approach, a switch-network of semiconductor switches or electrical relays is integrated into the PV array to choose a matching-configuration for the load. The absence of high-frequency operation, oscillations in the DC voltage and power processing stages are some inherent advantages of this approach. This paper presents a procedure to design a specific size Dynamic PV array, such that, it produces MPP or close to MPP power at all load conditions. Further, a mathematical relationship between the size of DPVA and the Minimum Output Power (MOP) it can produce is derived. Simulations and a six-module experimental tests are conducted to validate the derived relation.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation and performance evaluation of a Linear Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor prototype
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper deals with theoretical evaluation and practical determination of the parameters of a 3-phase, 4 pole, 320 W, 5 m/s linear permanent magnet synchronous motor (LPMSM). The motor had been designed in the laboratory and fabricated at the works of local manufacturer. The parameters have been estimated by analytical calculations and validated using standard FEM packages. The practically determined machine parameters are found to be in excellent agreement with theoretically estimated values. This fact highlights the accuracy of the design, precision of fabrication and the correctness of the testing exercise. The field weakening capability of the LPMSM motor has also been investigated.

articleTitle: Sensor-less Control of a PMSM for Safety Critical Applications Using Hysteresis Current Control in Case of an Encoder Failure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Encoders are one of the critical parts in an electric drive system. In safety critical applications like an air plane a redundant and robust sensor-less controller with an approval in aviation is required. This paper presents a hysteresis current controller, which is implemented on a FPGA. We simulated the switching action and the controller dynamics and measured it on a test bench. We describe the transients excited by the switching action analytically. Although transients are excited at the switching moment, a stable operation of the machine is ensured. The results of simulation and measurement of the switching action show a maximal deviation of 6% in the stator current amplitude. The excited transients describe a sinusoidal shape for the rotor speed. The analytical solution of the oscillation amplitude deviates from the measured results by a maximum of 14%.
