The oscillation frequency is 24% up to 35% smaller, depending on the operating point. The differences are due to the assumption of phase currents with a constant amplitude. It is shown that the dq-current components follow the constant torque hyperbola, if the current reference amplitude changes. In case of a load torque change they will move on the constant stator current circle and turning clockwise for a load torque decrease and counter clockwise for an increase. Due to the working principle of the controller, the current distortion is significant and is measured to 29% in a defined operating point. The measurement results validate the simulation results. The implemented hysteresis current controller can be used to improve the redundancy of a control structure.

articleTitle: Junction Temperature Calculation of an IGBT Module in Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new method of validation is proposed to the thermal behavior of IGBT module in variable speed drives. A platform has been setup for estimating the temperature raise of a detailed IGBT module, which include IGBTs and diodes. The present model takes the switching and the conduction losses of both IGBT and its anti-parallel diode of the inverter module into account. The thermal model is embedded in a function by providing the required inputs such as switching states, operating current and thermal equivalent resistance of IGBT and diode with relevant semi-conductor material properties. The results obtained from the calculation and the actual drive test results are compared for the purpose of validation, found that the result obtained are close to the actual test results with a accuracy above 95% for test cases mentioned.

articleTitle: Selection of Capacitor in PV System for Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discusses the calculation of capacitor value connected between a Solar PV and the relevant electric power converter operated under maximum power point condition. The capacitor value is important for extracting maximum power from solar PV system. A detailed analysis is presented to show the impact of the capacitor value on the maximum power point tracking capability under temperature and irradiation variation. Theoretical analysis is validated through simulation done in PSIM 9.1.1 and experiments performed on a 500-watt solar PV prototype system.

articleTitle: Current Distortion Effects on Front End of Variable Frequency Drive Under Shunt Active Filter Connected Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the pre-distortion effects of Shunt Active Filter (SAF) on Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) front end devices like diode bridge rectifier, DC link inductor and capacitor. SAF is connected at point of common coupling (PCC) to overcome harmonic effects of connected VFD in that grid. Active filter generally operates in different conditions including voltage imbalance up to 3% and varying rated load. Although harmonic mitigation is the focus point of SAF use, impedance seen by diode bridge rectifier is significantly reduced, resulting in larger DC filter capacitor ripple current, increased losses in DC link inductor and larger peak current on diode bridge rectifier. Effects of these parameter variations (including frequency range of 2-9 kHz), predominantly, are DC link inductor core loss, reduction in DC filter capacitor life time and increased conduction losses of diode bridge rectifier. A system with SAF is connected to grid driving a six-pulse rectifier VFD is studied under specified load conditions. Simulation studies are done in MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> followed by experimental test measurements. Reliability variation in front end rectifier utilities such as VFD with special emphasis on DC filter capacitor and DC link inductor is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Technical and Fiscal benefits of committing DG in Energy Market during contingency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper explains the contribution of Distributed generation (DG) in power market during normal and contingency conditions. This also shows the impact of DG on Locational Marginal Price (LMP) and voltage profile at the buses. The objective of this paper is to minimize the generation cost along with voltage profile improvement and reduction in real power losses. In this work, the optimal location of DG placement is determined on the basis of higher LMP method. The DG type considered is Type1 DG i.e. injecting both real and reactive power in the system. The Linear Programming Optimal Power Flow (LPOPF) is used to determine the LMP at all the buses. The study is done on modified IEEE WSCC 9 bus system. Power world Simulator is used as the tool for simulation.

articleTitle: Degradation of Input Displacement Power Factor by Input Current Filter and its Compensation for a Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The control of input displacement power factor independent of the load power factor is one of the advantages of a three phase to three phase Matrix Converter. An input current filter is normally used to filter out the unwanted distortion components of the input current drawn from the ac power supply. This input current filter introduces an undesirable leading phase shift in the input current even if the converter is controlled to draw unity displacement power factor current. This unwanted phase shift can be compensated by adjusting the angle of the input current vector of the converter. This paper proposes two control schemes to maintain unity displacement power factor at the ac supply side in presence of the input current filter. In the first method, an analytical solution of the required adjustment angle of the input current vector in d-q frame for the Matrix Converter is found and is used to generate the input reference current vector. This method relies on the values of the input filter parameters. In the second method, filter parameter value are not used or required. Instead the angle of the input current vector of the Matrix Converter is adjusted iteratively following a logic to get unity displacement factor at the input ac supply side. Simulation in MATLAB/Simulink software and real time simulation in Field Programming Gate Arrays (FPGA) platform are carried out for the two methods and results are presented.

Author Keywords: Control of input displacement power factor

articleTitle: Improved Selective Frequency Active Damping for Voltage Source Inverter with Output LC Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The filter inductor current of a LC-filtered voltage source inverter is usually fed back for active damping (AD) of LC resonance. However, it also increases inverter's harmonic output impedance, which consequently distorts the output voltage with nonlinear load. Alternatively, a selective frequency active damping (SFAD) has also been reported, which limits the damping action around resonance frequency only, and thus does not affect low/mid frequency behavior of the system. This paper investigates performance of SFAD scheme through discrete-time analysis. It is shown that digital delays degrades damping performance. Then, an improved design method for SFAD is presented which is experimentally shown to provide better transient and steady-state performance.

articleTitle: A New Interactive Control Algorithm of DSTATCOM for Power Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a new interactive control algorithm based on voltage references to improvise the performance of Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) for power quality improvement. The proposed control algorithm has advantages of reduction in computational burden and reduction of switching losses when compared to traditional methods. This scheme ensures unity power factor if the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) voltages are within the tolerable range, called as Current Control Mode (CCM). Otherwise, regulates the PCC voltages called Voltage Control Mode (VCM) operation. An adaptive DC voltage control has been proposed to improve the DSTATCOM performance, in terms of switching losses and efficiency. To show the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, simulation and experimental studies have been performed.

articleTitle: Estimation of Losses and Performance Parameters of Three Phase Induction Motor using Particle Swarm Optimization and H – G Diagram
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple, robust and improved parameter estimation technique for induction motor. This technique estimates the equivalent circuit parameters from measured voltage, current, power and speed data under running condition. The measured data were analyzed for estimating the equivalent circuit parameters using H -G diagram and particle swarm optimization. The estimated parameters and losses were compared with the values obtained through classical test procedures as per IEEE recommendation. The comparative study confirms that the proposed scheme can estimate the parameters and losses with a greater accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Propagation of Voltage Sag through Different Transformer Winding Connections
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Propagation of voltage sag after occurrence of fault in power transformer may develop high inrush current and subsequently may lead to failure of the transformer. Transformer inrush current have high magnitude and contain undesirable harmonics which may lead to unwanted tripping of protective relays, reverberation in the system and mechanical strain in the winding. This paper studies the effect of voltage sag propagating in the transformer due to various symmetrical and asymmetrical faults in a chronological manner. Though various studies has been carried out to express the effect of propagation and mitigation of voltage sag, the unique study presented in this paper very precisely describes and compares the propagation of voltage sag through different transformer connections in a methodical way. For the purpose of analysis different types of actual transformer of North Eastern Regional Transmission System has been taken and the analysis has been performed with the help of SIMULINK by considering the occurrence of all the major faults. The study presented in this paper will help the utilities to choose the best and appropriate connection of transformer leading to reduction in failure of power transformer and ensuing total reliability of the system and prevention of loss of economy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Factor and Efficiency of Three Phase Induction Motor Drive using Single Main PWM Switch and Three Auxiliary Switches
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel economic variable voltage high-frequency PWM direct AC to AC voltage controlled three phase induction motor drive. The drive consists of one main switch and three auxiliary controllable switches with AC freewheeling technique and adjustable dead-band between switches. This scheme would be useful for various Industrial drives for high power fans, pumps and blowers coupled to a three-phase induction motor. The proposed drive reduce the motor current thereby decreases the losses and improves the input power factor simultaneously with the reduced number of controllable switches as compared to conventionally used VVVF drive.

articleTitle: Optimized PWM Techniques with 3rd Harmonic Injection for Five Phase Concentrated Winding Induction Motor with Open-End Stator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents different approaches to optimize the PWM techniques for lower switching losses by using clamping technique for five-phase concentrated winding induction motor with an open-end stator. In such machines, apart from fundamental, the 3rd harmonic component also contributes to the electromagnetic torque generation. Thus, the addition of a 3rd harmonic component in the modulating waveform will also help in improving the torque handling capability of the motor. Apart from adding a 3rd harmonic component, proposed PWM techniques also minimize or mitigate the common mode current. In the given manuscript, three PWM schemes for dual inverter fed five phase concentrated winding induction motor with open-end stator are proposed. The proposed PWM techniques use the carrier-based approach, which avoids any sector identification or timing calculation. The given approaches are also verified using both simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: The Critical Penetration Level in Oscillator-Based Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Increasing renewable resource have been integrated to smart grid with excessive electronic equipment, dropping the inertia of power networks dramatically and affecting the stability of the whole system. It naturally raises the question that what the limit size of the renewable resource can be integrated into smart grid? This is a magnificent and vague problem so we attempt to solve it by analyzing the synchronization of oscillator-based smart grid as a small break point. Assuming smart grid as two coupled oscillator-networks, the maximal allowed number of oscillators, a presentation of critical penetration level to some extent, are derived for given coupling strengths. It is found that the inter-structure between oscillator-networks impacts the critical penetration level significantly. For balanced inter-structure, the critical penetration level is high. The findings may provide some help in designing the structure of smart grid and setting the local highest penetration level in certain area.

articleTitle: 1.618 – The golden number for generating five phase space vector PWM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The paper brings out the observation that all the space vectors of a five phase inverter both in the (α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, β<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) plane and (α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, β<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) plane can be automatically generated using the golden number 1.618. The repeated multiplication of the number generates all the five phase space vectors. This observation has been used to generate SVPWM for a five phase inverter and results are also presented. The logic for mapping the coordinates between the (α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, β<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>) and (α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) coordinates is also presented and utilized for automated generation of five phase SVPWM avoiding complex computations. The generation of SVPWM using the proposed method does not require look up tables and complex trigonometric computations. The proposed method is explained and validated for a two level inverter which can also be extended to any n-level inverter without increased complexity. The simulation of the work has been carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK for which results are presented.

articleTitle: Digital Current Hysteresis Controller Based on Wide Bandwidth Inductor Current Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Hysteresis controllers provide tight regulation in switching dc-dc converters with reduced filter components. Current hysteresis controller uses the inductor current ripple to generate PWM gate signal. Digital current hysteresis controller needs the inductor current in digital domain. Conventionally, the current is sensed using a wide bandwidth current sensor and a high speed ADC, but, these are costly devices. Hence, this paper presents a current hysteresis controller without a current sensing. A novel method is proposed to estimate the current using the switch node voltage of the converter. Estimated current is used by the current hysteresis controller. Experimental results are given to validate the proposed theory. For different hysteresis limits, the frequency of converter varies between 961 kHz and 350 kHz which is 6 % accurate with respect to the theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: A Novel Common Inverter Electric Spring Configuration in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Impending energy crisis and rapidly flourishing power demand is the concerning issue for the utility. The Renewable Energy Source (RES) turns out to the promising substituent for the fossil fuels thereby rendering power assets and environmental balance. Integration of RES with the grid is accompanied with the varying voltage and affecting quality of power. The novel concept of Electric Spring (ES) is applied to the load side for compensation by dynamic voltage injection. The behavior of capacitor for voltage stabilization is reviewed as the general idea. The paper proposes common inverter based ES configuration with modified control. A single inverter is used for integrating PV with grid and for realizing ES structure. The modification in the basic ES structure to the proposed configuration reduces the need of additional inverter, dc link and associated components, making the system cost effective. The algorithm for maximum power point tracking supports in enhancing the efficiency of the overall system. The satisfactory performance of the proposed system is tested through MATLAB Simulink Environment.

articleTitle: An Uni-directional Single-Phase Soft-switched Resonant High Frequency Link Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Renewable and alternate energy grid integration is an area of interest in the recent years due to the advancements made in Solar and Fuel Cells. This paper considers a single-stage single phase uni-directional High-Frequency Transformer (HFT) link DC-AC converter for grid integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DER). The HFT helps by providing galvanic isolation to protect DER from single faults at significantly low cost and size in comparison with Low Frequency Transformer (LFT). Resonant based power conversion in relatively high voltage DC-DC converters results in higher efficiency and power density. Soft switching due to device capacitances and HFT parasitic leakage inductances enables high frequency of operation. This paper presents a novel Parallel Resonant Converter (PRC) based control strategy that results in high quality adjustable frequency and amplitude AC and soft switching of all devices in the entire range of operation. A well-known single stage isolated inverter topology is slightly modified to incorporate PRC based operation. Simulation results are presented to validate the topology and proposed modulation scheme.

articleTitle: Indian Experience Of HVDC Event Analysis Using PMU Data
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Electrical power utilities in India along with system operator at State, Regional and National level follow Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC) and Central Electricity Authority's (CEA) grid standard regulations while managing and operating Indian grid having International connectivity. This paper describes utilisation of smartgrid technology like Wide Area Measurement/Monitoring Systems (WAMS) in analyzing event related to +/- 500kV, 1500MW Chandrapur-Padghe High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Bipole link in Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Company Limited (MAHATRANSCO) grid of Maharashtra in India. The paper covers representative analogy of HVDC related event using CIGRE-HVDC benchmark model covering simulation carried out in PSCAD mimicking the event. It presents case study explaining utilisation of synchrophasor system in understanding how power system operating parameters behaved in MAHATRANSCO grid during this event and steps taken to keep system in normal operating condition.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction of BLDC Motor With CUK Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In Brushless DC motor (BLDC) there is a ripple in torque during the phase current commutation, such torque ripple is undesirable. Mathematical analysis of ripple in torque during commutation interval is given in this paper and a strategy to minimize the torque ripple is presented. Cuk converter is used to control the DC-link voltage of inverter during the phase current commutation of BLDC motor. In this paper a new way to achieve the sudden increase in output voltage of a DC-DC converter by including an extra switch with new topology in the front end of an inverter is given. Finally the simulations are performed in Matlab/Simulink and the results are shown. From simulation results the effectiveness of torque ripple reduction by DC-link voltage control is confirmed.

articleTitle: Encoder-Less Field-Oriented Control of PMSM Drive using Adaptive Observer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a new full order adaptive observer is proposed based on the feedback provided by state variables of a surface mount permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) for field-oriented control. The control of the two-level voltage source inverter is achieved with Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM). The adaptation law for the estimation of rotor speed and position is based on Popov's hyperstability criteria. To improve the dynamic response of the motor, pole placement technique has been used. This in effect provides a good sensor-less control of PMSM. The proposed method performs well in the standstill as well as in low speed regions. In MATLAB/Simulink environment the simulation study is exercised and results were presented.

articleTitle: A Simple Indicator based PLL for Distorted Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple indicator based phase lock loop (PLL) which is capable of producing distortionless reference waveforms in case of the presence of unbalance and harmonics in the grid. The proposed configuration also has a faster dynamic response thus catering to phase jumps as well. Unlike the existing research works, this proposal doesnt make use of filtering, signal modifications or advanced algorithms. The simplest form of synchronous reference frame (SRF) PLL is retained and effectively made use of in the simplest way to achieve the objectives. The proposed concept makes use of the idea of controlling the instantaneous acceleration between the point of common coupling (PCC) space vector and the existing d-q frame by adding the error to the PLL. This addition is activated or disabled depending on the conditions like phase jump, unbalance and harmonics leading to the acceleration. Separate algorithms indicate the condition. The proposed concept is validated with sufficient simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of Controller for Selected Harmonic Power Elimination from DC Bus in Single Phase Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Single phase power converters operating in standalone mode, has to frequently supply the non-linear loads. Under such case, the power reflected onto the DC bus, contains harmonics other than the usual double-frequency component. This increases the stress on the DC bus capacitor and eventually brings down the life of the converter. This paper proposes a novel control strategy which makes use of the active power decoupling (APD) capacitor in order to neutralise the harmonic power components in addition to the double-frequency power component at the DC bus. In this, a mechanism is developed to directly control the harmonic power flow and its effectiveness is demonstrated with pertinent simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of a Modified Three Phase Line Impedance Stabilization Network for Conducted Emission Test
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The infiltration of power electronic devices in power system has led to high frequency noises being injected into the power grid, owing to the short turn-on and turn-off time of the semiconductor switches. This necessitates conducted emission (CE) tests to be carried out on devices which are intended to be connected to the power supply. Line Impedance Stabilization Network (LISN) is an apparatus recommended for conducted emission testing by standard setting organizations like Comite International Special des Perturbations Radioelectriques (CISPR). In this paper, a high precision and low cost LISN design is explained. The LISN components are designed to provide better decoupling of power supply noises from the measurement terminals, in addition to the other requirements such as providing low impedance path to high frequency disturbances introduced by the Equipment Under Test (EUT) and stabilizing the impedance across the measurement port. Conducted emission test has been carried out on 5kVA induction motor drive using modified LISN. Readings obtained from the LISN are compared with the conducted emission measured using a High Frequency Current Transformer (HFCT), for validating the effectiveness of the LISN component design.

articleTitle: Solar Photo Voltaic Based Power Supply for a Cyber Physical System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The use of dedicated Direct Current (DC) systems using Photo Voltaic (PV) and batteries are gaining importance. To conserve water in Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham a Cyber Physical System (CPS) is present in the existing water distribution system at various locations. This paper aims to propose a dedicated DC network with PV panels and batteries to power this CPS network. Three different configurations of DC networks are presented and the same is simulated in MATLAB with measured irradiance and temperature. The voltage variation at each load point, the energy losses and cost of implementations of three configurations are compared and the best possible dedicated DC design is identified.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation and performance evaluation of -aboratory developed Interior Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents detailed steps of parameter estimation and performance analysis of two interior permanent magnet(IPM) motors that have been designed in the laboratory and are in the winding stage at the works of a small local machines manufacturer. The parameters have been estimated using standard FEM packages and through analytical calculations under different operating conditions. The estimated parameters are used to evaluate the performance (such as torque, speed, efficiency) of the IPM motor. The effect of saliency on the motor performance has been highlighted. The effect of parameter variations on the performance of the machine has also been presented. The field weakening capability of the IPM motor has been studied too. The analytical and FEM-based results are presented for two laboratory designed IPM motor prototypes (5kW, 8 pole, 750rpm and 0.75hp, 4 pole, 1500rpm IPM motors).

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control Algorithm with Synthetic Voltage Vectors for Symmetrical Six-Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the synthetic voltage vector (VV) based direct torque control (DTC) algorithm for the six-phase symmetrical induction motor which is fed by six-leg two-level voltage source inverter (VSI). In DTC, levels of torque controller decide the content of torque ripples. Mostly, five-level torque comparators are preferred over the three-level torque comparators to improve the torque ripple content. When five-level torque comparator is used, small voltage vectors of dq-subspace are mapped in the xy-subspace. This subspace is not responsible for the torque production. It is proposed to form synthetic voltage vectors in order to reduce the xy-subspace flux. The developed algorithm is verified by the simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Speed Estimation in Induction Machines at all Speed Ranges Using Sensing Windings
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper discusses an approach to estimate the speed and position of an induction motor using a few additional sensing windings instead of the conventional mechanical sensors. Elimination of mechanical sensors is appreciated in motor control applications due to their drawbacks such as high cost, space consumption and low robustness. Unlike such direct speed sensors, the proposed sensing windings are used to estimate the speed indirectly. They can be introduced into the stator slots without affecting the constructional design of the motor. Exploiting the effect of rotor slot harmonics and induced electro motive force (EMF), the speed information can be extracted from the signals in the sensing windings in the entire speed range standstill. The effect of rotor slot harmonics is analyzed in detail along with Finite Element Analysis (FEA). The speed estimation scheme is discussed and the simulation results at various scenarios are presented. The test results from a real motor at medium speed are also given.

articleTitle: Replacing Si-IGBT by SiC Mosfet in high Gain Inverter: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: With the recent innovations and popularity of wide band gap devices (WBGD) like SiC and GaN Mosfets, it is very important to understand the feasibility of directly replacing their silicon counterparts by the WBGD, in power electronic converters, to achieve improved efficiency. This paper discusses the impact of replacement of Si-IGBT based design by SiC Mosfets in Boost-VSI. The challenges faced due to the sensitivity of SiC Mosfets to high frequency noises have been reported. Generally, modifying the gate drive circuit serves as a solution to the problem. This paper proposes a solution to deal with the challenges, without modifying the gate driver circuit. A 500W prototype of boost cascaded voltage source inverter (Boost-VSI) is designed and implemented using Si-IGBT as well as SiC Mosfet with same gate driver circuit. A comparative analysis of efficiencies of both the designs is done. Experimental results and analysis validate the significant increase in efficiency of the converter with SiC Mosfet.

articleTitle: Performance of a Dual port Asymmetrical MLI with Solar and Battery using Vertical Shift SPWM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this work, a dual port T-type Asymmetrical multilevel inverter (DP-AMI) is used with two sources namely the PV and the battery is considered. It is assumed that the low voltage level is obtained from battery and high voltage level is obtained from a PV based Boost converter output. Two switches with an antiparallel diode are used to modulate the low voltage level and a conventional VSI is used to obtain a high voltage level in the power circuit. A vertical shifted SPWM is used specifically for this power circuit for obtaining the switching mechanism of the DP-AMI circuit. The analytical study DP-AMI is interfaced between the low level input voltage sources solar and/or battery with the AC load or AC grid. The stepped input solar voltage together with the battery voltage will be converted to an ac source with the help of LC-filter. Using the control mechanism, it is found that the circuit offers improved conversion efficiency compared to the classic H-bridge inverter. It also helps in reducing size of the output filter which is cost effective and also results in less harmonic distortion. The simulation and observation is done for 5 kW load with different power factor's and also with different modulation indexes.

articleTitle: Grid Disturbance Analysis with Grid Connected Wind Energy System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Distributed Energy Resources (DER) are being used to support the energy requirement in the power system and to feed the local loads in remote area, where the utility grids are not available. DER, as a microgrids can also be used to regulate active and reactive power requirement as well as to fulfil the power quality requirement of the power system. In this paper, a grid interactive wind energy conversion system has been discussed and analyzed by connecting with IEEE-9 bus system in normal working condition as well as in faulty network condition. Mathematical modelling and simulation of the system has been done in MATLAB-RT-LAB and results have been validated in real time simulation environment.

articleTitle: An Odd Number of Pole Pairs to Minimize Cogging Torque With Mechanical Symmetry Preserved
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Permanent Magnet (PM) machines are becoming popular in industrial applications as they offer brushless solutions and high torque density, high efficiency compared to conventional electrical machines. One of the major issues of PM machines is torque ripple which is intrinsic in their design. Cogging torque is one of the major components which contribute to torque ripple. This work tries to minimize cogging torque in a 4 pole surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous machines (SPMSM) with PM shifting. But shifting of the PMs causes mechanical asymmetry. Centre of mass of the PM is deviated due to asymmetrical distribution of the PMs. Cogging torque is minimized with PM shifting with mechanical symmetry preserved for an odd number of pole pairs i.e. 6 pole machines by keeping the slots per pole pair and kVA rating of the machine same.

articleTitle: Independent Phase Current Control of a Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Open-winding permanent magnet (PM) motors are gaining popularity in transportation applications due to several advantages over traditional PM motors, such as a wider speed range, and better fault tolerance. This paper presents a current control technique wherein the individual harmonics of the winding current, resulting due to the harmonics in the machine back-EMF waveform, are controlled. Multiple harmonic controllers are used on different harmonic reference frames to ensure control of the corresponding harmonic currents. Real-time simulations are first presented to show the dynamic performance of the machine with the proposed current control technique for a wide variety of transient conditions such as machine start-up and fault operation with only two phases energized. To further validate the utility of the proposed current control technique, a torque-ripple minimization algorithm available in the literature, is used to generate current references for the proposed current controller. Real-time simulations are also presented for the torque-ripple minimization algorithm implementation along with the proposed current controller. This is followed by experimental implementation of the proposed controller. In the experimental implementation high bandwidth linear amplifiers are used to control the winding currents of a physical open-winding PM machine.

articleTitle: Modelling of Logic Circuit for Enabling High Speed Auto Reclosure of High Voltage System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Auto Reclosure (AR) function is an integral feature of high voltage transmission line for maintaining stability, availability and reliability. For the execution of successful AR function, modern numerical relays are used which consist of programmable logic involving series of binary input and output iterations. The primary condition for successful AR function is the clearance of transient faults. However along with the clearance of transient fault, the performance of AR function also depends upon the proper execution of programmable logics in the relay. In this paper a model has been developed in SIMULINK for formulation of a logical circuit consisting of binary input, binary output and logic gates. The output of the logical circuit leads to development of two unique blocks which consists of all the logical iterations for successful auto reclosure function during transient fault and auto reclose lock out function during persistent faults respectively. The model has been verified with data obtained from an actual fault occurred in a 400KV system of POWERGRID North Eastern Regional Transmission System and the performance has been validated. This paper will help the utilities to use the proposed blocks directly in the numeric relay for successful auto reclosure and lock out function respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Three-Level Neutral Point Clamped Inverter Fed Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Multi-level inverters have found wider scope of applications in medium as well as high-power adjustable-speed drives (ASDs) due to their capability of handling high powers and power quality friendly approach. For efficient control of ASDs, indirect vector control is used which has advantages like; elimination of retrofitting of shaft encoder, faster dynamic response, and low torque pulsations. Carrier less modulation techniques (e.g., space vector pulse width modulation) provide more maximum peak fundamental output voltage in linear range of modulation for multi-level inverters. However, carrier based control schemes provide simpler control and more flexibility in operation of the control, especially for dc-link capacitor voltage balancing. This paper focuses on analyzing performance of indirect vector control of induction motor, for phase disposition type of multi-carrier technique. Steady-state as well as dynamic performance of the three-level inverter based drive is analyzed by simulation studies. For experimental validation, hardware set-up of three-level neutral point clamped inverter controlled induction motor drive is developed using Arm Cortex ST32F4 in open-loop configuration. Experimental results depicting satisfactory operation of the developed drive in steady state are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Conformal Mapping Based Investigation of Torque Density and Ripple in SPM Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Torque density and ripple content in torque are two important criteria to assess the suitability of a motor for a considered application. This paper provides an overview on correlation between torque per unit rotor volume (TRV), flux density components, electrical loading and magnetic loading for surface mounted permanent magnet motors. These expressions are derived using Maxwell stress tensor and conformal mapping. The torque expression presented here helps in faster development of torque related back-end models required during design optimization process. The discussion presented here gives an overview on typical effects of stator slots on slotless field distributions, and the associated effects on TRV and ripple in torque.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable solar converter with inverter, chopper and rectifier operation for residential PV applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Reconfigurable solar converter is a new converter configuration which uses single phase single stage topology to perform inverter(dc-ac), chopper(dc-dc) and rectifier (ac-dc) operations. This converter solution minimises the number of conversion stages, which increases the efficiency and reduces the overall cost of the converter. Hence this converter solution is appealing for PV-battery-grid tied applications. This topology helps to reduce the harmonics by isolating the dc and ac loads to the dc supply side and ac supply side respectively. Reconfigurable converter is the basic building block for the future hybrid homes.

articleTitle: Explicit Model Predictive Control of Quadratic Boost Converter for High Step-Up Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a control design for constant frequency switch-mode DC-DC Quadratic Boost Converter (QBC) using Explicit Model Predictive Control (EMPC). The discrete-time state space model is derived for the QBC and formulated as Multi-Parametric Quadratic Programming (mpQP) problem. The solution to the optimization problem is the optimized control law calculated online using Multi-Parametric Toolbox 3.0 (MPT 3.0) and MATLAB. The simulation result shows the optimal performance of EMPC compared to the conventional PI controller.

articleTitle: Effects of Input Phase-Loss and Voltage Unbalance on Front end of Passive Low Harmonic Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Input Phase-loss condition is one of the abnormal operations in Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) system. The Power conversion equipment unit (VFD) must be operational with one line disconnected at the input as defined in international standards. However, the operation under Phase-loss condition to be considered with respect to power density of the VFD. Generally, most of the VFDs are having power limiting functions under Phase-loss condition, considering the increased stresses faced by front end rectifier components, inverter control performance and the life time of the electrolytic capacitors. The Phase-loss condition is detected by measuring the DC link voltage measurements. But these parameters vary in their characteristics while connecting passive harmonic trap filters with the VFD; which will lead to failure of front end devices and will reduce the life time if the Phase-loss detection does not happen in the right instance. This work presents the analysis of this Phase-loss and the Voltage Unbalance condition of VFD with Passive trap filters and to gives the relationship between the ripple current and the load variation. The work also addresses the Lifetime variation of the DC Link capacitors and the DC Link Inductor loss variation with the passive trap filter connected.

articleTitle: Certain Investigations of Lamination Materials and Rotor Slot Area of Induction Motor with Improved Performance
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The motor market is highly influenced by the magnet assisted motors, which increases the cost and complexity of the machines. Considering traditional machine which can satisfy industry and domestic needs, induction motor in highly preferred. Due to their robust construction and low cost, it is widely used in industrial and residential applications. It can be best suited for the traction and Industrial application if certain aspects like materials and rotor slot area is chosen properly. As power demand is drastically increasing day by day improvement in small change in the efficiency of the motor will bring a high reduction in power consumption. The performance of the machine-like rated torque and the efficiency can be improved with the rotor and stator lamination material. Also, the starting torque and the efficiency can be improved by optimizing the area of the rotor slots and winding factor. The investigation had been carried out to estimate the Best Performance Material (BPM) and the Best Slot Area (BSA).

articleTitle: Modifted Cost Function based Switching Frequency Reduction Analysis for Finite State-MPC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Finite state Model predictive control (FS-MPC) is one of the classifications of MPC that has been employed for switching control of voltage source inverters (VSIs). FS-MPC is based on the fundamental concept of optimized switching state selection corresponding to the minimum cost function /error function using finite states model of the power electronics converter. In this paper, modified FS-MPC based on the novel mathematical cost function is presented for reduction of switching frequency. An additional constraint of change in current error with conventional absolute error is formulated to present novel cost function. In addition, the cost function based on squared error is also formulated for in-depth analysis. The proposed novel cost function based FS-MPC is compared with previously presented FS-MPC based on the cost function with change in voltage vector constraint. FS-MPC is implemented in MATLAB-Simulink for a three-phase VSI and simulation results are obtained for performance analysis and validation of the controller.

articleTitle: Pentagonal Space Vector Approach for Third Harmonic Injection Technique for Dual Five-Phase Open-Winding Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a new Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) technique, entitled as `pentagonal space vector approach' for five phase concentrated open-end winding induction motor. The concentrated winding machine enables the utilization of the third harmonic component. The proposed PWM technique helps to enhance the 3rd harmonic voltage component along with the fundamental in the inverter output voltage. The effect of the variation in the 3rd harmonic injection for conventional approach and proposed pentagonal approach has also been discussed in the given manuscript. Further, the utilization of the DC bus has also been emphasized by using open-end winding. In order to use a single DC bus for both the inverters of the open-end winding motor, common mode voltage has been eliminated completely to increase the lifetime of the bearings and reduce losses, caused by common mode current.

articleTitle: Assessment of Noise Reduction in Switched Reluctance Motor Using Conformal Mapping
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Switched reluctance motor (SRM) offers unique advantages in terms of robustness and simplicity in construction. But, noise generated in SRM is high compared to other motors. A significant difference in the radial forces of attraction between stator and rotor at aligned and unaligned rotor positions leads to higher noise generation. Noise reduction techniques can be classified into two primary domains: design modifications and post-design control schemes. Finite element analysis (FEA) tools are widely used for assessment of noise reduction techniques. In the proposed work, conformal mapping (CM) based analysis is carried out to assess a post-design control scheme involving current shaping. Comparable simulation results are obtained for radial force calculation dependent estimation of noise reduction from CM and FEA based methods. CM leads to computationally efficient and simple to implement noise reduction assessment procedure. In cases where design is already optimized or available and control schemes are to be assessed for noise reduction, CM based analysis can be done.

articleTitle: Internal Faults in Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: The Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) has modular and redundant structure, which makes it more reliable during certain fault conditions. Hence MMC technology has received considerable attention among various topologies for interconnecting High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) grid. Existing literature has devoted limited focus on the behavior of the MMC during internal fault condition. This paper presents the switching as well as approximate voltage source model of MMC with analysis of its internal fault current behavior. It also presents an analytical approach for calculating harmonic components in arm current. The simulation studies with both MMC models rated at 161 kV, 625 MVA are performed using MATLAB/Simulink. For this study the power transfer is controlled by changing modulation signal. Presented results emphasize on understanding fault current behavior for various internal faults in MMC.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Multi-Phase Rectifier With Reduced Magnetic Rating
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a 20-pulse asymmetric multiphase rectifier (AMPR) suitable for medium and high-power applications. Unlike the other state-of-the-art 20-pulse delta connected autotransformers, the proposed delta connected AMPR has an ability to reduce input harmonics, maintains high efficiency and requires a magnetic rating of only 30.12% of the nominal load thereby a significant reduction in space, weight, and overall cost required are the salient features of the proposed AMPR. Firstly, the proposed AMPR configuration is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment for evaluating its viability under different loading conditions, and the results are illustrated. Also, a prototype is developed, and the experimental measurements obtained are presented to validate the feasibility and operability of the proposed AMPR. The proposed AMPR offers a total harmonic distortion of 3.7% and can operate at near-unity power factor complying with the IEEE and IEC standards.

articleTitle: A Design Proposal for Butter Extraction System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Conventionally, butter is extracted by agitating dairy products, such as curd, fermented milk or fresh cream. A stirring rod is used to stir the curd or fresh cream inside a cylindrical vessel manually either using ropes or with crank assembly. This process is adopted in all the village households of agricultural communities in India and other developing countries. The process of butter extraction is also mechanized using electric motors and is being used in dairy industries where production of huge quantity of butter is involved; however, a butter extraction system suitable for household application, where less quantity of butter is produced. This will be one of the main sources of revenue for villagers. This present butter extraction method is demands huge physical work and lacks in efficiency and quality. Without standard guidelines for procedure or standard steps to follow, the present process is difficult to reiterate. The focus of this paper is to update the current manual method to electric driven butter extraction system for small-scale application. The butter churner is stirred vigorously in both front and backward directions with the electric drive, which will help in separating the butter from the cream or curd. The operation of butter extraction system is observed to be a non-linear system due to variable churning speed requirement. The main aim of this paper is to propose the design aspects, which includes electrical and mechanical design of butter extraction system to have better performance in terms of productivity rate, saving time and simplicity of use.

articleTitle: A Power Management Algorithm for DC Microgrid Based on Virtual Storage in Source
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A low voltage DC microgrids are gaining importance to penetrate the renewable energy sources (RES). This paper proposes an adaptive approach for power management based on virtual storage in the source. In DC microgrid every source is designed with extra power capacity. In the source, the additional power available beyond its average rated value is considered as virtual storage. The proposed control algorithm generates new references considering virtual storage in the source. This improves the effective utilization of source. Therefore it reduces the stress and charging/discharging cycles of energy storage system (ESS), therefore the life span of ESS increases. The DC microgrid is having low inertia. The proposed control scheme utilizes the extra power in the source to improve inertia of system. The system bus voltage is regulated at its nominal value. The proposed control algorithm is tested in real time simulator.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Coreless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Position holding Mechanism for Spacecraft Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper investigates the performances of 3-phase and 2-phase coreless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) for a position holding mechanism used in spacecraft. Configuration study of coreless PMSM was carried out to select the stator-rotor configuration and it is found that enclosed rotor has higher torque density than outside rotor configuration. Detailed design and analysis of 3-phase and 2-phase PMSM were carried out. Rotor is designed to generate sinusoidal flux in the airgap. Three different winding pattern for 3-phase PMSM were studied and the Sine distributed winding generates higher torque. 3-phase and 2-phase PMSM are realized and characterized. Ripple free torque is achieved in both motors. 3-Phase PMSM has better performance indices than 2-Phase PMSM. Torque density of 2-phase PMSM is 33% lesser than 3-phase PMSM. If torque density is the driving factor, 3-phase PMSM is the ideal choice. With resolver as the angle sensor, for position holding application, 2-phase PMSM is a better option.

articleTitle: Development of low cost electrical nerve stimulator based on a simple circuit topology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents detailed design of a simple low cost circuit topology for electrical nerve stimulator. To synthesize the required electrical current signal from a voltage source, a transconductance amplifier has been introduced. In order to maintain a good quality of current signal envelope with no rising or falling edge harmful distortion as well as independent of load resistance, a low pass filter as well as a Type-II compensator have been incorporated. Signal generation of desired pulse-width, frequency and magnitude are adjusted digitally through micro-controller with a vector keypad for user interface. Details analysis of circuit-configuration and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed circuit configuration as a stimulator.

articleTitle: Decoupled Vector Control of Grid Side Converter with Less Number of Sensors under imbalanced Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, decoupled double synchronous reference frame (DDSRF) theory is implemented by the help of one dc voltage, two ac voltage and two ac current sensors. These sensors are sufficient for the control of grid side converter (GSC) during balanced as well as imbalanced grid conditions in the three phase three wire system. Since, estimation of unknown voltage and current could be assumed correct as there is no path for the flowing of zero sequence current, while two line to line connected voltage sensors have the information of voltage imbalance during imbalanced grid conditions. Therefore, third phase voltage and current could be estimated by making the sum of two sensed quantities and one unknown variable equals to zero. In this paper, it is verified experimentally for the decoupled vector control of GSC, where, the positive and negative sequence voltages are decoupled through DDSRF while currents are decoupled through enhanced DDSRF methods in the respective dq-axes. It is implemented experimentally using TI-2407A DSP controller.

articleTitle: Modified Hysteresis Current Control for Single Phase Solar Grid-tie Z-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple novel technique to determine the shoot-through states in a hysteresis controlled solar grid connected single phase Z-source inverter (ZSI). The ZSI along with the proposed controller exhibits high efficiency due to the single stage conversion. Fast and robust dynamic response can be obtained by using hysteresis control. Hence the proposed control for ZSI is ideal for grid integration of photovoltaic sources. The error current is used to determine shoot-through states based on calculation of current limits as a function of the boost ratio and modulation index. The maximum boost ratio, that can be obtained by the proposed control without causing low frequency ripples in Z-source network, is expressed as a function of modulation index. To verify the analysis, simulations are performed for input and grid voltage variations using MATLAB-Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Two High Voltage Gain Non-isolated Dc-dc Converters with Ripple Free Input Current
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes two non-isolated high voltage gain dc-dc converters with ripple free input current. The circuits use three winding coupled inductor which allows to acheive high voltage conversion with an appropriate turns ratio. Active-clamp circuit is introduced to alleviate the adverse effects of leakage inductor, thereby reducing the voltage stress of main switch and resulting zero voltage turn-ON of both the active switches. Circuit configuration, the operation principles and the design considerations of the converters are presented in detail. A 300 W/400 V hardware prototype of one of the presented converters is fabricated and results obtained are shown to validate its workability.

articleTitle: Rotor Flux Observer for Speed Sensorless IFOC Induction Motor at Low Speeds
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, a method of rotor flux estimation is proposed to improve the characteristics performance of indirect field oriented controlled induction motor drives, at low speed and standstill. Traditionally, in voltage model rotor flux estimator, standard method is to use first order time delay element in place of pure integrator to counter the problem of dc drift and offset. Still, the performance of drive deteriorates when stator frequency is low and at standstill. Here, in addition to first order delay element, a high pass filter is included to reduce the dc offset effect. Also, reference flux space vector is added to the output of voltage model flux estimator, so that at low speed this reference value of flux is the output of the flux observer. In the proposed method, speed is estimated by comparing the torque producing stator current component computed using above flux observer, with reference stator current space vector obtained from speed PI loop. This difference is then fed to the proportional-integrator to minimize the error, generating the rotor speed. The proposed scheme is implemented using indirect field oriented control of induction motor and performance, in all operating conditions, including the critical low stator frequency range is verified using MATLAB Simulation.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement in AC-DC Converter Using Voltage Sensorless Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents the power quality improvement in power supply systems and explains the corrective measures taken by means of front-end AC-DC converter. The front-end AC-DC converter having a boost type delta connected rectifier with voltage sensorless control technique is proposed. The delta switch rectifier enables the zero-sequence component circulation and thereby reduces the third harmonic component in the input mains. Further, the input voltage sensorless control is developed for the proposed converter which can maintain the power quality well within the IEEE and IEC standards and also, yields lesser switching loss, reduced switching stress and high output voltage. The performance of the front-end AC-DC converter configuration is validated by simulating in the MATLAB Simulink environment and the results are presented. The experimental setup for the front-end AC-DC converter is implemented in the laboratory to validate the MATLAB simulation results.

articleTitle: Comparison of Planar Transformer Architectures and Estimation of Parasitics for High Voltage Low Power DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Planar Transformers are popularly used over conventional wire wound transformers for its design accuracy, high power density and low parasitics. For high voltage low power (HVLP) flyback converter with high switching frequency feeding a capacitive load, the leakage inductance and self-capacitance of the transformer along with other semiconductor parasitics significantly affect the performance of the converter. Different transformer winding architectures are explored to choose a transformer design with minimum parasitics. In this paper, rectangular winding planar transformer is evaluated for non-interleaved winding architecture and the spiral winding planar transformer for a high voltage low power flyback converter is evaluated for non-interleaved and interleaved winding architectures. The analytical expressions for leakage inductance and self-capacitance are verified using the frequency response analyzer (FRA) and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation results. The difference in the results obtained from analytical, 2D FEA and measurement results are compared. The designed HVLP rectangular and spiral winding PT is fabricated and tested with high voltage flyback converter prototype for 1 kV/5 W. The analytically computed parasitics of the transformer is verified with FEA model and also from the experimentally observed waveforms.

Author Keywords: High voltage low power flyback converter

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Distribution Network with DSTATCOM and WTDG using RTO Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, rooted tree optimization (RTO) technique is proposed to solve the optimum deployment problem of distributed static-compensator (DSTATCOM) and wind turbine type distributed generation (WTDG) in distribution network (DN) to enhance voltage profile, reduce loss, maximize economic benefit, and decrease level of pollution. To model the system properly, time-wise variation of both the system load and WTDG's power output are taken into account. Logical formulas are proposed to address the techno-economic and environmental impacts of the devices. The proposed method is tested on 33-bus DN and the obtained results validate the effectiveness of the present strategic methodology when compared with other algorithms. Also, a comparative performance analysis is carried out between DSTATCOM and WTDG, which will help the power industry to choose the most suitable one.

articleTitle: A Novel Communication-less Frequency Restoration Technique in Droop Controlled Inverter-based Islanded AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Active and Reactive power is shared between the inverters in an islanded AC Microgrid (MG) using droop control technique in a decentralized manner. Deviations in the frequency and voltage magnitudes, from their nominal values, are inevitable in the droop based power-sharing. To maintain the grid code, it is important to restore these parameters to their rated values, which is basically done by a secondary control layer in the hierarchical control system of an islanded AC Microgrid. This paper proposes a communication-less frequency restoration technique in the primary layer by adopting the property of Recursive Discrete Fourier Transform (RDFT) and Inverse Recursive Discrete Fourier Transform (IRDFT) in the droop control equation. This technique replicates the frequency response of a Band Pass Filter (BPF) and thus extracts the nominal frequency if there is a drift in frequency due to the active power-sharing. The proposed technique is validated with the help of simulation studies for the parallel operation of two three-phase inverters for various test cases.

articleTitle: Power quality improvement in BLDC motor drive using Bridgeless Modified Cuk converter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents a power factor correction (PFC) converter based bridgeless modified cuk (M-cuk) converter fed brushless DC (BLDC) motor drive. Here, the modification in conventional bridgeless Cuk converter is accomplished by including the voltage multiplier circuit with reduced switch current stress and semi soft switching mechanism to reduce converter switching losses for a wide range of speed. This proposed bridgeless PFC converter is explored theoretically and the performance parameters such as displacement power factor (PF), distortion PF and total harmonic distortion (THD) are evaluated and compared with the conventional bridgeless cuk configuration. The simulation is performed in the MATLAB/Simulink environment and the validation is done through a Xilinx SPARTAN 6 FPGA processor board.

articleTitle: Multilevel Inverter Based Single-Stage Grid Connected Photovoltaic System using Cascaded Two-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In the recent trend of using green energy, grid connected Photovoltaic (PV) systems are getting more popular. In this work, the modeling and control of multilevel inverter based single-stage grid connected photovoltaic system based on cascaded two-level inverter (CTLI) is carried out using MATLAB/Simulink. The multilevel inverter topology is developed by the cascade connection of two conventional voltage source inverters (VSI)) using open winding transformer. The inverters are controlled using hysteresis current controller for which the synchronizing reference currents are generated using p-q theory. The maximum power is extracted from the PV array under varying environmental conditions using fuzzy logic controller which generates the change in reference power to be injected into the grid by the CTLI. The CTLI based grid connected PV system is simulated for injecting active power produced by the PV array under varying solar insolation as well as varying load conditions. The simulation is also carried out demonstrating the effective utilization of the PV system by providing reactive power compensation during low or zero insolation conditions. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the control scheme of the CTLI based grid connected PV system for injecting active as well as reactive power in a controlled manner.

Author Keywords: maximum power point tracking, reactive power compensation

articleTitle: Building energy management system for transactive energy framework
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A novel Building Energy Management System (BEMS) based on Transactive Energy (TE) principles is presented which schedules the household appliances according to applicable time-of-use (TOU) prices, expected distributed energy resource generation, and user preferences for economy. The appliances in households are divided into four categories: uncontrolled (such as refrigerators, lights), deferrable (like washing machine, rice cooker, etc), controlled (such as air-conditioning), and energy storage devices. Mathematical models are presented for electricity usage for each type of appliance, and their operation constraints. The proposed BEMS minimizes the cost of electricity used along with minimizing the virtual costs (i.e. maximize usage value of electricity) associated with ageing of storage devices, thermal discomfort and waiting for services of different deferrable appliances. The problem is formed as a non-linear constrained optimization problem which is solved using a hybrid gradient descent algorithm. Simulations results are presented in MATLAB for different user preferences to verify the efficacy of the proposed algorithm. Proposed BEMS can also be utilized for estimating demand response (DR) from the consumer for given change in TOU prices.

articleTitle: Optimum Filtering Theory Based Control for Grid Tied PV-Battery Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper presents optimum filtering theory based control for three phase utility interfaced microgrid system based on the photovoltaic (PV) and a battery energy storage (BES) with improved power quality capabilities. This microgrid is integrated with the BES and PV array at DC bus of voltage source converter (VSC) to supply reserve power to local loads and distribution network. The controlled BES is used to enhance the stability and reliability of PV-BES microgrid system. The BES is not only beneficial on daily energy saving but it is also sized to furnish smoothing facilities to the PV-BES microgrid system. The optimum filtering theory based control is used to control the PV-BES microgrid system in current control mode. A PV feed-forward (PVFF) is incorporated in current control for injection of active power to the utility as well as to improve the dynamic operation of PV-BES microgrid system. The effectiveness of PV-BES microgrid system is validated experimentally.

articleTitle: A Distributed Control for Adequate Power Sharing Based on Available Power in Sources
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive distributed control algorithm for adequate power sharing between the sources based on available power in individual source. The proposed control calculates the droop constant for each source according to available power in source and bus voltage deviation. It restores the bus voltage deviation to its nominal value and it is based on incremental rate of change of power. It worked with minimum sensors and the overall system becomes easy to control. The designed supervisory control will manage the power balance in the microgrid by incorporating energy storage system (ESS) into the service. The mode of operation of ESS is decided by the bus voltage deviation. The proposed control algorithm is tested in real time simulator.

articleTitle: DC Fault Tolerant Hybrid Multilevel Converter Topologies for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) systems are quite popular in high power transmission systems as it offers low losses, high quality output voltage, modular and scalable structure as compared to the two level voltage source converter based HVDC systems. However, inability to block dc fault current is a major concern of conventional MMC-HVDC system, especially for the overhead HVDC system. In this paper, the performance of conventional MMC with half bridge submodules is analyzed for dc side fault. In the event of a dc side fault, the conventional MMC acts as an uncontrolled diode rectifier and feeds very high current to dc fault. To tackle this problem, different techniques have been discussed in the literature. This paper gives a brief overview of dc fault tolerant techniques discussed in the literature. Moreover, in this paper, a detailed comparison between different hybrid topologies with dc fault tolerant capability is performed on the basis of required number of switches and capacitors. Furthermore, the fault tolerant capability of MMC with bipolar (full bridge) submodule is experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Power Balance for WTG - Solar PV Fed DC Microgrids with Battery and Supercapacitor Support
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wind and solar are the most emerging renewable energy sources to meet residential load demands and to make the environment healthy, cleaner and greener. When these sources are combined to have a DC microgrid, problem of power fluctuation among the sources and loads occurs. Also the problem of grid voltage stability is faced. Although battery energy storage system solves these problems but due to demerits and limitations of batteries and due to superseding characteristics of supercapacitors, combination of battery and supercapacitor is used to solve the above mentioned problems. Battery has low power density but high energy density whereas supercapacitor has high power density but lower energy density. So, battery provides lower power for longer duration and supercapacitor provides high power for shorter duration. This paper presents a control strategy to solve power fluctuation problem using combination of battery and supercapacitor for Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) and Solar PV fed DC microgrid in islanded mode of operation.

articleTitle: Seven-Level Packed U-Cell (PUC) Converter with Natural Balancing of Capacitor Voltages
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: A Packed U-Cell (PUC) converter is presented in this paper. The converter uses a single DC source and two capacitors. The capacitors converge to the desired voltages without any closed loop control. The isolated DC source and the capacitor voltages together are maintained at a ratio of 3:2:1. Therefore, the PUC converter can generate a seven-level output voltage at unity modulation index. When compared to cascaded H-bridge converters, the PUC converters offer limited number of switching states for a given number of DC sources. These limited number of states have been utilized to deal with the capacitor voltages in open loop and is the main advantage of the proposed PUC converter. So, capacitors of the proposed PUC converter, have the ability to settle down to their steady state voltages from any arbitrary initial conditions. The proposed inverter can work for any practical load power factor. Operation of the topology is validated through simulations in MATLAB/ Simulink.

articleTitle: Rapid LVRT Control of a DFIG-Based Wind Power Plants Based on Adaptive IQ-V Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: Wind turbine generator should inject the reactive power to support the grid voltage and suppress the increase in the DC-link voltage during a fault in order to fulfil the low voltage ride-through (LVRT) requirement in grid codes. This paper proposes a rapid LVRT control of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) based Wind Power Plants (WPPs) based on the adaptive reactive current to voltage characteristics that suppresses the rise in DC-link voltage by reducing the torque in the rotor side converter (RSC) of the DFIG in proportion to the voltage dip and weighting factor at the terminals of the DFIGs. The current priorities from the real current to the reactive current to inject more reactive power to support the grid voltage during a fault is proposed in this scheme. The RSC of the DFIG is operated in the voltage control mode with the slope of the reactive current capability to the voltage tolerance around a rated value. In addition, slope is changed relying on the voltage dip during a fault to support the grid voltage. The proposed scheme is performed for twenty units of 5-MW DFIGs using an EMTP-RV simulator. The results depict that the scheme rapidly supports the grid voltage and suppresses the rise in DC-link voltage during a fault.

articleTitle: Effect of Flux Barrier Shape on the Performance of a Two-Pole Line-Start Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Power Electronics, Drives and Energy Systems (PEDES)
abstract: In this paper, the performance comparison and optimization study of a two-pole line-start synchronous reluctance motor (LS SyRM) with three different rotor geometries is presented. U-shape, rectangular and inverted U-shape flux barriers are considered for the comparison study. Unlike in the conventional LS SyRM, the flux barriers are filled with aluminium to form a cage, so as to avoid the additional ribs which deteriorate the motor saliency ratio.
